title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄序
我
國家稽古選士之典令天下有
司計三歲大比而賓興焉維
時
今上臨御四載適當其期巡按陝
西監察御史郭〔庭梧〕寔司監
===
臨洒以前巡按御史王〔君賞〕
禮聘四方釁序之秩俾董校
事越八月四日〔魁〕等趨聘至
自四方御史雅注遴才禮遇
殊揩〔魁〕等謝弗任滋懼比入
簾乃以〔魁〕暨教諭張〔師載〕司
考試教諭栗〔保民〕李〔奇〕彭〔程〕
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄序

我國家稽古選士之典，令天下有司計三歲大比而賓興焉。維時今上臨御四載，適當其期。巡按陝西監察御史郭〔庭梧〕寔司監臨，洒以前巡按御史王〔君賞〕禮聘四方釁序之秩，俾董校事。越八月四日，〔魁〕等趨聘至自四方。御史雅注遴才，禮遇殊揩，〔魁〕等謝弗任，滋懼。比入簾，乃以〔魁〕暨教諭張〔師載〕司考試，教諭栗〔保民〕、李〔奇〕、彭〔程〕
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

Our dynasty, following the ancient institutions for selecting scholars, commands the responsible officials throughout the realm to conduct a great examination every three years and to honor and recommend worthy candidates as guests. At this time, the reigning emperor had occupied the throne for four years, and the appointed examination year duly arrived. Guo Tingwu, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Shaanxi, was responsible for supervision. Together with [?] the former Regional Inspector, Censor Wang Junshang, he ceremonially invited men holding posts in educational establishments [?] from throughout the realm to oversee the examination.

On the fourth day of the eighth month, we—Kui and the others—arrived from various places in response to the invitation. The censor had long devoted his attention to selecting talent and accorded us exceptional courtesy [?]. We protested our inability to undertake the responsibility and grew still more apprehensive. When we entered the examiners’ quarters, Kui and Zhang Shizai, an Instructor, were assigned to serve as Examiners; the Instructors Li Baomin, Li Qi, and Peng Cheng …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
孟〔晉賢〕謝〔邦泰〕司同考試提
調則左布政使曹〔金〕右叅議
中〔佐〕監試則按察副使張一
〔齊〕范〔懋和〕暨百司御事罔不
毖簡以充既鎖院之夕列炬
焚香盥手籲天肅禮〔魁〕等于
庭而誠之曰惟
===
聖天子寤寐求賢奚啻饑渴惟多
方內外望治需才奚啻雲霓
惟八郡三陲抱藝之士所視
軒輊脫穎奚啻神明厥惟慎
哉已復進大小百司誠之曰
孔子不云乎執事敬惟吾與
爾事在薦賢可無敬乎詩曰
punctuated: 孟〔晉賢〕、謝〔邦泰〕司同考試。提調則左布政使曹〔金〕、右叅議中〔佐〕；監試則按察副使張一〔齊〕、范〔懋和〕，暨百司御事，罔不毖簡以充。既鎖院之夕，列炬焚香，盥手籲天，肅禮〔魁〕等于庭，而誠之曰：「惟聖天子寤寐求賢，奚啻饑渴！惟多方內外望治需才，奚啻雲霓！惟八郡三陲抱藝之士，所視軒輊脫穎，奚啻神明！厥惟慎哉！」已復進大小百司，誠之曰：「孔子不云乎：『執事敬。』惟吾與爾，事在薦賢，可無敬乎？詩曰：
translation_en:
…Meng Jinxian and Xie Bangtai served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Cao Jin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Zhong Zuo [?], Right Assistant Administration Commissioner. Overseeing the examination were Zhang Yiqi and Fan Maohe, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioners. They and all the officials attending to the work were carefully selected to fill their posts.
On the evening when the examination compound had been locked, torches were arrayed and incense burned. Having washed his hands and invoked Heaven, he ceremoniously received Kui and the others in the courtyard and admonished them [?], saying: “Our sage Son of Heaven seeks worthy men waking and sleeping—with a longing greater even than hunger or thirst! Throughout the many regions, within and beyond the capital, people look for good government and need talented men—with a longing greater even than that for clouds promising rain! The men of scholarly accomplishment from the eight prefectures and three frontier regions look to you to determine their relative standing and enable outstanding talent to emerge, regarding you as more than divine powers! Be ever watchful!”
He then summoned all the officials, high and low, and admonished them [?], saying: “Did Confucius not say, ‘Be reverent in attending to affairs’? Our task, yours and mine, is to recommend worthy men. Can we be without reverence? The Book of Odes says: …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
夙夜匪懈今日之謂矣尚其
同心哉于時〔魁〕等百司罔不
稽首再拜奉誠惟謹厥明乃
進巡按陜西監察御史潘〔民〕
〔模〕今御史劉〔堯卿〕提學副使
徐〔善慶〕前後所取士二千有
奇三試之矢心甄別得士六
十五人錄其姓名及文之純
者以
===
獻〔魁〕以職事當敘諸首簡因僭
言曰維茲關陜古雍州也河
嶽孕靈是生英雋故世稱豪
傑輒首三秦厥惟舊哉因憶
往爲諸生閒嘗披閱圖經夢
punctuated:
「夙夜匪懈」，今日之謂矣。尚其同心哉！」于時〔魁〕等百司罔不稽首再拜，奉誠惟謹。厥明，乃進巡按陜西監察御史潘〔民〕〔模〕、今御史劉〔堯卿〕、提學副使徐〔善慶〕前後所取士二千有奇，三試之，矢心甄別，得士六十五人。錄其姓名及文之純者以獻。
〔魁〕以職事當敘諸首簡，因僭言曰：維茲關陜，古雍州也。河嶽孕靈，是生英雋，故世稱豪傑，輒首三秦，厥惟舊哉！因憶往爲諸生，閒嘗披閱圖經，夢
translation_en:
…“‘Be unremitting day and night’: this speaks of today. May you all act with one heart!” Thereupon Kui and all the other officials bowed their heads to the ground and bowed twice, most respectfully receiving these earnest admonitions. The next morning, they admitted the more than two thousand candidates selected at successive stages by Pan Minmo, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Shaanxi; Liu Yaoqing, the current Censor; and Xu Shanqing, Vice Commissioner in charge of education. They examined them three times and, pledging themselves to conscientious discrimination, selected sixty-five men. They recorded their names and those of their compositions that were of unalloyed merit, for presentation to the throne.
As his official duties required Kui to write a preface for the opening leaves, he ventured to say: This region of Guanshan was the ancient province of Yongzhou. Its rivers and mountains nurture spiritual potency, bringing forth outstanding men. Thus, whenever people speak of heroes and men of distinction, they place the Three Qin regions first. This has indeed long been so! I recall that formerly, when I was a government student, I would sometimes spend my leisure reading illustrated geographical accounts, dreaming…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
厤秦隴思欲泛洪河闚巨靈
陟二華盱秦嶺一慰遡洄仰
止之願無從也迺今服官豐
校應聘而來始浮于河達于
渭已而歷潼關踰華陰至止
長安時秋水方盛澎湃淪漣
仰瞻華嶽終南出沒雲漢曰
===
美哉山河此天下之奇觀也
昔人所稱陝區不其然哉豪
傑者將在是乎旣而偕諸同
事入棘院縱觀多士之文其
立言雖殊類皆明於經術之
故察於性命之微通於時務
之變其氣昌而不肆其志遠
punctuated: 厤秦隴，思欲泛洪河，闚巨靈，陟二華，盱秦嶺，一慰遡洄仰止之願，無從也。迺今服官豐校，應聘而來，始浮于河，達于渭，已而歷潼關，踰華陰，至止長安。時秋水方盛，澎湃淪漣，仰瞻華嶽、終南，出沒雲漢，曰：「美哉山河！此天下之奇觀也。昔人所稱陝區，不其然哉！豪傑者將在是乎？」旣而偕諸同事入棘院，縱觀多士之文，其立言雖殊，類皆明於經術之故，察於性命之微，通於時務之變。其氣昌而不肆，其志遠
translation_en:
…traveled in dreams through Qin and Long. I wished to sail upon the mighty Yellow River, glimpse the Great Spirit, ascend the two Hua peaks, and gaze upon the Qinling Mountains, thus satisfying for once my longing to seek out and look up to these places; yet I had no means of doing so. Now, holding an educational post at Feng [?], I came in response to an invitation. First I sailed upon the Yellow River and reached the Wei; then I passed through Tongguan, crossed Huayin, and arrived at Chang’an. The autumn waters were then at their height, surging and rippling. Looking up, I beheld Mount Hua and Mount Zhongnan appearing and disappearing amid the clouds of the Milky Way, and said: “How beautiful these mountains and rivers are! This is a wondrous sight under Heaven. Is this not indeed the Shaanxi region praised by men of old? Surely outstanding men are to be found here?”

Then I entered the examination compound with my colleagues and surveyed the candidates’ writings. Though their formulations differed, they were generally all lucid in their understanding of the principles of classical learning, discerning in the subtleties of human nature and destiny, and conversant with the changes in contemporary affairs. Their spirit was vigorous without being unrestrained; their aspirations were far-reaching…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而不迂其辭達而不支美而
非夸質而不俚咸可以儕于
作者之塗而鳴我
國家之盛焉因語諸同事者曰
於戲休哉此西土之善鳴者
也昔人所云嶽降非虛語哉
豪傑者非其人耶唯我
===
國家二百年于玆菁我棫樸之
化達於天下漸漬淪浹暨我
聖天子御極文教維新黎獻共臣
薄於海外矧玆岐豐之舊猶
有聖王之遺化者宜彬彬翼
翼若是乎其盛也抑余于多
士尤有所忠告焉昔傳稱雍
punctuated: 而不迂，其辭達而不支，美而非夸，質而不俚，咸可以儕于作者之塗，而鳴我國家之盛焉。因語諸同事者曰：「於戲，休哉！此西土之善鳴者也。昔人所云嶽降，非虛語哉！豪傑者非其人耶？唯我國家二百年于玆，菁我棫樸之化達於天下，漸漬淪浹。暨我聖天子御極，文教維新，黎獻共臣，薄於海外。矧玆岐豐之舊，猶有聖王之遺化者，宜彬彬翼翼若是乎其盛也！抑余于多士尤有所忠告焉。昔傳稱雍
translation_en: …yet not impractical. Their language is expressive without rambling, elegant without exaggeration, substantial without vulgarity. All may rank alongside accomplished authors and give voice to the flourishing of our dynasty. I therefore said to my colleagues: “Ah, how splendid! These are men of the western lands who give eloquent voice to their age. The ancients’ saying that the sacred peaks send down great men was surely no empty phrase! Are these not those outstanding men? For two hundred years now, our dynasty’s nurturing influence, celebrated in the Odes’ luxuriant mugwort [?] and clustered oaks, has reached throughout the realm, gradually permeating it to its depths. Since our sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne, cultural instruction has been renewed; worthy men everywhere have become his subjects, his influence reaching even beyond the seas. How much more so here in the ancient lands of Qi and Feng, where the transforming influence of the sage kings still survives! It is fitting that cultivated refinement and reverent diligence should flourish so abundantly here! Yet I have, especially, some earnest advice for these many scholars. An ancient account says of Yong…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
州土厚水深其民厚重質直
無驕惰浮靡之習凡民猶然
矧士人哉故其士人皆果敢
剛毅無巽懦輭美之風是以
其文亦皆卓犖雄偉無骫骳
萎薾之氣異日者祇奉
大對布列庶司當必有忠藎之
士不二心之臣出于其間以
===
仰副
聖主側席之求以共成輯寧之治
也已迺或忘其先資虧厥素
履顧自諉曰謀適不用也人
將訾之矣尚得謂之秦有人
哉主司者何以逭其罪也聞
punctuated:
州土厚水深，其民厚重質直，無驕惰浮靡之習。凡民猶然，矧士人哉？故其士人皆果敢剛毅，無巽懦輭美之風。是以其文亦皆卓犖雄偉，無骫骳萎薾之氣。異日者，祇奉大對，布列庶司，當必有忠藎之士、不二心之臣出于其間，以仰副聖主側席之求，以共成輯寧之治也已。
迺或忘其先資，虧厥素履，顧自諉曰：「謀適不用也。」人將訾之矣，尚得謂之秦有人哉？主司者何以逭其罪也？聞
translation_en:
…the region has deep soil and deep waters; its people are earnest, steadfast, unpretentious, and upright, without habits of arrogance, indolence, frivolity, or extravagance. If even the common people are like this, how much more so its scholars! Thus its scholars are all resolute, courageous, firm, and persevering, free from any tendency toward timidity, weakness, or pliant ingratiation. Their writings, accordingly, are outstanding and majestic, without any air of contortion or feebleness. In days to come, when they reverently present their responses at the Palace Examination and take their places in the various offices, surely there will emerge from among them men of devoted loyalty and ministers of undivided allegiance, who will fulfill our sage sovereign’s eager quest for worthy men and together bring about peaceful and harmonious government.
But if any forget their original endowments and compromise their accustomed conduct, merely excusing themselves by saying, “It is only that my counsels have not been put to use,” people will censure them. Could it still be said that Qin has worthy men? How could those presiding over the examination escape blame? I have heard…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之周人以玉爲璞宋人以腊
爲朴周人聞宋人有璞也禮
而索觀之宋人藏之什襲已
而出之乃腊也周人掩口而
笑今多士爲腊乎爲玉乎無
使主司若宋人然俾周人之
掩口也多士幸相與毖之是
===
舉也總督軍務前右都御史
兼兵部右侍郎王〔崇古〕今右
都御史兼兵部左侍郎王〔之
誥〕相繼殫猷靖域綏厥士類
巡撫陜西右副都御史張〔師
載〕保釐底績文教以興屬條
代屆行今右副都御史楊〔思
punctuated:
之。周人以玉爲璞，宋人以腊爲朴。周人聞宋人有璞也，禮而索觀之。宋人藏之什襲，已而出之，乃腊也。周人掩口而笑。今多士爲腊乎？爲玉乎？無使主司若宋人然，俾周人之掩口也。多士幸相與毖之。
是舉也，總督軍務前右都御史兼兵部右侍郎王〔崇古〕、今右都御史兼兵部左侍郎王〔之誥〕，相繼殫猷靖域，綏厥士類。巡撫陜西右副都御史張〔師載〕，保釐底績，文教以興。屬條代屆行，今右副都御史楊〔思
translation_en:
…this. A man of Zhou called jade “pu” (璞, unworked jade), while a man of Song called dried meat “pu” (朴). Hearing that the man of Song possessed a “pu,” the man of Zhou courteously asked to see it. The man of Song had stored it in ten layers of wrapping. When he finally brought it out, it was dried meat. The man of Zhou covered his mouth and laughed. Now, are you assembled scholars dried meat, or are you jade? Do not let the examination officials become like the man of Song, causing the man of Zhou to cover his mouth in laughter. May you scholars take heed together.
For this examination, the successive supreme commanders of military affairs—the former holder, Wang Chonggu, Censor-in-chief of the Right and concurrently Vice Minister of War of the Right, and the present holder, Wang Zhigao, Censor-in-chief of the Right and concurrently Vice Minister of War of the Left—have devoted their utmost planning to pacifying the region and fostering its scholars. Zhang Shizai, Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi and Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right, achieved results in maintaining peace and good governance, enabling literary education to flourish. As the time for his replacement and departure arrived [?], the present Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right, Yang Si…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
忠
風猷丕著士心夙嚮巡撫
右僉都御史延綏李〔尚智〕今
何〔東序〕寧夏沈〔應時〕甘肅王
〔輪〕撫治鄖陽汪〔道昆〕相與孱
騭中外雅重文教監察御史
茶馬楊〔相〕河東鹽法郜〔永春〕
稽餉蕭〔廩〕洪敷風紀士習丕
===
振兵科左給事中楊〔一魁〕戶
部郎中張〔體乾〕王〔基〕趙〔大倫〕
中書舍人孫〔惟清〕行人司左
司副唐〔文燦〕右事茲土嘉樂
敷惠左叅政溫〔如春〕右叅政
于〔錦〕梁〔明翰〕馮〔舜漁〕楊〔衍慶〕
左叅議沈〔人种〕右叅議楊〔樞〕
punctuated: 忠，風猷丕著，士心夙嚮。巡撫右僉都御史延綏李〔尚智〕、今何〔東序〕，寧夏沈〔應時〕，甘肅王〔輪〕，撫治鄖陽汪〔道昆〕，相與孱騭中外，雅重文教。監察御史茶馬楊〔相〕、河東鹽法郜〔永春〕、稽餉蕭〔廩〕，洪敷風紀，士習丕振。兵科左給事中楊〔一魁〕，戶部郎中張〔體乾〕、王〔基〕、趙〔大倫〕，中書舍人孫〔惟清〕，行人司左司副唐〔文燦〕，右事茲土，嘉樂敷惠。左叅政溫〔如春〕，右叅政于〔錦〕、梁〔明翰〕、馮〔舜漁〕、楊〔衍慶〕，左叅議沈〔人种〕，右叅議楊〔樞〕，
translation_en:
…[Yang Sizhong's] exemplary conduct and accomplishments were conspicuous, and the scholars had long looked up to him. The Grand Coordinators holding the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief—Li Shangzhi of Yansui and the present incumbent, He Dongxu; Shen Yingshi of Ningxia; and Wang Lun of Gansu—together with Wang Daokun, Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang, jointly exerted themselves within and without [?] and consistently esteemed literary instruction. The Investigating Censors Yang Xiang, responsible for tea and horses; Gao Yongchun, responsible for the Hedong salt administration; and Xiao Lin, responsible for auditing military provisions, broadly upheld discipline, greatly revitalizing scholarly conduct.

Yang Yikui, Left Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War; Zhang Tiqian, Wang Ji, and Zhao Dalun, Bureau Directors in the Ministry of Revenue; Sun Weiqing, a Drafter in the Secretariat; and Tang Wencan, Left Associate Director of the Office of Messengers, served in this territory [?] and gladly extended their beneficence. Wen Ruchun, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Yu Jin, Liang Minghan, Feng Shunyu, and Yang Yanqing, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Shen Renzhong, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Yang Shu, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
副使祁〔天敘〕張〔守中〕劉〔應時〕
張〔志孝〕楊〔栢〕僉事栗〔魁〕周〔馬〕
文〔健〕都司署都指揮僉事張
一〔正〕詹〔恩〕皆綜理防範協恭
于外右布政使楊〔守魯〕按察
使王〔元春〕趨事始至樂觀厥
成行太僕寺卿周〔京〕許〔東望〕
===
少卿劉〔時舉〕苑馬寺卿侯〔東〕
〔萊〕少卿黃〔襄〕同事一方法得
書
山東兖州府東平州儒學學
正高〔魁〕謹序
punctuated:
副使祁〔天敘〕、張〔守中〕、劉〔應時〕、張〔志孝〕、楊〔栢〕，僉事栗〔魁〕、周〔馬〕、文〔健〕，都司署都指揮僉事張一〔正〕、詹〔恩〕，皆綜理防範，協恭于外。右布政使楊〔守魯〕、按察使王〔元春〕，趨事始至，樂觀厥成。行太僕寺卿周〔京〕、許〔東望〕，少卿劉〔時舉〕，苑馬寺卿侯〔東〕〔萊〕，少卿黃〔襄〕，同事一方，法得書。
山東兖州府東平州儒學學正高〔魁〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Surveillance Vice Commissioners Qi Tianxu, Zhang Shouzhong, Liu Yingshi, Zhang Zhixiao, and Yang Bai; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Li Kui, Zhou Ma [?], and Wen Jian; and Zhang Yizheng and Zhan En, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners in the Regional Military Commission—all coordinated defensive precautions and worked together respectfully outside the examination compound. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Shoulu and Surveillance Commissioner Wang Yuanchun had only just arrived to take up their duties and were pleased to witness the examination’s successful completion. Zhou Jing and Xu Dongwang, Ministers of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud; Liu Shiju, its Vice Minister; Hou Donglai, Minister of the Court of Imperial Horse Pasturage; and Huang Xiang, its Vice Minister, served together in the same region and were therefore entitled, according to the rules, to be recorded here.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Gao Kui, School Director of the Confucian School of Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
樊遲問仁子曰愛人問知子曰知人
唯天下至聖爲能聰明睿知足以有臨也
其爲氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間其爲氣也配義與道無是
餒也是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
行有不慊於心則餒矣我故曰告子未
嘗知義以其外之也必有事焉而勿正
心勿忘勿助長也
===
內陽而外陰內健而外順內君子而外小
人
易
當位以節中正以通
夫易廣矣大矣以言乎遠則不禦以言乎
邇則靜而正以言乎天地之間則備矣
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
夫坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

樊遲問仁，子曰：「愛人。」問知，子曰：「知人。」

唯天下至聖，爲能聰明睿知，足以有臨也。

其爲氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其爲氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。行有不慊於心，則餒矣。我故曰：「告子未嘗知義，以其外之也。」必有事焉而勿正，心勿忘，勿助長也。

內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人。

易

當位以節，中正以通。

夫易，廣矣，大矣！以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正；以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Fan Chi asked about benevolence. The Master said, “Love others.” He asked about wisdom. The Master said, “Know others.”

Only the supreme sage under Heaven possesses the keen hearing, clear vision, profound understanding, and wisdom sufficient to preside over others.

As vital force (qi), it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. As vital force, it accompanies righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves. It is produced by the accumulation of righteous deeds, not acquired through an isolated act of righteousness. If one’s conduct fails to satisfy one’s heart, it starves. Thus I said, “Gaozi has never understood righteousness, because he regards it as external.” One must constantly attend to its cultivation without anticipating results. The heart must neither forget it nor help it grow by force.

Yang within and yin without; strength within and compliance without; gentlemen within and petty men without.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Occupying the proper position, one exercises restraint; through centrality and correctness, one achieves free passage.

How broad and great are the Changes! Speaking of what is distant, they have no bounds; speaking of what is near, they are still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, they encompass it all. Qian, when still, is concentrated; when moving, it is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness. Kun, when still, is closed; when moving, it opens. Thus it brings forth breadth …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
廣大配天地變通配四時陰陽之義配
日月易簡之善配至德
黃帝堯舜垂衣裳而天下治
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
德帝曰俞允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無遺
賢萬邦咸寧
厥土惟黃壤厥田惟上上
嚴恭寅畏天命自度
===
穆穆在上明明在下灼于四方
詩
鳲鳩在桑其子在棘淑人君子其儀不忒
其儀不忒正是四國
豈敢定居一月三捷
思皇多士生此王國王國克生維周之楨
敬之敬之天維顯思命不易哉無曰高高
在上陟降厥士日監在茲維予小子不
聰敬止日就月將學有緝熙于光明佛
punctuated:
廣大配天地，變通配四時，陰陽之義配日月，易簡之善配至德。
黃帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而天下治。

書
后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。帝曰：「俞！允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。」
厥土惟黃壤，厥田惟上上。
嚴恭寅畏，天命自度。
穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方。

詩
鳲鳩在桑，其子在棘。淑人君子，其儀不忒。其儀不忒，正是四國。
豈敢定居？一月三捷。
思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。
敬之，敬之！天維顯思，命不易哉！無曰高高在上，陟降厥士，日監在茲。維予小子，不聰敬止。日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。佛
translation_en:
…Its breadth and greatness match Heaven and Earth; its change and adaptability match the four seasons; the meaning of yin and yang matches the sun and moon; the excellence of ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.
The Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed.

Book of Documents
When the ruler recognizes the difficulty of being a ruler, and ministers recognize the difficulty of being ministers, government is well ordered and the common people apply themselves earnestly to virtue. The emperor said: “Yes! If it is indeed so, no good counsel will remain hidden, no worthy person will be left overlooked in the countryside, and the myriad states will all be at peace.”
Its soil is yellow loam; its fields are of the highest grade.
Be solemnly reverent, respectful, and fearful; measure yourself against Heaven’s mandate.
Majestic above, brilliantly discerning below, their radiance shines throughout the four quarters.

Book of Odes
The cuckoo is in the mulberry tree; its young are in the thorn bushes. The good man, the noble man, is unerring in his deportment. Unerring in his deportment, he sets right the states in all four quarters.
How could we dare to settle down? In one month we gained three victories.
How splendid are the many worthy men born in this royal kingdom! The royal kingdom can indeed bring them forth: they are the supporting pillars of Zhou.
Be reverent, be reverent! Heaven is manifestly discerning; its mandate is not easy to retain! Do not say that it is high, high above: it ascends and descends among its officers [?], daily watching over us here. I, the young one, lack understanding of reverence. Advancing day by day and progressing month by month, I shall learn to attain ever greater brightness. Assist …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時仔肩示我顯德行
春秋
春鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘
楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾
子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐
鄭十有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕
===
冬十有二月祭伯來〔隱公元年〕春王正月
公會王人齊侯宋公衛侯許男曹伯陳
世子款盟于洮〔僖公八年〕楚子蔡侯次
于厥貉〔文公十年〕六月公會宋公陳侯
衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同盟
于新城〔文公十有四年〕
公會晉侯及吳子於黃池〔哀公十有三年〕
禮記
忠信禮之本也義理禮之文也
punctuated:
時仔肩，示我顯德行。

春秋
春，鄭人來輸平。〔隱公六年〕
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。〔僖公四年〕
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月，己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕
冬，十有二月，祭伯來。〔隱公元年〕春，王正月，公會王人、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、許男、曹伯、陳世子款盟于洮。〔僖公八年〕楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉。〔文公十年〕六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。〔文公十有四年〕
公會晉侯及吳子於黃池。〔哀公十有三年〕
禮記
忠信，禮之本也；義理，禮之文也。
translation_en:
…in bearing this burden, and show me manifestly virtuous conduct.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, men of Zheng came to offer peace. 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin〕

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army; the covenant was concluded at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕

In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they made a joint covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕

In winter, in the twelfth month, the Earl of Zhai came. 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke met the king’s representative, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, heir apparent of Chen, to make a covenant at Tao. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xi〕 The Viscount of Chu and the Marquis of Cai encamped at Juehe. 〔Tenth year of Duke Wen〕 In the sixth month, the duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they made a joint covenant at Xincheng. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen〕

The duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Ai〕

Record of Rites

Loyalty and trustworthiness are the foundation of ritual; righteousness and principle are its outward form.

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮
天子者與天地參故德配天地兼利萬物
與日月並明明照四海而不遺微小其
在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕處則聽
雅頌之音行步則有環佩之聲升車則
有鸞和之音居處有禮進退有度百官
得其宜萬事得其序
先勞而後祿不亦易祿乎
===
第貳場
論
爲政貴有以來天下之善
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令州郡舉茂才異等可爲將相詔〔元封五年〕
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬
punctuated:
春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。

天子者，與天地參，故德配天地，兼利萬物，與日月並明，明照四海而不遺微小。其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽雅頌之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。

先勞而後祿，不亦易祿乎？

第貳場
論
爲政貴有以來天下之善。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令州郡舉茂才異等可爲將相詔〔元封五年〕。
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕。
擬
translation_en:
Bringing forth in spring and nurturing growth in summer constitute benevolence; gathering in autumn and storing in winter constitute righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music; righteousness is akin to ritual.

The Son of Heaven forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Thus his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, benefiting all things alike; his brilliance equals that of the sun and moon, illuminating all within the Four Seas without overlooking even the smallest things. At court, he follows the ordered principles of benevolence, sagacity, ritual, and righteousness; at leisure, he listens to the sounds of the Odes and Hymns. When he walks, his jade pendants sound; when he mounts his carriage, its bells ring. His conduct accords with ritual, and his advances and withdrawals observe due measure. The hundred officials each find their proper place, and all affairs attain their proper order.

If service comes before emoluments, does this not make emoluments easy to bestow?

Second Session
Discourse
In governing, what matters is having the means to attract the goodness of all under Heaven.

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Draft an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty ordering the provinces and commanderies to recommend men of outstanding talent and exceptional ability fit to serve as generals or chief ministers. 〔Fifth year of Yuanfeng.〕
Draft a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty conferring upon Fang Xuanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Thirteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Draft…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
三殿工成
欽定名額頒示中外廷臣
賀表〔嘉靖四十一年〕
判語五條
官員赴任過限
人戶以籍爲定
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
脩理橋梁道路
===
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問古者嗣服守文之主所以撫成業而致
盛治者其道非一也然詩書所載則于
敬天法祖三致意焉豈二者守成之要
與粤若夏商代有令主而說者何獨以
成王爲首稱與載觀周公戒成王曰無
念爾祖曰永言配命是矣乃其所自爲
佐武王觀兵開創不知於文王以服事
punctuated:
三殿工成，欽定名額，頒示中外，廷臣賀表〔嘉靖四十一年〕。
判語五條：官員赴任過限；人戶以籍爲定；禁止師巫邪術；邊境申索軍需；脩理橋梁道路。
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：古者嗣服守文之主，所以撫成業而致盛治者，其道非一也。然詩書所載，則于敬天法祖三致意焉。豈二者守成之要與？粤若夏商，代有令主，而說者何獨以成王爲首稱與？載觀周公戒成王，曰「無念爾祖」，曰「永言配命」，是矣。乃其所自爲，佐武王觀兵開創，不知於文王以服事
translation_en:
…a congratulatory memorial from the court officials on the completion of the three palace halls, whose names were imperially determined and promulgated at court and throughout the realm. 〔The forty-first year of Jiajing, 1562〕
Five legal judgments: Officials exceeding the time allowed for taking up their appointments; determining households’ status by their registration; prohibiting the heterodox arts of spirit mediums; requisitioning military supplies in frontier regions; repairing bridges and roads.
Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: In antiquity, rulers who succeeded to the throne and upheld the established institutions had more than one way of preserving the achievements they inherited and bringing about flourishing government. Yet the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents repeatedly emphasize revering Heaven and emulating one’s ancestors. Are these two things the essentials of preserving an inherited achievement? The Xia and Shang dynasties each had excellent rulers; why, then, do commentators single out King Cheng for foremost praise? Consider, moreover, the Duke of Zhou’s admonitions to King Cheng: “Do you not bear your ancestor in mind?” and “Ever seek to accord with the Mandate.” These are indeed right. Yet in his own conduct he assisted King Wu in reviewing his forces and founding a new dynasty. I wonder how this compared with King Wen’s serving …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
殷昭事上帝得無異與抑創守果二道
與及孔子論武周則又槩以達孝稱之
抑又何與歷漢唐宋英君誼辟非無克
盡其道者彼其崇泰時守斜封何又以
爲不足敬且法與至如宋臣有謂人君
若不畏天何事不可爲者有謂祖宗法
度不可廢者又有謂天不足畏祖不足
法者果孰爲正與我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏開天統人上謹明畏下
===
垂法守
存心有錄
昭鑒有錄可爲萬世不易之法程矣我
成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運以其所以欽若
憲章者著爲
聖學心法
文華寶鑑暨我
世宗肅皇帝纘承丕基
欽天有頌
punctuated: 殷、昭事上帝，得無異與？抑創守果二道與？及孔子論武、周，則又槩以達孝稱之，抑又何與？歷漢、唐、宋，英君誼辟，非無克盡其道者。彼其崇泰、時守、斜封，何又以爲不足敬且法與？至如宋臣，有謂人君若不畏天，何事不可爲者；有謂祖宗法度不可廢者；又有謂天不足畏、祖不足法者。果孰爲正與？我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，開天統人，上謹明畏，下垂法守。存心有錄，昭鑒有錄，可爲萬世不易之法程矣。我成祖文皇帝誕膺鴻運，以其所以欽若、憲章者，著爲《聖學心法》、《文華寶鑑》。暨我世宗肅皇帝纘承丕基，欽天有頌，
translation_en:
…Yin and illustriously serving the Lord on High—was there not a difference? Or are founding a dynasty and preserving it indeed two distinct ways? When Confucius discussed King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, however, he praised both alike for their consummate filial piety. Why was this? Throughout the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, there were certainly enlightened rulers and righteous sovereigns capable of fully fulfilling this way. Why, then, are their practices of “exalting Tai,” “seasonal observance,” and issuing “slant-sealed” appointments [?] nevertheless considered insufficiently worthy of reverence and emulation? As for the ministers of the Song, some said, “If a ruler does not fear Heaven, what might he not do?” Others said, “The laws and institutions of the ancestors must not be abandoned.” Yet others said, “Heaven need not be feared, and the ancestors need not be taken as models.” Which view is truly correct?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the realm of China, inaugurated Heaven’s mandate, and united its people. Above, he conscientiously maintained enlightened reverence; below, he handed down laws to be observed. There is a record concerning preserving the mind and a record concerning clear discernment, which can serve as unchanging standards for ten thousand generations. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen received the great mandate and set forth his means of reverently following Heaven and taking the ancestors as models in Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) and Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian). Then our Emperor Shizong Su succeeded to the great dynastic foundation; for revering Heaven, he composed a eulogy…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
敬一有箴
祖德有詩謌
陵有述固宛乎三聖相授受一道也可得而揄
揚其萬一與我
皇上踐祚以來
郊廟必躬必親於諸臣章奏動求
祖宗舊制所謂嚴恭寅畏作求世德者亦既至
矣而頻年災祲屢聞治效未臻豈圖治
之道抑有進于敬
===
天法
祖之外與子諸士抱致君之猷求試于有司頤
聖天子新德之助云
畢所藴以爲
問天地之道易知簡能古未有文也自儒
者各抒所見以立言而道始紛然多岐
矣由今攷之易曰河出圖洛出書聖人
則之謂伏羲則之以畫八卦神禹則之
以敘九章似也而或謂則龍馬爲圖非
punctuated:
《敬一》有箴，祖德有詩謌，陵有述，固宛乎三聖相授受一道也。可得而揄揚其萬一與？我皇上踐祚以來，郊廟必躬必親，於諸臣章奏動求祖宗舊制，所謂嚴恭寅畏、作求世德者，亦既至矣。而頻年災祲屢聞，治效未臻，豈圖治之道，抑有進于敬天法祖之外與？子諸士抱致君之猷，求試于有司，頤聖天子新德之助云，畢所藴以爲。

問：天地之道，易知簡能，古未有文也。自儒者各抒所見以立言，而道始紛然多岐矣。由今攷之，《易》曰：「河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」謂伏羲則之以畫八卦，神禹則之以敘九章，似也。而或謂則龍馬爲圖，非
translation_en:
…there is an admonition on Maintaining Unity in Reverence, poems and songs on ancestral virtue, and an account of the mausoleum. Surely these clearly embody the single Way transmitted successively among the three sage sovereigns. Can you extol even a ten-thousandth part of it? Since Our Emperor ascended the throne, he has invariably attended the suburban and ancestral temple sacrifices in person. In considering his ministers’ memorials, he constantly seeks the established institutions of his ancestors. What is called being solemnly reverent and respectfully fearful, and seeking to perpetuate the virtue of preceding generations, has thus reached its utmost expression. Yet reports of disasters and ominous phenomena have repeatedly arrived in recent years, and the desired results of government have not been attained. Could the way of seeking good government require something beyond revering Heaven and emulating the ancestors? You gentlemen cherish plans for guiding your ruler toward perfection and present yourselves for examination before the responsible officials. The concluding exhortation apparently asks you to set forth all that you have in store to assist the sage Son of Heaven in renewing his virtue [?; the transcription here is garbled].

Question: The Way of Heaven and Earth is easy to know and simple in its operation; in antiquity there were as yet no written formulations. Only after scholars began setting forth their respective views in words did the Way become confusedly divided into many paths. Examining the matter from the present standpoint, the Book of Changes says: “The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as models.” To say that Fuxi took the former as his model in drawing the Eight Trigrams, and that the divine Yu took the latter as his model in arranging the nine divisions, seems plausible. Yet some say that taking the dragon-horse as a model produced a chart, not…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
爲卦則洛龜爲書非爲疇果何所見與
有謂十爲河圖九爲洛書似也而或謂
九爲河圖十爲洛書抑何所據與有謂
河圖爲體洛書爲用者體用不一源與
有謂河圖主常洛書主變者常變果二
道與又有謂河圖天道而洛書人道河
圖天道無心而洛書聖人有憂然與否
與同一造化也河圖以相生順布于五
位而洛書以相制逆施于八方同一象
===
數也河圖之數五十有五而洛書之數
四十有五其旨可得而聞與易本自河
圖何以爲周孔之易其義則洛書疇本
自洛書何以爲洪範之用不出于河圖
此皆道統所由傳治道所攸繫者不可
以無辨也子諸士研理待問久矣竊願
有聞焉
問人才之盛衰古稱氣運之隆替世道之
治忽繫焉信斯言也運隆化洽宜莫如
punctuated:
爲卦，則洛龜爲書，非爲疇，果何所見與？有謂十爲河圖、九爲洛書，似也，而或謂九爲河圖、十爲洛書，抑何所據與？有謂河圖爲體、洛書爲用者，體用不一源與？有謂河圖主常、洛書主變者，常變果二道與？又有謂河圖天道而洛書人道，河圖天道無心而洛書聖人有憂，然與否與？同一造化也，河圖以相生順布于五位，而洛書以相制逆施于八方；同一象數也，河圖之數五十有五，而洛書之數四十有五，其旨可得而聞與？《易》本自河圖，何以爲周孔之《易》，其義則洛書？疇本自洛書，何以爲《洪範》之用，不出于河圖？此皆道統所由傳、治道所攸繫者，不可以無辨也。子諸士研理待問久矣，竊願有聞焉。
問：人才之盛衰，古稱氣運之隆替，世道之治忽繫焉。信斯言也，運隆化洽，宜莫如
translation_en:
…to make the trigrams, and took the turtle of the Luo River as the model for the Writing, rather than for the categories. What insight, indeed, underlies this claim? The assertion that ten represents the River Chart and nine the Luo Writing seems plausible; yet some say that nine represents the River Chart and ten the Luo Writing. On what grounds? Some hold that the River Chart constitutes substance and the Luo Writing function. Do substance and function not share a single source? Some hold that the River Chart governs constancy and the Luo Writing change. Are constancy and change really two distinct Ways? Others say that the River Chart represents the Way of Heaven and the Luo Writing the human Way, and that the River Chart, as the Way of Heaven, acts without conscious intent, whereas the Luo Writing embodies the sage’s concern. Is this so or not? Both embody the same creative transformations: yet the River Chart distributes the mutually generating phases in forward order among the five positions, while the Luo Writing deploys the mutually controlling phases in reverse order through the eight directions. Both embody the same images and numbers: yet the numbers of the River Chart total fifty-five, while those of the Luo Writing total forty-five. May we hear the meaning of this? The Book of Changes originally derives from the River Chart. Why, when it becomes the Book of Changes of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, does its meaning follow the Luo Writing? The categories originally derive from the Luo Writing. Why, in their application in the Great Plan, do they remain within the scope of the River Chart? These are all matters through which the succession of the Way is transmitted and upon which the Way of government depends; they must be carefully distinguished. You gentlemen have long studied principle in readiness for questioning. I would venture to ask to hear your views.
Question: Regarding the flourishing and decline of men of talent, the ancients spoke of the rise and fall of the fortunes of vital force, upon which order and disorder in the world depend. If these words are true, then for flourishing fortunes and all-pervading moral transformation, surely nothing should compare with …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
唐虞三代之初而于稽其才則舜五人
武王十人何若是少耶乃孔子稱才難
則又獨以爲盛焉何耶且阿衡以匹夫
興湯而三仁不能以存殷亦有三治保
衛三傑啓漢而人龍不足以延劉治忽
果無關于人才之多寡耶謂養之貴豫
矣而巖穴肇中興之業垂綸啓清明之
化養之果何校也謂求之貴廣矣而岳
牧之諮視辟舉制科之所取廣狹有間
===
而才不加多抑又何耶我
聖祖奮起淮甸除穢伐暴王師所向豪傑景從
一時翊
運佐命元勳方之舜武可得而歷數其盛與
我
皇上嗣守洪圖勵精化理辟德行舉遺佚虛心
求才奚啻饑渴而又數
詔內外臣工各舉所知可謂望治之極矣屬者
南北多事疆場未靖司銓者將慎簡以
punctuated: 唐虞三代之初，而于稽其才，則舜五人、武王十人，何若是少耶？乃孔子稱才難，則又獨以爲盛焉，何耶？且阿衡以匹夫興湯，而三仁不能以存殷；亦有三治保衛，三傑啓漢，而人龍不足以延劉，治忽果無關于人才之多寡耶？謂養之貴豫矣，而巖穴肇中興之業，垂綸啓清明之化，養之果何校也？謂求之貴廣矣，而岳牧之諮，視辟舉制科之所取，廣狹有間，而才不加多，抑又何耶？我聖祖奮起淮甸，除穢伐暴，王師所向，豪傑景從。一時翊運佐命元勳，方之舜武，可得而歷數其盛與？我皇上嗣守洪圖，勵精化理，辟德行，舉遺佚，虛心求才，奚啻饑渴！而又數詔內外臣工，各舉所知，可謂望治之極矣。屬者南北多事，疆場未靖，司銓者將慎簡以
translation_en:
…the beginnings of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and of the Three Dynasties. Yet when we examine their men of talent, Shun had five and King Wu ten. Why were they so few? Confucius spoke of the difficulty of finding talent, yet singled out these times as flourishing in it. Why? Moreover, the A-heng, Yi Yin, rose from the position of a commoner to bring Tang to power, whereas the three humane men could not preserve Yin. There were also the “three who governed and protected Wei” [?]. The Three Heroes established the Han, yet the “dragon among men” could not prolong the rule of the Liu house. Is good government or disorder truly unrelated to the number of talented men?

It is said that talent must be nurtured in advance; yet a man from a rocky cave laid the foundations for a restoration, and a man dangling a fishing line inaugurated enlightened rule. What difference, then, does nurturing talent really make? It is said that the search for talent must be broad; yet consultation with the chiefs of the regions and provincial governors differed in scope from recruitment through summons, recommendation, and special examinations. Why, then, did talent not become more abundant?

Our Sagely Progenitor rose in the Huai region, swept away corruption, and attacked the violent. Wherever his royal armies advanced, outstanding men followed like shadows. Can the abundance of those founding worthies who assisted his destined rise and aided his receipt of Heaven’s mandate be enumerated and compared with those of Shun and King Wu?

Our Emperor has inherited and safeguards the great imperial enterprise. He devotes himself to transformative government, summons men of virtuous conduct, and brings forward worthy men who have been overlooked. His open-minded quest for talent exceeds even hunger and thirst! Moreover, he has repeatedly commanded officials at court and in the provinces each to recommend those they know. His desire for good government may indeed be called utmost. Recently, troubles have multiplied in both north and south, and the frontiers remain unsettled. Those responsible for selecting officials will carefully choose them on the basis of…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
素而臨事有乏才之嘆其故何耶諸士
子夙以古才賢自期待繼自今將服案
有位其何所施措以比隆唐虞三代之
盛惟勿諱勿讓
問理財之道其來遠矣考之周禮所載理
其財之出而已而國不見其不足乃後
世理其財之入隨事立法而國用恒歉
焉此其故何與無論三代以上即在叔
世有患年饑用不足者而或告以薄稅
===
斂有貿租賦歲倍者而辭以爲反裘負
薪果足國之道有不在于厚征與亦有
歲蠲田租之半已而罷除十年者一時
號稱殷富其後言利之臣筭無遺利乃
不免爲虛耗豈賦斂之厚薄無關于財
用之充詘與嗣是以還有多方進者而
國用愈困有上會計錄者而撙節未聞
抑又何與我
國家稽古定制田有定賦賦有常法可謂纖
punctuated:
素，而臨事有乏才之嘆，其故何耶？諸士子夙以古才賢自期待，繼自今將服案有位，其何所施措，以比隆唐虞三代之盛？惟勿諱勿讓。
問：理財之道，其來遠矣。考之《周禮》所載，理其財之出而已，而國不見其不足。乃後世理其財之入，隨事立法，而國用恒歉焉，此其故何與？無論三代以上，即在叔世，有患年饑用不足者，而或告以薄稅斂；有貿租賦歲倍者，而辭以爲反裘負薪。果足國之道有不在于厚征與？亦有歲蠲田租之半，已而罷除十年者，一時號稱殷富。其後言利之臣筭無遺利，乃不免爲虛耗，豈賦斂之厚薄無關于財用之充詘與？嗣是以還，有多方進者，而國用愈困；有上《會計錄》者，而撙節未聞，抑又何與？我國家稽古定制，田有定賦，賦有常法，可謂纖
translation_en:
…in advance, yet when affairs arise there are lamentations over the lack of capable men. Why is this? You candidates have long aspired to emulate the talented and worthy men of antiquity. From this time forward, you will undertake official service [?] and hold office. What measures will you take to rival the flourishing ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties? Speak without concealment or diffidence.
Question: The way of managing public finances has a long history. Examining what is recorded in the Rites of Zhou, we find only the regulation of expenditure, yet the state did not suffer insufficiency. In later ages, however, governments regulated revenue and established rules as circumstances arose, yet state funds were constantly inadequate. Why was this? Leaving aside the Three Dynasties and earlier times, even in ages of decline, when someone worried that famine had left resources insufficient, he might be advised to reduce taxation. When someone proposed doubling annual revenue from land taxes [?], the proposal was rejected as being like carrying firewood while wearing a fur coat inside out. Can it be that the way to provide adequately for the state does not lie in heavy taxation? There were also rulers who remitted half the land tax each year and subsequently abolished it for ten years; their times were renowned for prosperity. Later, ministers who advocated financial gain calculated every possible source of profit, yet depletion could not be avoided. Can the severity or lightness of taxation have no bearing on the sufficiency or insufficiency of public funds? Thereafter, some brought in revenue by many means, yet state finances became still more straitened; others submitted Records of Fiscal Accounts, yet nothing was heard of economies in expenditure. Why, again, was this? Our dynasty consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions: land has fixed tax assessments, and taxation follows regular rules. These may be said to encompass the minutest…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
悉具備公私兼利矣嗣我
皇上登極之初
崇儉恤民罷不急之役停採辦之科
詔下所司有曰天下軍民十分窮困國用雖詘
豈忍照常徵派有曰朕加意節省用自有餘
除民今歲田租十之五踰年
建儲禮成又
詔賜民田租十之三至哉
王心古堯舜禹湯文武之仁天下不啻過也何
===
頃歲部國空虛邊鎮餽餉所需大司農
每告匱焉至
請下廷臣條上封事彙爲理財集議一書檄行
中外覆議以
聞者夫事窮則變變則通不知當何如而後可
以爲足國足民之策也爾諸生雅抱經
國之猷願明以告我
問方今天下之務可言者多矣其最重且
急者莫先於備邊而備邊之道莫要於
punctuated:
悉具備，公私兼利矣。嗣我皇上登極之初，崇儉恤民，罷不急之役，停採辦之科。詔下所司，有曰：「天下軍民十分窮困，國用雖詘，豈忍照常徵派？」有曰：「朕加意節省，用自有餘。」除民今歲田租十之五。踰年，建儲禮成，又詔賜民田租十之三。至哉，王心！古堯舜禹湯文武之仁天下，不啻過也。何頃歲部國空虛，邊鎮餽餉所需，大司農每告匱焉？至請下廷臣條上封事，彙爲《理財集議》一書，檄行中外，覆議以聞者。夫事窮則變，變則通，不知當何如而後可以爲足國足民之策也？爾諸生雅抱經國之猷，願明以告我。

問：方今天下之務，可言者多矣。其最重且急者，莫先於備邊；而備邊之道，莫要於
translation_en:
…complete in every detail, benefiting both public and private interests. Then, at the beginning of His Majesty’s reign, he upheld frugality and showed solicitude for the people, abolished nonessential labor services, and suspended levies for procurement. An edict issued to the responsible offices stated: “The soldiers and common people throughout the realm are in extreme distress. Though state funds are inadequate, how could I bear to impose levies as usual?” It also stated: “If I take special care to economize, there will naturally be more than enough for expenditure.” He remitted five-tenths of the people’s land tax for that year. The following year, when the ceremony establishing the heir apparent was completed, he again decreed a remission of three-tenths of the people’s land tax. How consummate is the royal heart! His benevolence toward all under Heaven more than surpasses that of the ancient rulers Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Why, then, have the state’s coffers [?] been empty in recent years, with the Minister of Revenue repeatedly reporting insufficient funds for the provisions and pay required by the frontier garrisons? Matters have reached the point that a request was made to have court officials submit sealed memorials setting out their proposals, to compile these into a volume entitled Collected Deliberations on Managing State Finances, and to circulate it by official dispatch to officials at court and in the provinces for further deliberation and reports to the throne. Now, when affairs reach an impasse, change follows; through change, a way opens. What, then, should be done to devise a policy that will provide sufficiency for both the state and the people? You students have long cherished plans for governing the state; I ask you to explain them clearly to me.

Question: Among the affairs of the realm today, there is much that could be discussed. Of the most important and urgent, none takes precedence over frontier defense; and among the means of defending the frontier, none is more essential than…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
兵將二者古今言任將制兵之法載在
往籍乚暇論已先是玁狁匪茹憑陵我
城郭虔劉我人民秉樞者有憂焉請
詔下中外臣工各陳所爲禦戎之策其論將有
曰求之貴廣任之貴專儲之貴豫是矣
乃今選之世冑出之因藝拔之行伍辟
之武科不可謂不廣也與之生殺貸之
小過以盃戰爲功而不以損傷爲罪不
可謂不專也自襲廕之士以至於廢閑
===
之錄列之將牒需次而拜不可謂不豫
也其論兵有曰養之貴優選之貴精練
之貴熟是矣乃今屯粒之外繼之民運
又繼之
內帑養之不已厚乎汰其老稚補其逋亡惟
其人不惟其數選之不已精乎操習有
期教演有法
聖天子大閱以振作于上憲臣分閱以激勵于
外練之不已熟乎如此者固宜將識士
punctuated: 兵將二者。古今言任將制兵之法，載在往籍，乚暇論已。先是玁狁匪茹，憑陵我城郭，虔劉我人民。秉樞者有憂焉，請詔下中外臣工，各陳所爲禦戎之策。其論將，有曰：「求之貴廣，任之貴專，儲之貴豫。」是矣。乃今選之世冑，出之因藝，拔之行伍，辟之武科，不可謂不廣也。與之生殺，貸之小過，以盃戰爲功，而不以損傷爲罪，不可謂不專也。自襲廕之士，以至於廢閑之，錄列之將牒，需次而拜，不可謂不豫也。其論兵，有曰：「養之貴優，選之貴精，練之貴熟。」是矣。乃今屯粒之外，繼之民運，又繼之內帑，養之不已厚乎？汰其老稚，補其逋亡，惟其人，不惟其數，選之不已精乎？操習有期，教演有法，聖天子大閱以振作于上，憲臣分閱以激勵于外，練之不已熟乎？如此者，固宜將識士
translation_en:
…the two elements of soldiers and generals. Methods of appointing generals and managing troops, discussed from antiquity to the present, are recorded in earlier writings; there is no leisure to discuss them here [?]. Previously, the Xianyun showed no restraint, assailing our cities and slaughtering our people. Those directing military affairs were troubled by this and requested an imperial edict ordering officials at court and in the provinces each to present proposals for resisting the invaders. Concerning generals, some said: “In seeking them, breadth matters; in employing them, undivided authority matters; in keeping them in reserve, advance preparation matters.” This is correct. Now they are selected from hereditary military families, brought forward on the basis of their skills [?], promoted from the ranks, and recruited through the military examinations. The search can hardly be called narrow. They are granted authority over life and death and forgiven minor faults; their fighting is counted as merit [?], while casualties are not treated as grounds for punishment. Their authority can hardly be called divided. From men who inherit office or receive it through hereditary privilege to those dismissed or left idle [?], they are entered in the registers of generals and appointed when their turn comes. This can hardly be called a lack of advance preparation.

Concerning soldiers, some said: “In supporting them, generosity matters; in selecting them, quality matters; in training them, proficiency matters.” This is correct. Now grain from military agricultural colonies is supplemented by grain transported by the civilian population, and further supplemented from the imperial treasury. Is their support not already generous? The old and the young are discharged, and deserters and the dead are replaced; attention is paid to the men themselves, not merely to their numbers. Is selection not already exacting? Drills take place at set times, and instruction and exercises follow established methods. The sage Son of Heaven holds grand reviews to rouse them from above, while censorial officials conduct separate reviews to spur them on in the provinces. Is their training not already thorough? Under such arrangements, surely generals ought to understand their soldiers…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
情士識將意昔人所謂如身之使臂臂
之使指以戰則克以守則固可也夫何
頻年以來醜虜內侮長驅深入而兵將
迄無成功其故可得而聞與抑任將制
兵之法或有出于羣議所未及與其在
陜西四鎮雖連歲烽燧稍寧而徹桑土
以爲陰雨之備不可以不講也諸士生
長密邇邊陲籌苛之稔矣盍詳著于篇以
觀爾經濟之藴
punctuated: 情，士識將意，昔人所謂如身之使臂、臂之使指，以戰則克，以守則固，可也。夫何頻年以來，醜虜內侮，長驅深入，而兵將迄無成功？其故可得而聞與？抑任將制兵之法，或有出于羣議所未及與？其在陜西四鎮，雖連歲烽燧稍寧，而徹桑土以爲陰雨之備，不可以不講也。諸士生長密邇邊陲，籌苛之稔矣，盍詳著于篇，以觀爾經濟之藴？
translation_en: …the feelings of the soldiers, while the soldiers understand their commanders’ intentions. As the ancients put it, this should be like the body directing its arms and the arms directing their fingers: victorious in battle and secure in defense. Why, then, in recent years have the detestable raiders invaded our territory and driven deep into it, while our soldiers and commanders have yet to achieve success? May we hear the reasons? Or might there be methods of appointing commanders and organizing troops that lie beyond what collective deliberation has so far considered? As for the four garrisons of Shaanxi, although their beacon signals have been somewhat quieter for several years running, we must still discuss gathering mulberry-root bark to prepare for rainy weather—that is, taking precautions against future danger. You gentlemen were born and raised close to the frontier and are well versed in planning for its difficulties [?]. Why not set forth your views in detail in your essays, so that we may see the depth of your capacity for statecraft?
