It is not merely that he is easy to remunerate when rewards are assigned for merit: even if the provisions that replace farming are insufficient, he does not worry. How could one say that, because obtaining them is difficult, he is difficult to remunerate? Although the emoluments intended to support the worthy are not withheld from Confucians, his ambition lies in achieving meritorious deeds, and he has no leisure to reckon his profit. It is not merely that he is easy to remunerate when service brings the honor of support [?]: even if the means provided to sustain his integrity are inadequate, he puts them out of mind. How could one say that, because maintaining him is difficult, remunerating him consequently…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
難哉是蓋處則爲純儒出則爲純臣者也豈與
徇私謀利之臣可同日語乎大抵持身事君無
二道而忠廉一心也故忠臣不私而家之厚者
於國必薄三代以下若晏平仲季文子者亦庶
幾約已爲國者乎然而功烈自卑公室自弱吾
不知其先勞者何義也無已其惟鞠躬盡瘁而
不以餘財負主者歟先儒許其有儒者氣象良
以是哉
第貳場
===
論
爲政貴有以來天下之善
文在中
同考試官教諭粟　批〔宏博以藻彩而愈文充贍以琢裁而益粹且一結渾脫先秦語意蓋工於篇而邃於〕
思者敬服
同考試官教諭李　批〔議論曾𤇆古雅充潤題義無餘蘊矣讀之令人三復不忍釋手予其三秦〕
之傑歟
punctuated:
難哉？是蓋處則爲純儒，出則爲純臣者也，豈與徇私謀利之臣可同日語乎？大抵持身事君無二道，而忠廉一心也。故忠臣不私，而家之厚者，於國必薄。三代以下，若晏平仲、季文子者，亦庶幾約已爲國者乎？然而功烈自卑，公室自弱，吾不知其先勞者何義也。無已，其惟鞠躬盡瘁，而不以餘財負主者歟？先儒許其有儒者氣象，良以是哉！

第貳場

論
爲政貴有以來天下之善
文在中

同考試官教諭粟，批〔宏博以藻彩而愈文，充贍以琢裁而益粹，且一結渾脫先秦語意，蓋工於篇而邃於〕思者，敬服。

同考試官教諭李，批〔議論曾𤇆，古雅充潤，題義無餘蘊矣。讀之令人三復，不忍釋手，予其三秦〕之傑歟！
translation_en:
…could providing him with a stipend then be difficult? Such a man is a pure Confucian scholar in retirement and a pure minister in office. How could he be spoken of in the same breath as ministers who pursue private interests and seek profit? Broadly speaking, conducting oneself and serving one’s ruler are not two separate ways: loyalty and incorruptibility spring from one heart. Thus a loyal minister does not pursue private advantage; one who lavishes resources upon his household must stint his state. Since the Three Dynasties, men such as Yan Pingzhong and Ji Wenzi have perhaps come close to practicing personal frugality for the sake of the state. Yet their achievements remained modest, and their ruling houses grew weak. I do not understand what principle informed their putting toil first. Must we, then, turn to the man who devoted himself utterly to his duties and did not betray his lord by leaving surplus wealth? Earlier Confucian scholars acknowledged that he possessed the bearing of a true Confucian. Surely this was why!

Second Session

Discourse
“In governing, what matters is having the means to attract all the good in the realm.”
By Wen Zaizhong 文在中.

Comment by Associate Examiner Su 粟, Instructor: “Broad and extensive, it becomes still more elegant through literary embellishment; ample and rich, it becomes still more refined through polishing and pruning. Moreover, its conclusion flows with unforced ease, conveying the language and spirit of the pre-Qin masters. Here is someone accomplished in composition and profound in thought. I respectfully admire him.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li 李, Instructor: “The argument is [?], classically elegant, ample, and rich, leaving none of the topic’s implications unexplored. Reading it makes one return to it repeatedly, unwilling to put it down. Are you not an outstanding talent of the Sanqin region?”

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張　批〔體格正大辭氣冲融可與論〕
政矣宜錄以式
考試官學正高　批〔明暢可誦〕
天下之道忘其在我者常裕而矜其所長者必
隘君子不自足其所已能而以其所不能者取
諸人則天下之治成矣何則天下不可以徒治
也所以爲之綱維而整齊之者有政焉政以綱
維整齊乎天下則其務誠繁而吾以一人之智
力聰明役役焉圖之將見智力愈竭聰明愈困
===
而天下之治卒不可得而理矣故善圖治者以
爲吾既以一身操可治之權則天下之才皆吾
之才天下之善皆吾之善吾惟延之以誠接之
以禮休休焉以廣其度則衆善畢集而天下有
餘治吾何爲敝精疲神以自用爲哉此好善所
以優于天下而朱子所以謂爲政者貴有以來
天下之善也且夫君子之爲天下國家也猶工
師之爲巨室也引繩墨運規矩操斧斤以爲欂
櫨榱桷栒楔户牖有非一手一足之所能致者
punctuated:
考試官教諭張，批〔體格正大，辭氣冲融，可與論〕政矣，宜錄以式。
考試官學正高，批〔明暢可誦〕。
天下之道，忘其在我者常裕，而矜其所長者必隘。君子不自足其所已能，而以其所不能者取諸人，則天下之治成矣。何則？天下不可以徒治也。所以爲之綱維而整齊之者，有政焉。政以綱維整齊乎天下，則其務誠繁，而吾以一人之智力聰明，役役焉圖之，將見智力愈竭，聰明愈困，而天下之治卒不可得而理矣。故善圖治者以爲：吾既以一身操可治之權，則天下之才皆吾之才，天下之善皆吾之善。吾惟延之以誠，接之以禮，休休焉以廣其度，則衆善畢集，而天下有餘治。吾何爲敝精疲神，以自用爲哉？此好善所以優于天下，而朱子所以謂爲政者貴有以來天下之善也。且夫君子之爲天下國家也，猶工師之爲巨室也。引繩墨，運規矩，操斧斤，以爲欂櫨、榱桷、栒楔、户牖，有非一手一足之所能致者。
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The composition is upright and grand in form, and its language and tone are harmonious and easy. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss government. It should be recorded as a model.”
Examiner Gao, School Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent, well worth reciting.”
In the affairs of the world, those who forget their own abilities always have ample capacity, whereas those who pride themselves on their strengths inevitably become confined. If the gentleman does not rest content with what he can already do, but draws on others for what he cannot do, good government throughout the realm will be achieved. Why is this? The realm cannot be governed single-handedly. Government provides the framework that holds it together and brings it into order. Since government must hold the realm together and order it, its tasks are indeed numerous. If I labor at them with only one person’s intelligence, strength, and discernment, these powers will become increasingly exhausted and strained, and in the end the realm’s affairs will still prove impossible to put in order.
Thus one who knows how to seek good government reasons: Since I hold in my own person the authority to govern, all the talents of the realm are my talents, and all the goodness of the realm is my goodness. If I simply invite others with sincerity, receive them with ritual courtesy, and generously broaden my capacity to accommodate them, every kind of goodness will gather, and there will be more than enough capacity to govern the realm. Why should I wear out my energies and exhaust my spirit by relying solely on myself? This is why a love of goodness makes one amply capable of governing the realm, and why Master Zhu said that those who govern should prize having the means to attract the goodness of the realm.
Moreover, the gentleman’s governance of the realm and its states is like a master builder’s construction of a great house. Stretching the inked measuring cord, wielding compass and square, and handling axes and adzes to make brackets, rafters, crossbars, doorposts, doors, and windows—these include things that no single pair of hands and feet can accomplish…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
使工師事事而自用之則天下之拙工也此猶
其小者也天以於穆尸其柄而日月以司暄雨
露以司潤風雷以司鼓霜雪以司斂五氣四序
以司推行夫然後天得以成其化使天而自爲
之暄爲之潤爲之鼓斂推行則天道亦幾乎息
矣况乎天下之大兆民之廣所以寄賴乎我者
饑寒昏墊之欲得其所顓明强弱之欲復其性
禮樂欲其明備政教欲其脩舉天地欲其位育
日月星辰欲其貞麗雨暘燠寒風欲其時若昆
===
蟲鳥獸草木欲其茂對四海八荒九夷百蠻欲
其撫御其責不既重哉以如是之責而萃于吾
之一身將責以智慮乎智可以解紛也而一人
之智何以周天下之務將責以强乎强可以有
爲也而一人之强何以勝天下之繁將責以聞
識乎聞識可以給辨也而一人之聞識何以盡
天下之聰明故君子于此欲有以稱天下之責
則必深長思曰謂吾足智矣而視天下以愚可
乎謂吾强矣而視天下以弱可乎謂吾多聞識
punctuated: 使工師事事而自用之，則天下之拙工也。此猶其小者也。天以於穆尸其柄，而日月以司暄，雨露以司潤，風雷以司鼓，霜雪以司斂，五氣四序以司推行。夫然後天得以成其化。使天而自爲之暄，爲之潤，爲之鼓斂推行，則天道亦幾乎息矣。况乎天下之大，兆民之廣，所以寄賴乎我者：饑寒昏墊之欲得其所，顓明强弱之欲復其性，禮樂欲其明備，政教欲其脩舉，天地欲其位育，日月星辰欲其貞麗，雨暘燠寒風欲其時若，昆蟲鳥獸草木欲其茂對，四海八荒九夷百蠻欲其撫御。其責不既重哉？以如是之責而萃于吾之一身，將責以智慮乎？智可以解紛也，而一人之智何以周天下之務？將責以强乎？强可以有爲也，而一人之强何以勝天下之繁？將責以聞識乎？聞識可以給辨也，而一人之聞識何以盡天下之聰明？故君子于此欲有以稱天下之責，則必深長思曰：「謂吾足智矣，而視天下以愚，可乎？謂吾强矣，而視天下以弱，可乎？謂吾多聞識
translation_en:
… If a master builder undertook every task himself, relying solely on his own abilities, he would be the clumsiest craftsman in the world. Yet this is still a minor example. Heaven, profound and silent, presides over its authority, while the sun and moon administer warmth, rain and dew administer moisture, wind and thunder administer stirring into motion, frost and snow administer gathering in, and the five vital energies and four seasons administer the onward course of change. Only then can Heaven accomplish its transforming work. If Heaven itself had to provide warmth and moisture, stir things into motion and gather them in, and carry forward their successive changes, then even the Way of Heaven would nearly cease.

How much more is this true of the vast realm and its countless people! What they depend upon me for is this: that those suffering hunger, cold, distress, and inundation should find their proper place; that the dull and intelligent, strong and weak should recover their inherent nature; that rites and music should be clearly established and complete; that government and instruction should be cultivated and put into effect; that Heaven and Earth should occupy their proper places and all things receive nourishment; that the sun, moon, and stars should remain properly attached to their appointed stations; that rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind should accord with their seasons; that insects, birds, beasts, grasses, and trees should flourish in harmony; and that the Four Seas, the Eight Wildernesses, the Nine Yi, and the Hundred Man should be pacified and governed. Is this responsibility not exceedingly heavy?

With such responsibilities concentrated in my single person, shall I look to intelligence and deliberation to fulfill them? Intelligence can resolve entanglements, but how can one person's intelligence encompass all the affairs of the realm? Shall I look to strength? Strength can accomplish things, but how can one person's strength cope with the realm's manifold concerns? Shall I look to learning and knowledge? Learning and knowledge can enable ready discernment, but how can one person's learning and knowledge encompass all the perceptiveness and understanding in the realm? Thus, if the gentleman wishes to measure up to his responsibilities toward the realm, he must reflect deeply and at length, saying: “May I consider myself sufficiently wise and regard everyone in the realm as foolish? May I consider myself strong and regard everyone in the realm as weak? May I consider myself widely learned and knowledgeable …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
矣而視天下以聾瞶可乎又必深長思曰大智
如舜而好問察多才藝如周公而三吐握天縱
多能如孔子而好敏求此三聖人者豈不自知
其能而好爲是屑屑然之不憚煩哉無亦以天
下之善無窮而一人有不足恃者乎故智不如
舜吾何爲而不好問且察才藝不如周公吾何
爲而不吐握天縱不如孔子吾何爲而不敏求
易曰山上有澤咸君子以虛受人言山澤之氣
乘虛而通也彖曰觀其所感而天地萬物之情
===
可見矣感之義大矣哉詩曰采葑采菲無以下
體言葑菲小物也猶有足采焉况于善之大乎
故使爲政者必其自智自强自聞識而後用之
則山澤不相通也葑菲不足采也吾恐滿假之
態一彰而天下之智者强者多聞識者必將曰
彼智矣而何有于吾之智彼强矣而何有于吾
之强彼多聞識矣而何有于吾之聞識由是天
下之懷才抱德者皆將裹足不敢入境孰肯甘
心降氣以聽彼訑訑然之拒哉夫以天下之政
punctuated: 矣，而視天下以聾瞶，可乎？又必深長思曰：「大智如舜，而好問察；多才藝如周公，而三吐握；天縱多能如孔子，而好敏求。此三聖人者，豈不自知其能，而好爲是屑屑然之不憚煩哉？無亦以天下之善無窮，而一人有不足恃者乎？故智不如舜，吾何爲而不好問且察？才藝不如周公，吾何爲而不吐握？天縱不如孔子，吾何爲而不敏求？」《易》曰：「山上有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。」言山澤之氣乘虛而通也。《彖》曰：「觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。」感之義大矣哉！《詩》曰：「采葑采菲，無以下體。」言葑菲小物也，猶有足采焉，况于善之大乎？故使爲政者必其自智、自强、自聞識而後用之，則山澤不相通也，葑菲不足采也。吾恐滿假之態一彰，而天下之智者、强者、多聞識者必將曰：「彼智矣，而何有于吾之智？彼强矣，而何有于吾之强？彼多聞識矣，而何有于吾之聞識？」由是天下之懷才抱德者，皆將裹足不敢入境，孰肯甘心降氣，以聽彼訑訑然之拒哉？夫以天下之政
translation_en:
…and regard everyone under Heaven as deaf and blind—is that permissible? He must also reflect deeply: “Even Shun, with his great wisdom, delighted in questioning and examining; even the Duke of Zhou, with his many talents and accomplishments, repeatedly spat out his food and held his unbound hair to receive worthy men; even Kongzi, endowed by Heaven with many abilities, delighted in diligently seeking knowledge. Could these three sages have been unaware of their own abilities, choosing to busy themselves with such details and never shrinking from the trouble? Was it not because the goodness found throughout the world is inexhaustible, while the abilities of one person cannot be wholly relied upon? Thus, since my wisdom falls short of Shun’s, why should I not delight in questioning and examining? Since my talents and accomplishments fall short of the Duke of Zhou’s, why should I not interrupt eating and washing my hair to receive worthy men? Since my natural endowments fall short of Kongzi’s, why should I not diligently seek knowledge?”

The Book of Changes says: “Above the mountain is a marsh: Influence. The noble man accordingly receives others with an open mind.” This means that the vital energies of mountain and marsh communicate through openness. The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Observe what they influence, and the true dispositions of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things can be seen.” Great indeed is the significance of influence! The Book of Odes says: “When gathering turnips and radishes, do not reject them on account of their lower parts.” This means that even such humble things as turnips and radishes have something worth gathering—how much more so the greater good found in people!

Thus, if those who govern insist on relying upon their own wisdom, their own strength, and their own learning and discernment before putting anything to use, then mountain and marsh cannot communicate, and turnips and radishes have nothing worth gathering. I fear that once their self-satisfied arrogance becomes apparent, the wise, the strong, and those of extensive learning and discernment throughout the world will surely say: “He is wise already—what use has he for my wisdom? He is strong already—what use has he for my strength? He already has extensive learning and discernment—what use has he for mine?” Consequently, all those throughout the world who possess talent and virtue will hold back, not daring to enter his territory. Who would willingly humble himself merely to hear that complacent rejection? Now, as for the government of all under Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
待我而備天下之治待我而成而吾方拒人于
千里之外以自用其所長則是瞳不以日月也
潤不以雨露也鼓不以風霤也斂不以霜雪也
推行不以五氣四序也其何以爲天道則是繩
墨不以衆任而以工師規矩斧斤不以衆任而
以工師欂櫨樉桷栒楔户牖不以衆任而以工
師其爲以爲巨室君子知其然以爲吾有天下
國家之政吾治天下國家也吾治天下國家則
吾之善天下國家之善也天下國家之善吾之
===
善也何我非人何物非我由是體澤山之虛以
立其感法地山之謙以廣其益廓太公之量以
弘其受誠心以延之緩辭以導之和顏色以接
之皇皇焉如不及已未善吾舍焉人有善吾從
焉芻蕘可詢則不以人廢葑菲可采則不以物
遺禹聞之而拜吾益以旌焉周公三吐握吾百
焉由是戴仁負義之士近而州里遠而四海之
廣小而一才一藝大而馮翼孝德皆將裹糧載
質以遊于吾之庭如商賈之趨市行旅之赴家
punctuated: 待我而備，天下之治待我而成，而吾方拒人于千里之外，以自用其所長，則是瞳不以日月也，潤不以雨露也，鼓不以風霤也，斂不以霜雪也，推行不以五氣四序也，其何以爲天道？則是繩墨不以衆任而以工師，規矩斧斤不以衆任而以工師，欂櫨樉桷栒楔户牖不以衆任而以工師，其爲以爲巨室？君子知其然，以爲吾有天下國家之政，吾治天下國家也。吾治天下國家，則吾之善，天下國家之善也；天下國家之善，吾之善也。何我非人？何物非我？由是體澤山之虛以立其感，法地山之謙以廣其益，廓太公之量以弘其受，誠心以延之，緩辭以導之，和顏色以接之，皇皇焉如不及。已未善，吾舍焉；人有善，吾從焉。芻蕘可詢，則不以人廢；葑菲可采，則不以物遺。禹聞之而拜，吾益以旌焉；周公三吐握，吾百焉。由是戴仁負義之士，近而州里，遠而四海之廣，小而一才一藝，大而馮翼孝德，皆將裹糧載質，以遊于吾之庭，如商賈之趨市，行旅之赴家。
translation_en:
…depends on me for its completion, and orderly government throughout the realm depends on me for its achievement. Yet if I keep others a thousand li away and rely solely on my own strengths, this would be like providing illumination [?] without the sun and moon, moisture without rain and dew, stirring things without wind and rain [?], drawing things inward without frost and snow, and advancing the processes of nature without the five vital forces and the four seasons. How could this constitute the Way of Heaven? It would be like entrusting the inked marking line, the compass and square, the axes and adzes, and the brackets, beams and rafters [?], crosspieces and wedges, doors and windows, all to the master craftsman rather than distributing these responsibilities among the workers. How could a great mansion be built in this way [?]?

The gentleman understands this and thinks: “I bear responsibility for governing the realm and its states and households; I govern them. Since I govern them, my goodness is their goodness, and their goodness is mine. In what respect am I not others? What thing is not part of me?” Thus he embodies the receptivity of the marsh above the mountain to establish mutual responsiveness, and models himself on the humility of the earth above the mountain to broaden the benefits he receives. He expands his capacity to match that of the Grand Duke, Taigong, so as to receive others more generously. He invites them with sincerity, guides them with gentle words, and welcomes them with a kindly expression, eagerly striving as though he could never do enough. “Where my own conduct is not good [?], I abandon it; where others possess goodness, I follow it. If grass-cutters and wood-gatherers can be consulted, I will not dismiss their counsel because of who they are. If turnips and radishes are worth gathering, I will not overlook them because of what they are. Yu bowed upon hearing good counsel; I will go further in honoring it. The Duke of Zhou spat out his food and grasped his unbound hair three times to receive worthy men; I will do so a hundred times.”

Thus men who uphold benevolence and bear righteousness, from nearby communities to the farthest reaches within the Four Seas, whether possessing a single talent or skill, or the greater qualities of supporting others and filial virtue [?], will all pack provisions and carry gifts of introduction to visit my court, like merchants hastening to market and travelers making their way home.

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
吾不有其智而天下之智歸焉吾不有其强而
天下之强歸焉吾不有其聞識而天下之聞識
歸焉譬則昆山之玉隋和之寶明月之珠大阿
之劍鮮離之馬翠鳳之旗靈鼉之鼓夜光之璧
犀象之器所謂不產于秦而皆秦之有也夫然
後以天下才治天下事吾惟宰其功而已矣以
天下事付天下之能者吾惟觀其成而已矣我
無專智而有餘智我無專强而有餘强我無專
聞識而有餘聞識由之以禮樂則明備以刑政
===
則脩明以饑寒昏墊則無不安其所以顓明强
弱則無不適其性以裁成其道輔相其宜則天
地可位萬物可育日月星辰可以順軌雨暘燠
寒風可以時若昆蟲草木鳥獸之繁可以時育
四海八荒九夷百蠻之在撫御者可化而歸其
始也以天下之責而統之為一人之責其旣也
以一人之責而分之為衆人之責其究也至于
衆人之責舉而一人之責以塞故以此而君則
為堯舜為禹湯文武而君道成矣以此而相則
punctuated: 吾不有其智，而天下之智歸焉；吾不有其强，而天下之强歸焉；吾不有其聞識，而天下之聞識歸焉。譬則昆山之玉、隋和之寶、明月之珠、大阿之劍、鮮離之馬、翠鳳之旗、靈鼉之鼓、夜光之璧、犀象之器，所謂不產于秦而皆秦之有也。夫然後以天下才治天下事，吾惟宰其功而已矣；以天下事付天下之能者，吾惟觀其成而已矣。我無專智而有餘智，我無專强而有餘强，我無專聞識而有餘聞識。由之以禮樂則明備，以刑政則脩明，以饑寒昏墊則無不安其所，以顓明强弱則無不適其性。以裁成其道、輔相其宜，則天地可位，萬物可育，日月星辰可以順軌，雨暘燠寒風可以時若，昆蟲草木鳥獸之繁可以時育，四海八荒九夷百蠻之在撫御者可化而歸。其始也，以天下之責而統之為一人之責；其旣也，以一人之責而分之為衆人之責；其究也，至于衆人之責舉而一人之責以塞。故以此而君，則為堯舜、為禹湯文武，而君道成矣；以此而相，則
translation_en:
I do not claim wisdom as my own, and the wisdom of all under Heaven converges upon me; I do not claim strength as my own, and the strength of all under Heaven converges upon me; I do not claim learning and knowledge as my own, and the learning and knowledge of all under Heaven converge upon me. It is like the jade of Mount Kun, the treasures of Sui and He, the bright-moon pearls, the sword Da’e, the horse Xianli, banners adorned with kingfisher feathers and phoenixes, drums of sacred alligator hide, night-shining jade discs, and vessels of rhinoceros horn and ivory: as the saying goes, none were produced in Qin, yet all were possessed by Qin. Only then can I employ the talents of all under Heaven to manage the affairs of all under Heaven, merely presiding over their achievements. Entrusting the affairs of all under Heaven to its capable people, I need only observe their accomplishment. I possess no exclusive wisdom, yet have wisdom to spare; no exclusive strength, yet have strength to spare; no exclusive learning and knowledge, yet have learning and knowledge to spare.

Applying this to rites and music makes them illustrious and complete; to punishments and government, well ordered and clear. Among those suffering hunger, cold, and the misery of inundation, none will lack a secure place; among the dull [?] and intelligent, the strong and weak, none will fail to find conditions suited to their nature. By bringing the Way of Heaven and Earth to completion and assisting what is fitting to them, Heaven and Earth can take their proper places and the myriad things can be nourished. The sun, moon, and stars can follow their courses; rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind can arrive in season; and the multitudes of insects, plants, birds, and beasts can flourish at their proper times. Those within the Four Seas and Eight Wastes, the Nine Yi and Hundred Man peoples, who are under our care and governance can be transformed and give their allegiance.

At the outset, the responsibilities of all under Heaven are gathered into the responsibility of one person. Thereafter, that one person’s responsibility is apportioned among the many. Ultimately, the responsibilities of the many are discharged, and thereby the responsibility of the one is fulfilled. Thus, one who rules by this means becomes a Yao or Shun, a Yu, Tang, Wen, or Wu, and fulfills the Way of the ruler; one who serves as chief minister by this means will …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
爲臯夔爲伊傅周召而相道得矣君德脩則萬
民化相道得則萬國理天下不足治矣嚮使自
矜而不虛拒人于千里而不受則雖堯舜禹湯
文武之爲君臯夔伊傅周召之爲臣亦不能治
矣何也舍好善而望治是猶適越而北轅也驅
馳雖勤其曷能及乎雖然不好善無以來天下
之善固不足言矣亦有好善而不足以來天下
之善者何哉天下有陽好而陰嫉者有始好而
終疎者其失也僞有實好而不知其善者其失
===
也愚有知而不能舉舉不能先者其失也命有
一于此皆非所謂能好也天下豈肯輕身而來
告以善哉故僞則拒人甚于訑訑人將有惟恐
其影嚮之不幽矣愚則碔砆進而和璧去矣命
則利餌者進而冥鴻遠矣孟子稱樂正子以好
善而許其優于天下非以其爲信人乎書秦誓
言大臣一个人也徒以其斷斷好善不特足以
利黎民而后世子孫皆能保焉至于娼嫉之人
非不知善之當好徒以其好之不誠非特遠而
punctuated: 爲臯夔，爲伊傅周召，而相道得矣。君德脩則萬民化，相道得則萬國理，天下不足治矣。嚮使自矜而不虛，拒人于千里而不受，則雖堯舜禹湯文武之爲君，臯夔伊傅周召之爲臣，亦不能治矣。何也？舍好善而望治，是猶適越而北轅也。驅馳雖勤，其曷能及乎？雖然，不好善，無以來天下之善，固不足言矣。亦有好善而不足以來天下之善者，何哉？天下有陽好而陰嫉者，有始好而終疎者，其失也僞；有實好而不知其善者，其失也愚；有知而不能舉，舉不能先者，其失也命。有一于此，皆非所謂能好也。天下豈肯輕身而來告以善哉？故僞則拒人甚于訑訑，人將有惟恐其影嚮之不幽矣；愚則碔砆進而和璧去矣；命則利餌者進而冥鴻遠矣。孟子稱樂正子以好善，而許其優于天下，非以其爲信人乎？《書》《秦誓》言大臣一个人也，徒以其斷斷好善，不特足以利黎民，而后世子孫皆能保焉。至于娼嫉之人，非不知善之當好，徒以其好之不誠，非特遠而
translation_en:
…become Gao Yao and Kui, Yi Yin and Fu Yue, or the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, and thus attain the proper way of the minister. When the ruler’s virtue is cultivated, the myriad people are transformed; when the proper way of the minister is attained, the myriad states are well ordered. Governing all under Heaven then presents no difficulty. If, instead, they were conceited rather than receptive, keeping others a thousand li away and refusing to receive them, then even rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and ministers such as Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, could not achieve good government. Why? To abandon the love of goodness yet hope for good government is like setting out for Yue with one’s carriage facing north. However diligently one drives, how could one arrive?
Yet those who do not love goodness and thus cannot attract the goodness of all under Heaven scarcely need discussion. There are also those who love goodness but still cannot attract it. Why is this? Some outwardly love it but inwardly resent it; some love it at first but eventually become estranged from it. Their failing is insincerity. Some sincerely love it but cannot recognize what is good. Their failing is foolishness. Some recognize worthy men but cannot promote them, or promote them without giving them precedence. Their failing is “command” [?]. Anyone with even one of these failings cannot be said truly to know how to love goodness. How could people throughout the realm willingly lower themselves by coming to tell such a person what is good?
Insincerity therefore repels people more strongly than self-satisfied arrogance: people will fear only that their very shadows and sounds are not sufficiently concealed. With foolishness, stones resembling jade are advanced while the jade disk of He is cast away. With “command” [?], those lured by profit advance, while the wild geese soaring in the heights withdraw far away. When Mengzi praised Yuezhengzi for loving goodness and judged him more than equal to governing all under Heaven, was it not because he was a trustworthy man? The “Oath of Qin” in the Book of Documents speaks of a certain minister. Simply because he sincerely loves goodness, he can not only benefit the common people but also safeguard the descendants of later generations. As for the envious [?], it is not that they do not know goodness ought to be loved; it is simply that their love of it is insincere. Not only in the distant future…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
子孫不我能保雖近而黎民亦危而不安矣由
是觀之天下後世之利與不利而在乎一人好
善之實與不實爲政者其可以弗早辨哉
表
擬
三殿工成
欽定名額頒示中外廷臣
賀表〔嘉靖四十一年〕
高士徵
===
同考試官教諭謝　批〔士懋鼎新名崇三極〕
〔先皇弘功深意未易揄揚子能敷詞章以宣盛美而祝願數言尤徵忠愛非徒藻〕
〔麗爲工巳耳是用表出〕
考試官教諭張　批〔美華宏詞鋪張盛事于其身〕
〔伏睠畝而心遊〕
〔廊廟者耶日且觀光尚占敷對〕
考試官學正高　批〔以忠愛之意發典則之詞可以爲文矣〕
嘉靖四十一年某月某日恭遇
大工告成
punctuated:
子孫不我能保，雖近而黎民亦危而不安矣。由是觀之，天下後世之利與不利，而在乎一人好善之實與不實，爲政者其可以弗早辨哉？

表

擬三殿工成，欽定名額，頒示中外，廷臣賀表〔嘉靖四十一年〕
高士徵

同考試官教諭謝　批〔士懋鼎新，名崇三極。〕〔先皇弘功深意，未易揄揚。子能敷詞章以宣盛美，而祝願數言尤徵忠愛，非徒藻〕〔麗爲工巳耳，是用表出。〕

考試官教諭張　批〔美華宏詞，鋪張盛事。于其身〕〔伏睠畝而心遊〕〔廊廟者耶？日且觀光，尚占敷對。〕

考試官學正高　批〔以忠愛之意，發典則之詞，可以爲文矣。〕

嘉靖四十一年某月某日，恭遇大工告成。
translation_en:
…he cannot protect his descendants; even those close at hand, the common people, are endangered and cannot live in security. Viewed in this light, benefit or harm to the world and to later generations depends upon whether a single person’s love of goodness is genuine. How could those who govern fail to distinguish this early on?

Memorial

Draft congratulatory memorial by the court officials on the completion of the Three Halls, whose names were imperially determined and promulgated at court and throughout the realm. 〔Forty-first year of Jiajing [1562].〕
By Gao Shizheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔The undertaking is renewed with vigor [?], and the names exalt the Three Ultimates.〕〔The late emperor’s magnificent achievement and profound intentions are not easily extolled. You have elaborated your composition to proclaim their surpassing excellence, while your few words of benediction especially attest to loyalty and devotion. This is not merely a display of〕〔literary ornament and elegance; for this reason it has been singled out.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Splendid, grand language gives full expression to this magnificent occasion. Is he one whose person〕〔lies amid the fields [?], while his mind roams〕〔the halls of government? Soon he will behold the splendor of the court; we may yet anticipate his responses there [?].〕

Comment by Examiner Gao, School Instructor: 〔To express loyal devotion in language that accords with classical standards is indeed to be capable of literary composition.〕

On a certain day of a certain month in the forty-first year of Jiajing [1562], we respectfully mark the occasion of the completion of the great construction works…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
欽名三殿曰
皇極
中極
建極左右樓曰文昭武成門曰會極歸極弘政
宣治頒示中外者伏以
宸宇煇煌弘規奠萬年鞏固
璇題昭揭奧義超千古維新制允斷于
睿謨工實創于
帝造臣民快覩朝野欣騰臣等誠懽誠忭稽首
===
頓首竊惟明堂日御垂衣正八表之瞻蒼
闕天開懸法儼一王之制爰自合宮啓摽
都俞攸存粤若斯干興歌芋寧有在慨畢
宮于禹夏緣茅茨之肇除仰考室于周宣
繇威靈之丕振蓋大聖有作非無事以疲
民而羣情所鍾自率工以興事彼黃龍白
虎徒侈美于遊觀迨飛羽披香曾何關于
政治茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated:
欽名三殿曰皇極、中極、建極，左右樓曰文昭、武成，門曰會極、歸極、弘政、宣治，頒示中外者。
伏以宸宇煇煌，弘規奠萬年鞏固；璇題昭揭，奧義超千古維新。制允斷于睿謨，工實創于帝造。臣民快覩，朝野欣騰。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟明堂日御，垂衣正八表之瞻；蒼闕天開，懸法儼一王之制。爰自合宮啓摽，都俞攸存；粤若斯干興歌，芋寧有在。慨畢宮于禹夏，緣茅茨之肇除；仰考室于周宣，繇威靈之丕振。蓋大聖有作，非無事以疲民；而羣情所鍾，自率工以興事。彼黃龍、白虎，徒侈美于遊觀；迨飛羽、披香，曾何關于政治？茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下
translation_en:
…the three halls were imperially named Huangji, Zhongji, and Jianji; the towers to the left and right, Wenzhao and Wucheng; and the gates, Huiji, Guiji, Hongzheng, and Xuanzhi. These names were promulgated throughout the court and the realm.
We humbly consider that the imperial buildings shine resplendently: their grand design establishes an enduring foundation for ten thousand years. Their splendid name plaques are prominently displayed: their profound meaning surpasses the ages in its renewal. The plan was duly settled by Your sagacious deliberations; the work was indeed initiated by Your imperial undertaking. Officials and people delight to behold it; court and country surge with joy. We, Your servants, rejoice and exult, bowing our heads to the ground and knocking our foreheads upon it.
We humbly reflect that, when the sovereign daily presides in the Hall of Light, he governs with robes hanging still, directing the gaze of all the eight quarters. When the lofty palace gates open toward heaven, the displayed laws lend solemnity to the institutions of a sovereign. From the time when the Hegong palace first established its model [?], the spirit of consultation and assent between ruler and ministers was preserved there. When the song “Si Gan” arose, spaciousness and repose found their place. We contemplate the completion of the palace under Yu of Xia, beginning with the clearing away of thatched structures; we look up to the dedication of the palace under King Xuan of Zhou, which followed the great resurgence of his awe-inspiring authority. When a great sage undertakes construction, it is surely not to weary the people without cause. Rather, where the feelings of all converge, they naturally lead the craftsmen in undertaking the work. Those Huanglong and Baihu palaces merely lavished splendor on places for excursions and sightseeing; as for Feiyu and Pixiang, what connection did they ever have with governance? Now we have the good fortune reverently to encounter Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
御極統
天宅中法
祖秉一敬以慎五事道備冲和
齊八政以厚羣生功成位育
作威作福乾綱正而百度惟貞無黨無偏風
俗同而萬國以理白鹿玄龜符
景既壽域宏開于無疆瑤芝玉兔會
昌辰醇氣蔚蒸于有象屬者
皇穹陰隲顯示革舊之機
===
后德欽承懋建鼎新之業謀及卿士及卜筮人
神胥孚乃召司空召司徒經營聿始雖
聖慈屢戒乎勿亟而人心自悅于忘勞九有貢
珍斂五材而駢萃百靈默佑甫三載以克
成丹壁映朱閣之嶔崟巍然雲起金爵列
玉觚之璀璨美矣星羅樓觀山峙于東西
掖館霞披于左右撫茲偉構本丹書以受
玄符錫厥嘉名因洪範而闡精蘊惟
正殿爲
punctuated: 御極統天，宅中法祖，秉一敬以慎五事，道備冲和；齊八政以厚羣生，功成位育。作威作福，乾綱正而百度惟貞；無黨無偏，風俗同而萬國以理。白鹿玄龜符景既，壽域宏開于無疆；瑤芝玉兔會昌辰，醇氣蔚蒸于有象。屬者，皇穹陰隲，顯示革舊之機；后德欽承，懋建鼎新之業。謀及卿士及卜筮，人神胥孚；乃召司空，召司徒，經營聿始。雖聖慈屢戒乎勿亟，而人心自悅于忘勞。九有貢珍，斂五材而駢萃；百靈默佑，甫三載以克成。丹壁映朱閣之嶔崟，巍然雲起；金爵列玉觚之璀璨，美矣星羅。樓觀山峙于東西，掖館霞披于左右。撫茲偉構，本丹書以受玄符；錫厥嘉名，因洪範而闡精蘊。惟正殿爲
translation_en: …occupies the imperial throne and governs in accord with Heaven, dwells at the center and follows his ancestors. Upholding undivided reverence, he attends carefully to the Five Personal Matters, and his Way fully embodies balanced harmony. Regulating the Eight Affairs of Government to enrich the lives of all, he achieves the proper ordering and nurturing of all things. Dispensing punishments and blessings, he sets imperial authority aright, and every institution is correct. Without faction or partiality, he brings customs into accord, and the myriad states are well governed. White deer and dark tortoises manifest auspicious signs [?], and the realm of longevity opens out without limit; wondrous fungi and jade rabbits appear in this flourishing age, and pure vital energy rises abundantly into visible forms. Recently, august Heaven, through its unseen guidance, clearly revealed an opportunity to replace the old. Your Majesty reverently responded with imperial virtue and vigorously undertook the work of establishing the new. Counsel was sought from high ministers and officers, and through divination by tortoise shell and milfoil; men and spirits alike gave their assent. The Minister of Works and the Minister of Education were then summoned, and planning and construction began. Although Your Majesty’s compassionate concern repeatedly enjoined that there be no haste, the people gladly forgot their toil. The nine regions offered precious materials, and the five kinds of material were gathered in abundance. The hundred spirits silently lent their aid, and the work was completed in just three years. Vermilion walls set off the soaring red pavilions, rising majestically like clouds; golden birds stood in rows beside gleaming jade ornaments, beautifully arrayed like stars. Towers and belvederes rose like mountains to east and west; side halls spread like rosy clouds to left and right. Surveying these magnificent structures, Your Majesty drew upon the Cinnabar Writ to receive Heaven’s mysterious token of favor. In bestowing their fine names, he drew upon the Great Plan to elucidate its profound meaning. As for the principal hall, it serves as…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
正朝之地謂
皇極應
紫極之尊從殿以建以中期祇德以宰物傍扉
乃歸乃會協衆志以遵王文德昭而武功
成弛張之義以立弘其政以宣其治順化
之美斯彰是蓋萃
仁孝明聖之全格
天凝
命盡通變繼述之善知化窮神近以擴居重馭
===
輕之圖遠以爲光前裕後之計臣等慚同
欂櫨叨厠巖廊幸就日於
堯天共仰
九重之渙汗想盛於漢國遥聞四海之懽忻
北極而傾心惟深慶忭寔將擬南山以
獻祝冐罄揄揚伏願
扆徒蔵
昊眷益隆
聖祚彌篤闢四門之耳目
punctuated: 正朝之地，謂皇極，應紫極之尊。從殿以建以中，期祇德以宰物；傍扉乃歸乃會，協衆志以遵王。文德昭而武功成，弛張之義以立；弘其政以宣其治，順化之美斯彰。是蓋萃仁孝明聖之全，格天凝命，盡通變繼述之善，知化窮神。近以擴居重馭輕之圖，遠以爲光前裕後之計。臣等慚同欂櫨，叨厠巖廊，幸就日於堯天，共仰九重之渙汗；想盛於漢國，遥聞四海之懽忻。北極而傾心，惟深慶忭；寔將擬南山以獻祝，冐罄揄揚。伏願扆徒蔵，昊眷益隆，聖祚彌篤，闢四門之耳目。
translation_en:
…the place for formal court audiences, is called Huangji (Imperial Ultimate), corresponding to the exalted position of the Purple Pole. The subsidiary halls embody establishment and centrality [?], with the hope of reverently cultivating virtue to govern all things; the side gates signify returning and assembling, uniting the aspirations of the multitude in allegiance to the sovereign. Civil virtue shines and military achievement is accomplished, establishing the principle of relaxation and exertion. Government is enlarged and orderly rule made manifest, revealing the beauty of obedient transformation. This indeed brings together the full perfection of benevolence, filial piety, discernment, and sageliness, reaching Heaven and securing its mandate. It exhausts the excellence of adapting to change and carrying forward ancestral achievements, comprehending transformation and fathoming the divine. In the near term, it extends the design whereby the weighty center controls the lesser parts; in the long term, it provides for glorifying predecessors and enriching posterity.

We, your servants, feel ashamed to be mere bracket blocks, yet undeservedly occupy places in the lofty court. Fortunate to approach the sun beneath Yao’s sky, we together look up in reverence to the edict issuing from the ninefold palace. Imagining the splendor in the Han realm [?], we hear from afar the rejoicing throughout the Four Seas. Turning our hearts toward the Northern Pole, we feel only profound joy and celebration. We would indeed offer blessings likening your longevity to the Southern Mountain, venturing to pour forth all our praise. We humbly pray: [the phrase 扆徒蔵 is unclear], may Heaven’s favor grow ever greater, may the imperial fortune become ever firmer, and may the eyes and ears at the four gates be opened…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
萬壽日躋乎公堂舞兩階之羽干衆星環拱于
帝座天合高地合厚日合臨月合照
丹扆斂五福之有常民用睦穀用成國用乂家
用康
清禁綿百順于無替臣等無任欣躍屛營之至
謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
===
第叁塲
策
第一問
邢鳳毛
同考試官教諭李　批〔證經典以釋〕
〔聖訓具見淵源之學且敷衍明備而綢守忠歎深規服切忠愛之忱展卷〕
〔藹然溢之〕
考試官教諭張　批〔以大本大旨立意發揮精〕
〔逺詳盡可佳〕
punctuated:
萬壽日躋乎公堂，舞兩階之羽干，衆星環拱于帝座。天合高，地合厚，日合臨，月合照，丹扆斂五福之有常；民用睦，穀用成，國用乂，家用康，清禁綿百順于無替。臣等無任欣躍屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
邢鳳毛

同考試官教諭李批〔證經典以釋〕〔聖訓，具見淵源之學，且敷衍明備，而綢守忠歎深規服切忠愛之忱，展卷〕〔藹然溢之。〕

考試官教諭張批〔以大本大旨立意，發揮精〕〔逺詳盡，可佳。〕
translation_en:
…May your longevity increase daily in the public hall; may the dance with plumes and shields be performed between the two stairways, and may the assembled stars encircle the imperial throne. May Heaven unite its height, Earth its depth, the sun its watchful presence, and the moon its illumination; may the vermilion throne gather the enduring Five Blessings. May the people live in harmony, the grain ripen, the state enjoy order, and families enjoy well-being; may the imperial palace perpetually enjoy every favorable circumstance without decline. We, your servants, cannot contain our utmost joy and reverent awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to convey our congratulations to Your Majesty.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Xing Fengmao

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “He adduces the classics to explain the imperial instructions, fully displaying the depth and grounding of his learning. His exposition is clear and comprehensive. The passage concerning steadfast adherence, loyal counsel, and earnest devotion is garbled [?]. On opening the essay, one finds it overflowing with a warm spirit of loyalty and love for the sovereign.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He bases his argument on the great foundation and principal meaning, developing them with precision, depth, and thoroughness. Commendable.”

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正高　批〔敷陳明切具見忠愛〕
人君之世守鴻業也有保天下之大本而
後可以盡仁孝之實有周天下之大智而
後可以成繼述之功何則天人無二理仁
孝無二道人君之事天也猶乎其事親也
未有不實其心而能悅乎親者則亦未有
不實其心而能格乎天者也其法祖也猶
乎其法天也未有不達乎理而能法乎天
者則亦未有不達乎理而能法乎祖者也
===
故心以誠立則動爲實事而所以祈天求
命者有其本理以智研則事無膠固而所
以嗣大歷服者有其具夫然敬不假于靡
文之飾孝有待夫化裁之妙有不足以保
天下于可久綿世業于無疆也哉竊聞詩
大明有曰明明在下赫赫在上假樂曰不
愆不忘率由舊章斯二者以言乎創守則
均也而君子獨歸之守成蓋首出之君備
歷艱苦則憂勤之心必至固有不待敬而
punctuated:
考試官學正高，批〔敷陳明切，具見忠愛。〕

人君之世守鴻業也，有保天下之大本，而後可以盡仁孝之實；有周天下之大智，而後可以成繼述之功。何則？天人無二理，仁孝無二道。人君之事天也，猶乎其事親也。未有不實其心而能悅乎親者，則亦未有不實其心而能格乎天者也。其法祖也，猶乎其法天也。未有不達乎理而能法乎天者，則亦未有不達乎理而能法乎祖者也。故心以誠立，則動爲實事，而所以祈天求命者有其本；理以智研，則事無膠固，而所以嗣大歷服者有其具。夫然，敬不假于靡文之飾，孝有待夫化裁之妙，有不足以保天下于可久、綿世業于無疆也哉？竊聞《詩·大明》有曰：「明明在下，赫赫在上。」《假樂》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」斯二者，以言乎創守則均也，而君子獨歸之守成。蓋首出之君備歷艱苦，則憂勤之心必至，固有不待敬而
translation_en:
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition is clear and incisive, fully revealing loyalty and devotion.〕

For a ruler to preserve his grand enterprise from generation to generation, he must possess the great foundation for safeguarding All-under-Heaven before he can fully realize benevolence and filial piety. He must possess the great wisdom that comprehends All-under-Heaven before he can accomplish the work of carrying on his predecessors’ purposes and undertakings. Why is this? Heaven and humanity do not have separate principles; benevolence and filial piety do not follow separate ways. A ruler’s service to Heaven is like his service to his parents. No one whose heart lacks sincerity can please his parents; likewise, no one whose heart lacks sincerity can move Heaven. His taking his ancestors as models is like his taking Heaven as his model. No one who fails to comprehend principle can model himself on Heaven; likewise, no one who fails to comprehend principle can model himself on his ancestors.

Thus, when the heart is established through sincerity, every action becomes a substantive deed, and prayers to Heaven for its mandate have their foundation. When principle is investigated through wisdom, affairs are handled without rigidity, and the means of succeeding to the great imperial office are in place. In this way, reverence does not depend on the embellishments of elaborate ceremony, while filial piety requires skillful adaptation to changing circumstances. Could these fail to safeguard All-under-Heaven enduringly and perpetuate the hereditary enterprise without limit?

I have humbly heard these words from “Great Brightness” (Da Ming) in the Book of Odes: “Brightly illustrious below; gloriously radiant above.” “Admirable Joy” (Jia Le) says: “Neither erring nor forgetting, following the established rules.” These two passages apply equally to founding an enterprise and preserving it, yet gentlemen assign them specifically to preserving what has already been accomplished. For a founding ruler has experienced every hardship, and his concern and diligence must therefore be utmost. There are indeed those who, without having to strive for reverence, …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
自無不敬不待法而自我作則者也逆夫
纘緒之主坐享成業則惕厲之念易忽固
必知敬天而後可以格天知法祖而後可
以守祖也稽古夏啓首膺傳子之統而謳
歌訟獄歸焉非不足稱也然當二帝傳賢
之後茅茨之風未遠而菲食之家法猶存
以其所習見而能勿失焉未可以爲難也
商之大甲當處仁遷義之後而四方諸侯
歸焉非不足稱也然方其踐祚之初未聞
===
顧諟之伊訓而允德之不終雖其復歸于
亳而後增脩厥德焉未可以爲有初也至
于有周自后稷肇封千有餘年其豐亨非
一日也成王以禨祿而奉耆定之統其豫
養非有素也然當其廟見之始曰念茲皇
祖曰率時昭考是一念法祖之意旣已皇
皇如不及矣及其旣受羣臣之戒曰日就
月將曰佛時仔肩是一念敬天之忱若猶
以爲未足焉此其在開創猶以爲難而況
punctuated: 自無不敬，不待法而自我作則者也。逆夫纘緒之主，坐享成業，則惕厲之念易忽，固必知敬天而後可以格天，知法祖而後可以守祖也。稽古，夏啓首膺傳子之統，而謳歌訟獄歸焉，非不足稱也。然當二帝傳賢之後，茅茨之風未遠，而菲食之家法猶存，以其所習見而能勿失焉，未可以爲難也。商之大甲當處仁遷義之後，而四方諸侯歸焉，非不足稱也。然方其踐祚之初，未聞顧諟之伊訓，而允德之不終，雖其復歸于亳而後增脩厥德焉，未可以爲有初也。至于有周，自后稷肇封千有餘年，其豐亨非一日也。成王以禨祿而奉耆定之統，其豫養非有素也。然當其廟見之始，曰「念茲皇祖」，曰「率時昭考」，是一念法祖之意，旣已皇皇如不及矣。及其旣受羣臣之戒，曰「日就月將」，曰「佛時仔肩」，是一念敬天之忱，若猶以爲未足焉。此其在開創猶以爲難，而況
translation_en: …they naturally show reverence in everything, and, without awaiting a model to follow, themselves establish the standard. By contrast [?], a ruler who inherits the succession enjoys an accomplished enterprise without effort, and can easily neglect vigilance and caution. He must therefore know how to revere Heaven before he can move Heaven, and how to emulate his ancestors before he can preserve their legacy. Looking back to antiquity, Qi of Xia was the first to inherit rule through transmission from father to son; those singing praises and those seeking judgments in lawsuits alike turned to him. This certainly deserves commendation. Yet he came after the two emperors who had transmitted rule to worthy men: the ethos of thatched dwellings was not yet distant, and the ancestral rule of frugal eating still survived. Merely retaining what he had habitually witnessed cannot be considered difficult. Tai Jia of Shang came after a ruler who dwelt in benevolence and advanced toward righteousness, and the regional lords from all quarters rallied to him. This certainly deserves commendation. Yet when he first ascended the throne, he did not heed the teaching in the Instructions of Yi to keep his gaze fixed upon this [Heaven’s bright mandate], and failed to sustain true virtue. Although he cultivated his virtue further after returning to Bo, he cannot be said to have made a good beginning. As for Zhou, more than a thousand years had passed since Hou Ji first received his fief: its abundance and prosperity had not arisen in a single day. King Cheng, with auspicious fortune [?], took up a firmly established succession, though he had not long been nurtured in preparation for it. Yet at his first appearance in the ancestral temple, he said, “I remember this august grandfather,” and “I follow this illustrious deceased father.” His resolve to emulate his ancestors was already so earnest that he seemed afraid he could not measure up. After receiving the admonitions of his assembled ministers, he said, “Advance daily and progress monthly,” and “Aid me in bearing this burden.” Such was his sincere reverence for Heaven that he seemed still to consider his efforts insufficient. This would have been considered difficult even in founding a dynasty; how much more so…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
于撫巳成之業在長君猶不可必而况于
當富有之年此夏商之所以不可及而首
稱之所以爲無媿也自是以還漢之文帝
玄默恭儉而海內殷富似矣然禮樂則未
遑唐之高宗尊禮大臣而庶幾貞觀似矣
然覆氣則弗戒迄有宋眞宗寬仁慈愛帝
王之量似矣然矯誣上天而祖德亦隳曾
何以望有周之萬一哉肆我
太祖高皇帝受
===
命啓
運混一區宇嘗
諭輔臣曰人心乗氣機出入操存爲難又曰朕
上畏天地兢兢業業不敢自逸于是錄
存心以著敬天而又思所以爲燕詒之訓乃
採歷代諸王善可爲法惡可爲戒者輯爲
嗣君昭鑑錄以教
諸王其所以謹天命而垂典則視古帝王之
用心何異哉我
punctuated:
于撫巳成之業，在長君猶不可必，而况于當富有之年？此夏商之所以不可及，而首稱之所以爲無媿也。自是以還，漢之文帝玄默恭儉，而海內殷富，似矣，然禮樂則未遑；唐之高宗尊禮大臣，而庶幾貞觀，似矣，然覆氣則弗戒；迄有宋眞宗，寬仁慈愛，帝王之量，似矣，然矯誣上天，而祖德亦隳。曾何以望有周之萬一哉？
肆我太祖高皇帝受命啓運，混一區宇，嘗諭輔臣曰：「人心乗氣機出入，操存爲難。」又曰：「朕上畏天地，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」于是錄《存心》以著敬天，而又思所以爲燕詒之訓，乃採歷代諸王善可爲法、惡可爲戒者，輯爲《嗣君昭鑑錄》，以教諸王。其所以謹天命而垂典則，視古帝王之用心何異哉？我
translation_en:
…when preserving an enterprise already established! Even with an adult ruler, this could not be assured; how much less in years of abundant wealth? This is why the Xia and Shang could not match him, and why he deserved to be named foremost. Thereafter, Emperor Wen of the Han was quiet and reserved, reverent and frugal, and the realm was prosperous: he seemed comparable, yet he had no leisure to attend to rites and music. Emperor Gaozong of the Tang honored and treated his great ministers with courtesy and came close to the achievements of the Zhenguan reign: he seemed comparable, yet he failed to guard against “overturning qi” [?]. Then Emperor Zhenzong of the Song was generous, humane, kind, and loving, with the magnanimity of a true sovereign: he seemed comparable, yet he falsely invoked Heaven, and the virtue inherited from his ancestors was also brought to ruin. How could any of them hope to attain even a ten-thousandth of Zhou’s achievement?
Thus our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate, inaugurated the dynasty’s fortune, and unified the realm. He once instructed his assisting ministers: “The human mind comes and goes with the workings of qi; holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult.” He also said: “Above, I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth. Ever vigilant and diligent, I dare not indulge in ease.” He therefore compiled Preserving the Mind to make manifest his reverence for Heaven. Further considering how to provide instruction that would secure the well-being of his descendants, he selected examples from the princes of successive dynasties—good deeds that could serve as models and evil deeds that could serve as warnings—and compiled them into the Record of Clear Mirrors for Succeeding Rulers (Sijun zhaojian lu), with which to instruct the princes. In his reverence for Heaven’s mandate and his transmission of standards and rules, how did his intentions differ from those of the ancient emperors and kings? Our…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝奉
天纘序統御方夏甞自謂天之視聽相爲感通
人心之敬忽有間則天命之去留無常于是
因
存心錄爲
聖學心法而又謂
繼世之君謹守
祖法則
世祚延長乃
===
命儒臣集爲
文華寶鑑以貽世範其所以殷敬畏而裕
後昆視我
太祖之宏規寧有二哉我
列聖相繼握符主鬯上有以順
皇天鑒佑之心遠有以追
二祖德業之盛率是道也暨我
世宗肅皇帝
聖神文武欽明允恭位彌久而道彌隆德愈盛
punctuated:
成祖文皇帝奉天纘序，統御方夏，甞自謂天之視聽，相爲感通；人心之敬忽有間，則天命之去留無常。于是因《存心錄》爲《聖學心法》，而又謂繼世之君謹守祖法，則世祚延長，乃命儒臣集爲《文華寶鑑》，以貽世範。其所以殷敬畏而裕後昆，視我太祖之宏規，寧有二哉？
我列聖相繼握符主鬯，上有以順皇天鑒佑之心，遠有以追二祖德業之盛，率是道也。暨我世宗肅皇帝，聖神文武，欽明允恭，位彌久而道彌隆，德愈盛
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, Chengzu, received Heaven’s mandate and succeeded to the imperial line, ruling over the realm. He once observed that Heaven’s seeing and hearing and those of human beings respond to and communicate with one another; when the human heart wavers between reverence and heedlessness, Heaven’s mandate is inconstant in its departure or continuance. Accordingly, he drew upon the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu) to produce the Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). He further stated that if succeeding rulers scrupulously preserved their ancestors’ laws, the dynasty’s tenure would endure. He therefore commanded his Confucian ministers to compile the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian), to bequeath a model for successive generations. In deepening reverence and awe and providing abundantly for his descendants, how did his purpose differ from the grand designs of our Taizu?
Our successive sage emperors held the imperial insignia and presided over the ancestral sacrifices, thereby honoring above the intent of August Heaven in its watchful protection and emulating across the generations the flourishing virtue and achievements of the two founding ancestors. All followed this way. Coming to our Emperor Su, Shizong: sagely and spiritually perceptive, accomplished in civil and martial affairs, reverent and discerning, truly respectful—the longer he occupied the throne, the loftier his Way became, and the more abundant his virtue…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而化愈光以昭事上帝嘗
諭羣臣有曰知所尊以尊焉凡一言一動以至
于予賞刑罰不敢私一已之欲于是
欽天有頌
敬一有箴凡可以奉天則謹天戒者蓋匪徒託
之空言而已也以繩
祖武則又曰知所親以親焉凡出入語默以及
于民彝物則不敢作纖毫之惡于是
祖德有詩謌
===
陵有述所謂繼序思不忘者眞有一舉足而不
敢儆也至于去
昊天之名恭上
皇天上帝尊號發
皇祖所未發也祀
皇祖于
圜丘宗
皇考于
明堂備
punctuated: 而化愈光。以昭事上帝，嘗諭羣臣有曰：「知所尊以尊焉，凡一言一動，以至于予賞刑罰，不敢私一已之欲。」于是，欽天有頌，敬一有箴。凡可以奉天則、謹天戒者，蓋匪徒託之空言而已也。以繩祖武，則又曰：「知所親以親焉，凡出入語默，以及于民彝物則，不敢作纖毫之惡。」于是，祖德有詩，謌陵有述。所謂繼序思不忘者，眞有一舉足而不敢儆也。至于去昊天之名，恭上皇天上帝尊號，發皇祖所未發也；祀皇祖于圜丘，宗皇考于明堂，備
translation_en: …and his transforming influence grew ever more radiant. In reverently serving the Lord on High, he once instructed his ministers: “Know whom to honor, and honor him. In every word and action, even in granting rewards and imposing punishments, I dare not indulge my own desires.” Thus there was a eulogy on revering Heaven and an admonition on reverently maintaining unity. Whatever served to uphold Heaven’s standards and heed Heaven’s warnings was by no means entrusted merely to empty words. In following his ancestors’ footsteps, he also said: “Know whom to hold dear, and hold them dear. In going out and coming in, speaking and remaining silent, and in all that concerns the constant principles of human relations and the standards governing things, I dare not commit the slightest wrong.” Thus there were poems on ancestral virtue and an account concerning the imperial mausolea [?]. What is meant by “carrying on the succession and never forgetting it” was truly present even in taking a single step, when he dared not be vigilant [?]. As for removing the designation “Vast Heaven” and reverently conferring the exalted title “August Heaven, the Lord on High,” he instituted what his imperial ancestor had not instituted. He offered sacrifice to his imperial ancestor at the Circular Mound and honored his deceased imperial father as the ancestral recipient of sacrifice in the Hall of Light, completing …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
皇祖所未備也有保天下之大本而又有周天
下之大智此其所以度越成周而卓然擅
中興之美豈偶然哉我
皇上聰明
天啓
聖學日新爰自
踐祚以及
今日
經筵每資于啓沃
===
萬幾不憚乎
躬親饗
帝饗
親則務竭乎誠信大政大禮則動求乎
成法禱旱而甘澍時若荷天心之感應不啻速
也因澇而問䘏免稅務損上以益下惠何
渥也若此者成王之訪落陟降無以尚矣
乃者災沴頻疏于四方治效未臻于咸亨
此明問之所由發也然自愚言之古人君
punctuated: 皇祖所未備也。有保天下之大本，而又有周天下之大智，此其所以度越成周，而卓然擅中興之美，豈偶然哉！我皇上聰明天啓，聖學日新。爰自踐祚以及今日，經筵每資于啓沃，萬幾不憚乎躬親。饗帝饗親，則務竭乎誠信；大政大禮，則動求乎成法。禱旱而甘澍時若，荷天心之感應，不啻速也；因澇而問䘏免稅，務損上以益下，惠何渥也！若此者，成王之訪落陟降，無以尚矣。乃者災沴頻疏于四方，治效未臻于咸亨，此明問之所由發也。然自愚言之，古人君
translation_en:
…what the Imperial Ancestor had not fully provided. Possessing the great foundation for preserving All-under-Heaven, together with the great wisdom to care for it in its entirety, he thus surpassed the flourishing Zhou and stood preeminent in the glory of dynastic restoration. Could this have been mere chance?

Our Emperor’s intelligence is Heaven-inspired, and his sagely learning advances daily. From his accession down to the present, he has continually drawn upon the Classics Colloquium for instruction and enlightenment, never shrinking from personally attending to the myriad affairs of government. In offering sacrifices to the Supreme Deity and to his ancestors, he strives to exercise the utmost sincerity and good faith; in great affairs of state and major ceremonies, he invariably seeks established precedents. When he prayed during drought, welcome rain fell in due season: Heaven’s gracious response was swift indeed. In response to flooding, he inquired after and relieved those afflicted and remitted taxes, striving to diminish what those above received in order to benefit those below. How abundant his generosity! Even King Cheng’s seeking counsel at the outset of his reign and his reverent attentiveness, whether ascending or descending, could not surpass such conduct.

Recently, however, calamities and baleful disturbances have repeatedly been reported[?] throughout the realm, and the results of government have yet to attain universal prosperity. This is what prompted your discerning question. Yet, in my humble view, the rulers of antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之保天下者其心嘗自思曰天下者天之
所以子我祖之所以燕翼我者也天之所
以子我則不可不務脩德以爲承藉之地
祖之所以燕翼我則不可不務法守以爲
永保之圖又嘗自思曰保天下之道有情
有文有經有權人而不惟其情惟其文不
惟其權惟其經是膠柱而鼓瑟也故謂燔
柴燎望敬天在是矣而致嚴于圭璧祝史
之間如漢武之泰畤西畤非不虔也而或
===
以爲瀆焉謂不改其道法祖在是矣而不
達乎因陋襲舊之弊如唐睿宗之用斜封
非不述事也而或以爲過焉至于理所當
因則守王季之舊而不爲執理所當革則
攻文王之德而不爲變不然孔子豈以達
孝私一武周哉故君人者有保治之實心
而又有研幾之大智其敬天也非特文之
而已必也昊天曰明而無敢馳驅昊天曰
旦而無敢戲豫天道好生而不殺天道恒
punctuated: 之保天下者，其心嘗自思曰：「天下者，天之所以子我，祖之所以燕翼我者也。天之所以子我，則不可不務脩德，以爲承藉之地；祖之所以燕翼我，則不可不務法守，以爲永保之圖。」又嘗自思曰：「保天下之道，有情有文，有經有權。人而不惟其情，惟其文；不惟其權，惟其經，是膠柱而鼓瑟也。」故謂燔柴燎望，敬天在是矣，而致嚴于圭璧祝史之間，如漢武之泰畤西畤，非不虔也，而或以爲瀆焉。謂不改其道，法祖在是矣，而不達乎因陋襲舊之弊，如唐睿宗之用斜封，非不述事也，而或以爲過焉。至于理所當因，則守王季之舊而不爲執；理所當革，則攻文王之德而不爲變。不然，孔子豈以達孝私一武周哉？故君人者，有保治之實心，而又有研幾之大智。其敬天也，非特文之而已，必也昊天曰明，而無敢馳驅；昊天曰旦，而無敢戲豫。天道好生而不殺，天道恒
translation_en:
…those who preserved All under Heaven would often reflect in their hearts: “All under Heaven is what Heaven has bestowed upon me as its son, and what my ancestors have secured for my peace and protection. Since Heaven has bestowed it upon me as its son, I must devote myself to cultivating virtue, thereby providing a foundation for receiving and sustaining it. Since my ancestors have secured it for my peace and protection, I must devote myself to observing their established institutions, thereby planning for its lasting preservation.” They would also reflect: “The way to preserve All under Heaven has its substance and its forms, its constant principles and its discretionary adaptations. To consider only forms rather than substance, and only constant principles rather than discretionary adaptations, is like gluing the bridges of a zither in place and then playing it.”
Thus, one may say that revering Heaven consists in burning firewood in sacrifice and offering burnt sacrifices toward distant sacred places, and devote scrupulous attention to jade tablets and disks, invocators and scribes. Emperor Wu of Han’s sacrifices at the Tai and Xi altars were certainly devout, yet some regarded them as profanation. One may say that emulating one’s ancestors consists in not changing their ways, yet fail to comprehend the harm of perpetuating defective practices and following obsolete precedents. Emperor Ruizong of Tang’s use of irregular appointments issued in envelopes sealed obliquely certainly continued earlier practice, yet some regarded it as a fault. Where principle requires continuity, preserving Wang Ji’s old ways does not constitute obstinacy; where principle requires reform, ‘attacking King Wen’s virtue’ [?] does not constitute subversion. Otherwise, would Confucius have reserved his praise for universally recognized filial piety exclusively for King Wu and the Duke of Zhou?
Thus, a ruler must have a sincere resolve to preserve good government, together with the great wisdom to discern the first intimations of change. His reverence for Heaven must go beyond outward forms. He must act upon the words ‘Vast Heaven is clear-sighted,’ never daring to rush about unrestrained, and ‘Vast Heaven is luminous,’ never daring to indulge in frivolous pleasures. Heaven’s way cherishes life rather than killing; Heaven’s way is constant…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
久而有常天以大虛爲體而法之爲翕受
天以行健爲用而法之爲自强五材天所
生也制爲取用之節四氣天所序也律爲
時措之宜因福善以親賢懲禍淫以遠姦
發號施令罔有不臧一天之風霆雨露各
當其可也左右前後罔匪正人一天之衆
星旋繞罔不順軌也自深宮大內以至接
禮賢士大夫之際儼乎大祭之是承由嚮
晦宴息以至禮樂刑政之大昭乎上帝之
===
臨汝夫然則一敬達于上下而天人一致
所謂下有明明之德斯上有赫赫之命在
我矣有不足以安天下乎其法祖也非特
守之而已必也祖考以憂勤開基而不遑
暇逸祖考以敬義憲天而邁種厥德祖有
功而繼序其功焉宗有德而作求其德焉
心法可考用之爲直內之方身法可鑒資
之爲飭躬之準納諫咈咈祖德之含己也
而法之爲虛己望道未見祖德之謙己也
punctuated:
久而有常。天以大虛爲體，而法之爲翕受；天以行健爲用，而法之爲自强。五材，天所生也，制爲取用之節；四氣，天所序也，律爲時措之宜。因福善以親賢，懲禍淫以遠姦。發號施令，罔有不臧，一天之風霆雨露各當其可也；左右前後，罔匪正人，一天之衆星旋繞罔不順軌也。自深宮大內，以至接禮賢士大夫之際，儼乎大祭之是承；由嚮晦宴息，以至禮樂刑政之大，昭乎上帝之臨汝。夫然，則一敬達于上下，而天人一致。所謂下有明明之德，斯上有赫赫之命，在我矣。有不足以安天下乎？
其法祖也，非特守之而已。必也祖考以憂勤開基，而不遑暇逸；祖考以敬義憲天，而邁種厥德。祖有功，而繼序其功焉；宗有德，而作求其德焉。心法可考，用之爲直內之方；身法可鑒，資之爲飭躬之準。納諫咈咈，祖德之含己也，而法之爲虛己；望道未見，祖德之謙己也。
translation_en:
…enduring and constant. Heaven takes the great void as its substance; the ruler models himself on this through all-embracing receptiveness. Heaven takes vigorous movement as its operation; he models himself on this through self-strengthening. The five materials are produced by Heaven: he establishes limits on their acquisition and use. The energies of the four seasons are ordered by Heaven: he regulates his actions to suit their proper times. Following Heaven’s blessing of the good, he draws close to the worthy; heeding its punishment of the wicked, he keeps the treacherous at a distance. In issuing commands and promulgating orders, nothing is other than good—just as Heaven’s winds, thunder, rain, and dew each occur as is fitting. Those to his left and right, before and behind him, are all upright men—just as Heaven’s multitude of stars revolve without departing from their courses. From his life deep within the palace to his reception and courteous treatment of worthy scholar-officials, he is solemn, as though conducting a great sacrifice. From resting as darkness falls to the great affairs of ritual, music, punishments, and government, he is keenly conscious that the Lord on High watches over him. Thus, a single reverence reaches above and below, and Heaven and humanity are at one. What is meant by saying, “When there is manifest virtue below, there is a glorious mandate above,” is then realized in oneself. Could this fail to bring peace to all under Heaven?
His emulation of his ancestors likewise consists of more than merely preserving their legacy. Since his forebears founded their enterprise through anxious diligence, he must allow himself no leisure or ease. Since his forebears took Heaven as their model through reverence and righteousness, he must vigorously cultivate their virtue. Where the founding ancestor achieved merit, he continues that achievement; where succeeding ancestors possessed virtue, he seeks to realize that virtue. Their methods of cultivating the mind can be examined: he employs them as a means of making himself upright within. Their methods of personal conduct offer a mirror: he draws on them as a standard for disciplining himself. Accepting remonstrance, even when it is insistently contrary [?], expresses the ancestral virtue of self-restraint [?]; he models himself on this by setting aside his own conceit. Looking toward the Way as though he had not yet perceived it expresses the ancestral virtue of humility…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而法之以戒盈以其所以應天者而祈乎
天以其所以順人者而安乎人敬以事神
和以接物一肅肅雍雍之遺也不狃近利
惟懷永圖一不泄不忘之舊也自食息起
居以至于恭已南面之上非先王之法行
不敢行自燕對近習以至于顧問大廷之
際非先王之法言不敢言夫然則一道揆
于先後而祖孫同德所謂作室而肯堂墍
播而肯穫在我矣有不足以綿世業乎夫
===
仁以事天則詒謀不孤而事親之孝以得
孝以事親則成命可凝而事天之仁以盡
善乎宋臣司馬光曰人君若不畏天則何
事不可為羅從彥曰祖宗德澤不可恃法
度不可廢可謂深得守成之道矣彼有謬
為天變不足畏祖宗不足法如安石者豈
非天下后世逢君之罪人哉方今
聖天子勵精于其上而又有賢宰執篤棐于其
下所以翊成
punctuated:
而法之以戒盈，以其所以應天者而祈乎天，以其所以順人者而安乎人。敬以事神，和以接物，一肅肅雍雍之遺也；不狃近利，惟懷永圖，一不泄不忘之舊也。自食息起居，以至于恭已南面之上，非先王之法行不敢行；自燕對近習，以至于顧問大廷之際，非先王之法言不敢言。夫然則一道揆于先後，而祖孫同德，所謂作室而肯堂、墍播而肯穫，在我矣，有不足以綿世業乎？夫仁以事天，則詒謀不孤，而事親之孝以得；孝以事親，則成命可凝，而事天之仁以盡。
善乎宋臣司馬光曰：「人君若不畏天，則何事不可為？」羅從彥曰：「祖宗德澤不可恃，法度不可廢。」可謂深得守成之道矣。彼有謬為天變不足畏、祖宗不足法，如安石者，豈非天下后世逢君之罪人哉？方今聖天子勵精于其上，而又有賢宰執篤棐于其下，所以翊成
translation_en:
…and emulate this to guard against complacency. Pray to Heaven by the very means through which the ancestors responded to Heaven; bring peace to the people by the very means through which they accorded with the people. Serve the spirits with reverence and engage with others harmoniously: all this is the legacy of their solemnity and concord. Do not become attached to immediate gains, but cherish enduring plans: all this continues their tradition of neither slackening nor forgetting. From eating, resting, and daily activities to sitting reverently upon the south-facing throne, dare perform no deed other than the exemplary deeds of the former kings. From informal audiences with intimate attendants to consultations in the great court, dare utter no words other than the exemplary words of the former kings. Thus one standard of the Way unites predecessors and successors, and ancestors and descendants share the same virtue. What is meant by willingly building the hall when a house has been planned, and willingly reaping what has been sown [?], then rests with me. Could this be insufficient to perpetuate the hereditary enterprise? For if one serves Heaven with benevolence, the plans bequeathed to posterity will not go unsupported, and filial devotion in serving one’s parents will thereby be attained. If one serves one’s parents with filial devotion, the established mandate can be secured, and benevolence in serving Heaven will thereby be fully realized.
Well did the Song minister Sima Guang say: “If a ruler does not fear Heaven, what deed would he be unwilling to commit?” Luo Congyan said: “The virtue and beneficence of the ancestors cannot be relied upon; their laws and institutions must not be abandoned.” They may indeed be said to have profoundly understood the way to preserve an inherited achievement. As for those like Anshi who falsely maintain that Heaven’s anomalies need not be feared and the ancestors need not be emulated, are they not culpable before all under Heaven and later generations for pandering to their rulers? At present, our sagely Son of Heaven devotes his energies to government above, while worthy chief councillors give him steadfast assistance below, thereby helping to accomplish…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
一代光明俊偉之業端有在矣雖然頌成王
者言周公之功不衰此又賢宰執今日之
事也於愚生何有哉
第二問
文在中
同考試官教諭栗　批　圖書理數原非淺學所能測識
篇中探溯本原究析同異且推極天人合一之妙聖神功化之全真
所謂獨觀其深者可以徵夙蘊矣錄之
考試官教諭張　批　闡發理數之學洞悉無遺可謂
潛心有素者
考試官學正高　批　理數微□作者多所未悉獨子
得之
===
造化有一定之體聖人因數以察理而天
地之秘以彰造化有自然之用聖人顯道
以祐神而天地之化以成夫天下之物天
下之數為之也天下之數天下之理主之
也理隱於無形而其朕莫測數呈於有象
而其幾未著聖人不得已而本其數以見
punctuated:
一代光明俊偉之業，端有在矣。雖然，頌成王者言周公之功不衰，此又賢宰執今日之事也，於愚生何有哉？

第二問
文在中

同考試官教諭栗，批：圖書理數，原非淺學所能測識。篇中探溯本原，究析同異，且推極天人合一之妙、聖神功化之全，真所謂獨觀其深者，可以徵夙蘊矣。錄之。

考試官教諭張，批：闡發理數之學，洞悉無遺，可謂潛心有素者。

考試官學正高，批：理數微□，作者多所未悉，獨子得之。

造化有一定之體，聖人因數以察理，而天地之秘以彰；造化有自然之用，聖人顯道以祐神，而天地之化以成。夫天下之物，天下之數為之也；天下之數，天下之理主之也。理隱於無形，而其朕莫測；數呈於有象，而其幾未著。聖人不得已而本其數以見
translation_en:
…the radiant and magnificent achievements of a dynasty indeed have their foundation in this. Nevertheless, those who praise King Cheng speak of the enduring accomplishments of the Duke of Zhou. This, too, is the responsibility of our worthy chief councillors today. What part could an ignorant student such as I have in it?

Second Question
Wen Zaizhong

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: The principles and numbers of the River Chart and Luo Writing are certainly beyond the understanding of those of shallow learning. This essay traces their origins and thoroughly analyzes their similarities and differences. It further explores to the utmost the subtlety of the unity of Heaven and humanity and the completeness of the transformative achievements of the sagely and divine. Its author truly merits the description of one who alone perceives their depths; this attests to his long-cultivated learning. Selected for inclusion.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: He elucidates the study of principles and numbers with thorough insight, leaving nothing unexplored. He may indeed be called one who has long devoted himself to this study.

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: The subtleties of principles and numbers [?] are in many respects imperfectly understood by other writers; you alone have grasped them.

The creative transformations of the cosmos have a fixed underlying structure. The sages examine principles through numbers, thereby revealing the secrets of Heaven and Earth. These transformations have a spontaneous operation. The sages make the Way manifest to assist the spiritual powers, thereby bringing the transformations of Heaven and Earth to completion. All things under Heaven are formed by the numbers of the world; the numbers of the world are governed by its principles. Principles lie concealed in the formless, and their traces cannot be fathomed; numbers appear in visible configurations, yet their incipient workings are not manifest. The sages therefore have no choice but to take these numbers as their basis in order to discern…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道體之全推其義以盡裁成之妙此天地
聖人相待以成而後天地有全能聖人有
全功矣請因明問而敬陳之夫道何爲而
始也由天地而始也道何爲而終也由聖
人而終也易大傳曰河出圖洛出書聖人
則之蓋昔者庖犧氏之繼天而王也有龍
馬負圖出于河其文一六居北二七居南
三八居東四九居西五十居中本天地自
然生成之數也伏犧于其一三五七九而
===
識其爲奇也陽也天道也于其二四六八
十而識其爲耦也陰也地道也于是則之
以畫卦陰陽錯綜而乾兌離震巽坎艮坤
立焉此天地之化育所由肇也大禹之治
水功成也有神龜載書出于洛其文戴九
履一左三右七二四爲肩六八爲足本天
地自然貞勝之數也大禹于其一三五七
九而識其爲奇贏也陽當有餘也人所宜
扶也于其二四六八而識其爲耦乏也陰
punctuated: 道體之全，推其義以盡裁成之妙，此天地、聖人相待以成，而後天地有全能，聖人有全功矣。請因明問而敬陳之。夫道何爲而始也？由天地而始也。道何爲而終也？由聖人而終也。《易大傳》曰：「河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」蓋昔者庖犧氏之繼天而王也，有龍馬負圖出于河，其文一六居北，二七居南，三八居東，四九居西，五十居中，本天地自然生成之數也。伏犧于其一三五七九而識其爲奇也，陽也，天道也；于其二四六八十而識其爲耦也，陰也，地道也。于是則之以畫卦，陰陽錯綜，而乾、兌、離、震、巽、坎、艮、坤立焉，此天地之化育所由肇也。大禹之治水功成也，有神龜載書出于洛，其文戴九履一，左三右七，二四爲肩，六八爲足，本天地自然貞勝之數也。大禹于其一三五七九而識其爲奇贏也，陽當有餘也，人所宜扶也；于其二四六八而識其爲耦乏也，陰
translation_en:
…the substance of the Way in its entirety, and extend its principles to exhaust the subtle art of regulating and completing creation. Heaven and Earth and the sage thus depend upon one another for fulfillment; only then do Heaven and Earth exercise their full capacity and the sage achieve his full accomplishment. Allow me respectfully to set this forth in response to your illuminating question. Where does the Way begin? It begins with Heaven and Earth. Where does the Way reach its consummation? It reaches its consummation through the sage. The Great Commentary on the Book of Changes says: “The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as models.”

In ancient times, when Paoxi (Fuxi) succeeded Heaven as king, a dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River bearing a chart. In its markings, one and six occupied the north, two and seven the south, three and eight the east, four and nine the west, and five and ten the center. These were the natural numbers through which Heaven and Earth generate and complete things. In its one, three, five, seven, and nine, Fuxi recognized the odd numbers, yang, and the Way of Heaven; in its two, four, six, eight, and ten, he recognized the even numbers, yin, and the Way of Earth. He therefore took it as his model in drawing the trigrams. Through the interweaving of yin and yang, Qian, Dui, Li, Zhen, Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun were established. This was how the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth was initiated.

When Yu the Great completed his work of controlling the floods, a divine tortoise emerged from the Luo River bearing the Writing. Its markings bore nine above and one below, three on the left and seven on the right, two and four as shoulders, and six and eight as feet. These were the natural numbers through which Heaven and Earth prevail in constant alternation. In its one, three, five, seven, and nine, Yu the Great recognized that the odd numbers were in surplus: yang should have abundance, and people ought to support it. In its two, four, six, and eight, he recognized that the even numbers were deficient: yin…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當不足也人所宜抑也于是則之以第疇
因天責人而五行五事八政五紀皇極三
德稽疑庶徵福極陳焉此天地之化育所
由成也夫圖本無卦也而卦之理已寓書
本無疇也而疇之理已存伏犧則圖以畫
卦大禹則書以敘疇孔安國劉向父子非
無見也苟謂圖以龍馬而制則龍馬所載
爲何圖書以洛龜而成則洛龜所負爲何
象無乃以易言伏犧仰觀俯察以畫卦不
===
言龍馬而因以例書乎然安知龍馬非俯
察之一事也河圖呈于伏犧而十以闡其
全體洛書錫于神禹而九以著其大用闡
子明邵堯夫諸人未爲無見也苟謂以九
爲河圖則洩其秘于先者何以不舉其全
以十爲洛書則闡其用于後者何以反益
以十無乃以圖書互藏其用而託言于陳
希夷以爲二者皆出于伏犧乎然不知圖
書數各有定而理有攸當也要之圖書殊
punctuated: 當不足也，人所宜抑也。于是則之以第疇，因天責人，而五行、五事、八政、五紀、皇極、三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極陳焉。此天地之化育所由成也。夫圖本無卦也，而卦之理已寓；書本無疇也，而疇之理已存。伏犧則圖以畫卦，大禹則書以敘疇，孔安國、劉向父子非無見也。苟謂圖以龍馬而制，則龍馬所載爲何圖？書以洛龜而成，則洛龜所負爲何象？無乃以《易》言伏犧仰觀俯察以畫卦，不言龍馬，而因以例書乎？然安知龍馬非俯察之一事也？河圖呈于伏犧，而十以闡其全體；洛書錫于神禹，而九以著其大用。闡子明、邵堯夫諸人未爲無見也。苟謂以九爲河圖，則洩其秘于先者何以不舉其全？以十爲洛書，則闡其用于後者何以反益以十？無乃以圖書互藏其用，而託言于陳希夷，以爲二者皆出于伏犧乎？然不知圖書數各有定，而理有攸當也。要之，圖書殊
translation_en:
…ought to be deficient and ought to be restrained by human beings. Accordingly, he took this as his model in ordering the categories, holding human beings accountable according to Heaven. Thus were set forth the Five Agents, the Five Personal Activities, the Eight Affairs of Government, the Five Regulators of Time, the August Ultimate, the Three Virtues, the Examination of Doubts, the Various Signs, and Blessings and Calamities. Through these, the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth was brought to completion.

Now, the River Chart originally contained no trigrams, yet their principles were already implicit within it; the Luo Writing originally contained no categories, yet their principles were already present within it. Fuxi took the Chart as his model in drawing the trigrams; Yu the Great took the Writing as his model in arranging the categories. Kong Anguo and Liu Xiang and his son were not without insight in this matter. If one claims that the Chart was fashioned on the basis of the dragon-horse, then what chart was it that the dragon-horse carried? If the Writing was composed on the basis of the Luo turtle, then what image was it that the Luo turtle bore? Could it be that, because the Book of Changes says that Fuxi looked upward and examined things below in order to draw the trigrams, but does not mention the dragon-horse, one has applied the same reasoning to the Writing? Yet how can one know that the dragon-horse was not among the things he examined below?

The River Chart was presented to Fuxi, and through ten it disclosed its complete structure; the Luo Writing was bestowed upon the divine Yu, and through nine it manifested its great functioning. Chan Ziming [?], Shao Yaofu, and the others were not without insight. If one claims that the arrangement of nine is the River Chart, why did that which first disclosed the mystery not present it in its entirety? If the arrangement of ten is the Luo Writing, why did that which subsequently revealed its functioning instead add to it, bringing it to ten? Could it be that, because the Chart and the Writing each contain the other's functioning, one has attributed a statement to Chen Xiyi asserting that both originated with Fuxi? Yet this fails to recognize that the Chart and the Writing each have their own fixed numbers, and that their principles have their appropriate correspondences. In sum, the Chart and the Writing differ…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時而列數其象不能以不異圖書本數以
載理其究不能以不同故自其異者而觀
之河圖天數五地數五一陰一陽之道也
積之則天數二十五地數三十而五十有
五具焉天地之常陽不足而陰有餘也洛
書天數五地數四陽以統陰之義也積之
則天數二十五地數二十而四十有五具
焉天地之變陰宜消而陽宜長也河圖以
五生數統五成數同處其位陰陽合而後
===
生道備獨陽不生獨陰不成也洛書以五
奇數統四耦數而各處其方陰陽錯雜而
後有制陽得以兼陰陰不得以兼陽也河
圖運行之序始東次南次中次西次北左
旋一周而復起于東木火土金水生生之
本然也此兩儀四象八卦而六十四而四
千九十六萬事萬物之所從出也故曰天
地之大德曰生洛書推行之序始北次西
南次東次中次西北次西次東北
punctuated: 時而列數，其象不能以不異；圖書本數以載理，其究不能以不同。故自其異者而觀之，河圖天數五，地數五，一陰一陽之道也。積之則天數二十五，地數三十，而五十有五具焉。天地之常，陽不足而陰有餘也。洛書天數五，地數四，陽以統陰之義也。積之則天數二十五，地數二十，而四十有五具焉。天地之變，陰宜消而陽宜長也。河圖以五生數統五成數，同處其位，陰陽合而後生道備，獨陽不生，獨陰不成也。洛書以五奇數統四耦數，而各處其方，陰陽錯雜而後有制，陽得以兼陰，陰不得以兼陽也。河圖運行之序，始東，次南，次中，次西，次北，左旋一周而復起于東，木火土金水生生之本然也。此兩儀、四象、八卦，而六十四，而四千九十六，萬事萬物之所從出也。故曰：「天地之大德曰生。」洛書推行之序，始北，次西南，次東，次中，次西北，次西，次東北
translation_en: …at different times and array their numbers, so their configurations necessarily differ; the River Chart (Hetu) and Luo Writing (Luoshu) use numbers as the basis for conveying principle, so their ultimate purport necessarily coincides. Thus, viewed in terms of their differences, the River Chart has five heavenly numbers and five earthly numbers: this is the Way of alternating yin and yang. Added together, the heavenly numbers total twenty-five and the earthly numbers thirty, making fifty-five in all. This is the constant condition of Heaven and Earth: yang is deficient and yin has a surplus. The Luo Writing has five heavenly numbers and four earthly numbers: this expresses the principle of yang governing yin. Added together, the heavenly numbers total twenty-five and the earthly numbers twenty, making forty-five in all. This is the transformation of Heaven and Earth: yin ought to diminish and yang ought to grow. In the River Chart, the five generating numbers govern the five completing numbers, sharing their respective positions. Only after yin and yang unite is the way of generation complete: yang alone cannot generate, and yin alone cannot bring to completion. In the Luo Writing, the five odd numbers govern the four even numbers, each occupying its own direction. Only after yin and yang intermingle is there regulation: yang may encompass yin, but yin may not encompass yang. The River Chart’s sequence of circulation begins in the east, proceeds to the south, then the center, then the west, then the north; turning left through a complete circuit, it begins again in the east. This is the inherent order of the ceaseless generation of wood, fire, earth, metal, and water. From this come the Two Modes, the Four Images, the Eight Trigrams, then the sixty-four hexagrams, then the four thousand and ninety-six combinations: it is the source from which the myriad affairs and things emerge. Thus it is said: “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation.” The Luo Writing’s sequence of progression begins in the north, proceeds to the southwest, then the east, then the center, then the northwest, then the west, then the northeast…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
右旋一周而復究于南水火金木土相制
之妙用也比一消一長一闔一闢一進一
退四時日月所以相禪于無窮也故曰無
易則乾坤幾乎息矣河圖以六七八九附
于生數之外以盡陰陽進退饒乏之正而
其九者生于一三五之積六者生于二四
之積七者九之自西而南八者六之自北
而東蓋至是而陰陽老少互藏之變備矣
洛書以七八六九縱橫十五以盡陰陽消
===
長之理而其虛五分十則以一含九以二
含八以三含七以四含六蓋至是而陰陽
參伍錯綜之妙舉矣是固圖書之所以異
也而異者未始不同自其同者而觀之河
圖之一二三四各奠其方而常居內六七
八九各以其類而附于外是以內者爲主
而外爲客也洛書之一三七九各本其氣
而正其位二四六八各從其合而附于側
是以正者爲主而側爲客也此圖之未始
punctuated:
右旋一周而復究于南，水火金木土相制之妙用也。比一消一長，一闔一闢，一進一退，四時日月所以相禪于無窮也。故曰：「無易則乾坤幾乎息矣。」河圖以六七八九附于生數之外，以盡陰陽進退饒乏之正。而其九者，生于一三五之積；六者，生于二四之積；七者，九之自西而南；八者，六之自北而東。蓋至是而陰陽老少互藏之變備矣。洛書以七八六九縱橫十五，以盡陰陽消長之理。而其虛五分十，則以一含九，以二含八，以三含七，以四含六。蓋至是而陰陽參伍錯綜之妙舉矣。
是固圖書之所以異也，而異者未始不同。自其同者而觀之，河圖之一二三四，各奠其方而常居內；六七八九，各以其類而附于外。是以內者爲主，而外爲客也。洛書之一三七九，各本其氣而正其位；二四六八，各從其合而附于側。是以正者爲主，而側爲客也。此圖之未始
translation_en:
…turning right through one circuit and again reaching the south: this is the wondrous operation by which water, fire, metal, wood, and earth restrain one another. This [?] alternation of waning and waxing, closing and opening, advancing and retreating is how the four seasons, sun, and moon succeed one another without end. Thus it is said: “Without change, Qian and Kun would almost cease to operate.” The Yellow River Diagram (Hetu) places six, seven, eight, and nine outside the generating numbers, fully expressing the regular patterns of yin and yang in advancing and retreating, abundance and deficiency. Its nine arises from the sum of one, three, and five; six arises from the sum of two and four. Seven is nine moving from west to south; eight is six moving from north to east. At this point, the transformations through which old and young yin and yang contain one another are fully represented. The Luo River Writing (Luoshu) arranges seven, eight, six, and nine so that the vertical and horizontal totals are fifteen, fully expressing the principles of yin and yang waxing and waning. Leaving five out of account and dividing ten, it has one contain nine, two contain eight, three contain seven, and four contain six. At this point, the subtleties of the interweaving and recombination of yin and yang are fully displayed.
These are indeed the respects in which the Diagram and the Writing differ; yet what differs is never without common ground. Viewed in terms of what they share, the one, two, three, and four of the Yellow River Diagram each occupy their appointed direction and always lie within, while six, seven, eight, and nine are attached outside, each according to its kind. Thus those within are hosts, and those outside are guests. The one, three, seven, and nine of the Luo River Writing each take their proper position according to their vital force, while two, four, six, and eight are attached at the sides, each following its pairing. Thus those in the principal positions are hosts, and those at the sides are guests. This shows that the Diagram has never…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不抑陰而書之未始不尊陽也河圖之以
五居中也五生數之象實在焉下則天一
之象也上則地二之象也左則天三之象
也右則地四之象也中則天五之象也洛
書之以五居中也五奇數之象實在焉下
亦天一之象也左亦天三之象也中亦天
五之象也右亦天七之象也上則天九之
象也此圖之虛中而太極以立卽書之虛
中而五氣以萃也圖之一六同宗而位乎
===
北二七爲朋而位乎南三八同道而位乎
東四九爲友而位乎西五十相守而位乎
中生成五位之相得也其五獨居中而分
十者則外陰之義耳書之一正乎北而六
從之七正乎西而二附之三正乎東而八
隨之九正乎南而四因之是奇耦之各有
合也其五獨正乎中而黜十者則滅陰之
義耳此圖之生成未始不爲書之奇耦書
之正側未始不爲圖之內外也圖之虛五
punctuated: 不抑陰，而書之未始不尊陽也。河圖之以五居中也，五生數之象實在焉：下則天一之象也，上則地二之象也，左則天三之象也，右則地四之象也，中則天五之象也。洛書之以五居中也，五奇數之象實在焉：下亦天一之象也，左亦天三之象也，中亦天五之象也，右亦天七之象也，上則天九之象也。此圖之虛中而太極以立，卽書之虛中而五氣以萃也。圖之一六同宗而位乎北，二七爲朋而位乎南，三八同道而位乎東，四九爲友而位乎西，五十相守而位乎中，生成五位之相得也。其五獨居中而分十者，則外陰之義耳。書之一正乎北而六從之，七正乎西而二附之，三正乎東而八隨之，九正乎南而四因之，是奇耦之各有合也。其五獨正乎中而黜十者，則滅陰之義耳。此圖之生成未始不爲書之奇耦，書之正側未始不爲圖之內外也。圖之虛五
translation_en:
…never fails to restrain yin, while the Luo Writing never fails to honor yang. In the River Chart (Hetu), five occupies the center, and the configurations of the five generating numbers are indeed present: below is the configuration of Heaven’s one; above, Earth’s two; to the left, Heaven’s three; to the right, Earth’s four; and in the center, Heaven’s five. In the Luo Writing (Luoshu), five occupies the center, and the configurations of the five odd numbers are indeed present: below, likewise, is the configuration of Heaven’s one; to the left, Heaven’s three; in the center, Heaven’s five; to the right, Heaven’s seven; and above, Heaven’s nine. Thus, the Chart’s leaving the center empty so that the Supreme Ultimate is established is precisely the Writing’s leaving the center empty so that the five vital energies gather there.

In the Chart, one and six share a common lineage and occupy the north; two and seven are companions and occupy the south; three and eight follow the same way and occupy the east; four and nine are friends and occupy the west; five and ten keep together and occupy the center. These are the generating and completing numbers matching one another in the five positions. That five alone occupies the center while ten is divided expresses merely the principle of placing yin outside. In the Writing, one holds the principal position in the north and six follows it; seven holds the principal position in the west and two attaches itself to it; three holds the principal position in the east and eight follows it; nine holds the principal position in the south and four associates with it. Thus, the odd and even numbers each have their partners. That five alone holds the principal position in the center while ten is excluded expresses merely the principle of eliminating yin. Thus, the Chart’s generating and completing numbers are invariably the Writing’s odd and even numbers, while the Writing’s principal and lateral positions are invariably the Chart’s inner and outer positions. The Chart’s leaving five vacant…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
與十者太極也奇數二十耦數二十者兩
儀也以一二三四合六七八九者四象也
析四方之合以爲乾坤坎離補四隅之缺
以爲兌震巽艮者八卦也義固有所在矣
而書之虛五其中者是亦太極也奇偶各
居二十者兩儀也一二三四五合六七八
九縱横十五爲七八九六者四象也以四
方之正爲乾坤離坎以四隅之偏爲兌震
巽艮者亦八卦也是圖之體未始不含書
===
之用而書之用未始不具圖之體也此固
圖書之所以同也而同者不能以無殊易
曰顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同
憂天道也河圖之所由出也裁成天地之
道輔相天地之宜以左右民人道也此洛
書之所以爲有憂也後之儒者有見于其
同則謂圖書皆出于伏犠有見于其異則
謂洪範不由于洛書他如楊雄之太玄關
朗之洞極司馬之潛虛延壽之訓詁京房
punctuated: 與十者，太極也；奇數二十、耦數二十者，兩儀也；以一二三四合六七八九者，四象也；析四方之合以爲乾坤坎離，補四隅之缺以爲兌震巽艮者，八卦也。義固有所在矣。而書之虛五其中者，是亦太極也；奇偶各居二十者，兩儀也；一二三四五合六七八九，縱横十五，爲七八九六者，四象也；以四方之正爲乾坤離坎，以四隅之偏爲兌震巽艮者，亦八卦也。是圖之體未始不含書之用，而書之用未始不具圖之體也。此固圖書之所以同也，而同者不能以無殊。《易》曰：「顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」天道也，河圖之所由出也。「裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民」，人道也，此洛書之所以爲有憂也。後之儒者，有見于其同，則謂圖書皆出于伏犠；有見于其異，則謂洪範不由于洛書。他如楊雄之太玄、關朗之洞極、司馬之潛虛、延壽之訓詁、京房
translation_en: …and ten left vacant constitute the Supreme Ultimate. The odd numbers totaling twenty and the even numbers totaling twenty constitute the Two Modes. Pairing one, two, three, and four with six, seven, eight, and nine constitutes the Four Images. Separating the combinations at the four cardinal positions to form Qian, Kun, Kan, and Li, and filling the gaps at the four corners to form Dui, Zhen, Xun, and Gen, constitutes the Eight Trigrams. These arrangements certainly have their underlying significance. In the Writing, leaving the central five vacant likewise constitutes the Supreme Ultimate. The odd and even numbers each totaling twenty constitute the Two Modes. Combining one, two, three, four, and five with six, seven, eight, and nine, with vertical and horizontal totals of fifteen, to produce seven, eight, nine, and six constitutes the Four Images [?]. Taking the cardinal positions as Qian, Kun, Li, and Kan, and the oblique positions at the four corners as Dui, Zhen, Xun, and Gen, likewise constitutes the Eight Trigrams. Thus the substance of the Diagram always contains the function of the Writing, while the function of the Writing always possesses the substance of the Diagram. This is indeed what makes the Diagram and the Writing alike; yet their likeness cannot mean that they have no differences. The Book of Changes says: “It manifests itself in benevolence and conceals itself in its workings; it sets the myriad things in motion without sharing the sage’s cares.” This is the Way of Heaven, from which the River Diagram emerges. “To shape and complete the Way of Heaven and Earth, to assist what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby to guide the people”—this is the human Way, and this is why the Luo Writing involves care. Later Confucian scholars, perceiving their likeness, asserted that both the Diagram and the Writing originated with Fuxi; perceiving their differences, they asserted that the Great Plan did not derive from the Luo Writing. Other examples include Yang Xiong’s Supreme Mystery, Guan Lang’s Penetrating the Ultimate, Sima’s Hidden Void, Yanshou’s textual glosses, and Jing Fang’s…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之氣數王弼之理致皆穿鑿附會而造化
自然之功用始紛然不可窮矣大抵理一
而已有天地之造化有聖人之造化天地
之造化鬼神生成之本也聖人之造化酬
酢有相之道也不觀天地之化則無以見
聖人之道有所本不觀聖人之道則無以
見天地之化有所終故天無二日民無二
王陰晴治亂君子小人多寡之不齊者天
地之常也聖人以其常而通其變撥亂而
反之正尊君卑臣進君子退小人內中國
外夷狄所以扶陽抑陰賛天地之化育也
是故明此而帝堯舜之所以闢洪荒奠來
賴去四兇進元凱則治統立而道統以正
明此而師則周孔之所以象易繫辭擴天
理戒人欲因河圖之體本洛書之義則道
統明而治統以彰蓋天地以無心而成化
聖人雖有心而無爲無爲者非一無所爲
也盡人以合天也至于盡人以合天則亦
punctuated: 之氣數、王弼之理致，皆穿鑿附會，而造化自然之功用始紛然不可窮矣。大抵理一而已，有天地之造化，有聖人之造化。天地之造化，鬼神生成之本也；聖人之造化，酬酢有相之道也。不觀天地之化，則無以見聖人之道有所本；不觀聖人之道，則無以見天地之化有所終。故天無二日，民無二王。陰晴治亂，君子小人多寡之不齊者，天地之常也。聖人以其常而通其變，撥亂而反之正，尊君卑臣，進君子退小人，內中國外夷狄，所以扶陽抑陰，賛天地之化育也。是故明此而帝，堯舜之所以闢洪荒、奠來賴、去四兇、進元凱，則治統立而道統以正；明此而師，則周孔之所以象易繫辭、擴天理、戒人欲、因河圖之體、本洛書之義，則道統明而治統以彰。蓋天地以無心而成化，聖人雖有心而無爲。無爲者，非一無所爲也，盡人以合天也。至于盡人以合天，則亦
translation_en:
…the configurations of qi and numerical cycles of Jing Fang, and the principles and purport expounded by Wang Bi—all are strained interpretations and forced associations. Thus the spontaneous workings of creation and transformation become bewilderingly tangled and impossible to fathom exhaustively. In general, principle is one and nothing more; yet there is the creative transformation of Heaven and Earth, and there is the creative transformation of the sages. The creative transformation of Heaven and Earth is the foundation of the spirits’ generation and completion of things; the creative transformation of the sages is the way of responding to things and assisting their development. Without observing the transformations of Heaven and Earth, one cannot see that the Way of the sages has a foundation; without observing the Way of the sages, one cannot see that the transformations of Heaven and Earth have a consummation. Thus Heaven has no two suns, and the people have no two kings. The alternation of overcast and clear skies, order and disorder, and the unequal numbers of noble and petty men are constants of Heaven and Earth. Through these constants, the sages comprehend changing circumstances: they quell disorder and restore what is right, exalt the ruler and subordinate his ministers, advance noble men and dismiss petty men, and treat the central realm as internal and the Yi and Di peoples as external. By these means they support yang and restrain yin, assisting the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth.
