Thus, understanding this and acting as emperors, Yao and Shun opened up the primordial wilderness, laid a foundation upon which later generations could rely [?], removed the Four Villains, and advanced the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai. Thereby the succession of legitimate rule was established and the succession of the Way was set right. Understanding this and acting as teachers, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius set forth the images of the Changes and appended its statements, extended heavenly principle, warned against human desires, followed the structure of the River Chart, and took the meaning of the Luo Writing as their foundation. Thereby the succession of the Way was clarified and the succession of legitimate rule made manifest. For Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intention; the sages, though possessing conscious intention, act without contrivance. Acting without contrivance does not mean doing absolutely nothing: it means fulfilling human effort so as to accord with Heaven. When human effort is fully exerted so as to accord with Heaven, then this too is…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天道之無爲而天下國家可坐而理矣執
事策士以研理之學無亦欲其究圖書之
旨歸以求盡夫聖神功化之極乎顧愚何
足以及此
第三問
周策
同考試官教諭彭　批〔人才之盛衰係于時而所以致多才者亦係于用至于純心焉要矣作者見未逮此率亦未有定論〕
〔子其通達有□者乎可以觀才矣〕
===
考試官教諭張　批〔考論古今人才及用人之法甚〕
〔□□□□有要論可採錄之〕
考試官學正高　批〔用人要務得于有確見矣宜錄〕
〔□□式〕
執事有感于
廟堂需才之議以古今人才下策末學而欲
得卓犖雄渾之才以拔出魁壘用佐我
聖天子昌熙之運意甚隆也顧愚才未脫乎椽
桷形未超乎驪黃曷足以與于此哉雖然
punctuated:
天道之無爲，而天下國家可坐而理矣。執事策士以研理之學，無亦欲其究圖書之旨歸，以求盡夫聖神功化之極乎？顧愚何足以及此！

第三問
周策
同考試官教諭彭　批〔人才之盛衰係于時，而所以致多才者亦係于用。至于純心焉，要矣。作者見未逮此，率亦未有定論。〕〔子其通達有□者乎？可以觀才矣。〕
考試官教諭張　批〔考論古今人才及用人之法，甚〕〔□□□□，有要論可採錄之。〕
考試官學正高　批〔用人要務，得于有確見矣，宜錄〕〔□□式。〕

執事有感于廟堂需才之議，以古今人才下策末學，而欲得卓犖雄渾之才，以拔出魁壘，用佐我聖天子昌熙之運，意甚隆也。顧愚才未脫乎椽桷，形未超乎驪黃，曷足以與于此哉？雖然，
translation_en:
…the effortless action of the Way of Heaven, and all under Heaven, the state, and the family can be brought to order with ease. In examining candidates on the learning that investigates principle, do you not also wish them to probe the ultimate meaning of the River Chart and the Luo Writing, seeking thereby to comprehend fully the utmost achievements and transforming influence of the sage? Yet how could someone as ignorant as I attain this?

Third Question
Zhou Ce

Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: 〔The flourishing or decline of talent depends on the times, but bringing forth many talented people also depends on how they are employed. As for making the heart pure, that is essential. The writer’s understanding has not reached this point, and on the whole he has arrived at no settled judgment.〕〔Might you be someone of broad understanding who possesses □ [?]? Your talent can be discerned here.〕

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔His examination and discussion of talented people past and present, and of methods for employing them, are very〕〔□□□□ [?]. There are important arguments here worth selecting and recording.〕

Examiner Gao, School Instructor, comments: 〔On the essential tasks of employing people, he has attained definite insights [?]. This should be recorded〕〔□□ as a model [?].〕

Moved by the court’s discussions of its need for talent, you have set a policy question on talented people past and present before us humble students. You wish to find men of outstanding, powerful, and comprehensive abilities, to select preeminent figures and thereby assist the flourishing and harmonious reign of our sage Son of Heaven. Your purpose is most exalted. Yet my meager talent has not risen beyond that of ordinary rafters, nor has my outward form transcended the superficial distinctions between black and yellow horses. How could I be worthy of inclusion among such men? Nevertheless, …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
竊聞之漢史有云蓋有非常之功必有非
常之人然而非常之人共功率弘于草昧
之初何哉蓋草昧之初法制未定才將則
將焉才相則相焉無所謂例簿也而開創
之君惟其賢不惟其迹惟其稱不惟其資
無所謂牽制也若夫承平既久則規格科
條森然昭布而守文之世雖欲𨚫例顯庸
如吏議何知乎此則古今人才之盛衰始
有可言者矣易曰雲從龍風從虎聖人作
===
而萬物覩言君臣感應之不忒也詩曰鳳
凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧桐生矣于彼朝陽菶
菶萋萋雝雝喈喈言人才感召之有道也
粤稽古有虞以重華之德膺帝堯之禪當
時相與共治者有禹稷契臯陶伯益爲之
平水土敎稼穡明人倫飭五刑烈山澤以
翊成萬世永賴之功古今稱才之盛者莫
加焉迨至有周本執競之德爲弔伐之舉
當時相與興事者有周公召公南宮适散
punctuated:
竊聞之，漢史有云：「蓋有非常之功，必有非常之人。」然而非常之人，共功率弘于草昧之初，何哉？蓋草昧之初，法制未定，才將則將焉，才相則相焉，無所謂例簿也。而開創之君，惟其賢，不惟其迹；惟其稱，不惟其資，無所謂牽制也。若夫承平既久，則規格科條森然昭布，而守文之世，雖欲𨚫例顯庸，如吏議何？知乎此，則古今人才之盛衰始有可言者矣。
《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」言君臣感應之不忒也。《詩》曰：「鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡；梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。」言人才感召之有道也。
粤稽古，有虞以重華之德膺帝堯之禪，當時相與共治者，有禹、稷、契、臯陶、伯益，爲之平水土、敎稼穡、明人倫、飭五刑、烈山澤，以翊成萬世永賴之功，古今稱才之盛者莫加焉。迨至有周，本執競之德，爲弔伐之舉，當時相與興事者，有周公、召公、南宮适、散
translation_en:
…I have humbly heard that the History of the Han says: “For there to be extraordinary achievements, there must be extraordinary men.” Yet why is it that extraordinary men generally accomplish their greatest deeds [?] at the obscure beginnings of an age? At such beginnings, laws and institutions are not yet fixed: whoever has the talent to be a general is made a general, and whoever has the talent to be a chief minister is made a chief minister. There are no registers of precedents, so to speak. Founding rulers attend to a man’s worth, rather than merely his past record, and to his fitness for office, rather than merely his seniority. There are no such restraints. Once peace has long prevailed, however, regulations and statutory provisions stand densely arrayed and clearly promulgated. In an age devoted to preserving established institutions, even if one wishes to set aside precedent and employ men in prominent office, what can one do about the objections of the officials? Only when this is understood can one begin to discuss the flourishing and decline of talent in ancient and modern times.
The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all things behold him.” This speaks of the unfailing mutual response between ruler and ministers. The Book of Odes says: “The phoenix cries upon that lofty ridge; the wutong grows on its sunward slope. Luxuriant and flourishing are the trees; harmonious and melodious are the cries.” This speaks of the proper way to attract men of talent.
Examining antiquity, we find that the ruler of Yu, Shun, received Emperor Yao’s abdication through his virtue of renewed splendor. Those who then joined him in governing were Yu, Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Bo Yi. For him they put the waters and lands in order, taught sowing and reaping, clarified human relationships, regulated the Five Punishments, and cleared the mountains and marshes by fire. Thus they helped bring about achievements on which all generations would forever depend. Among those celebrated for an abundance of talent in ancient and modern times, none surpassed them. When the Zhou arose, its ruler, drawing upon his virtue of resolute strength, undertook punitive campaigns to relieve the suffering people. Those who joined him in this enterprise included the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, Nangong Kuo, and San…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宜生太顛閎夭呂望諸臣爲之疏附爲之
先後爲之奔走禦侮以弼成清明之化古
今言才之盛者莫加焉夫上有舜
武之爲君而後下有五臣十人爲之佐下
有五臣十人爲之佐而後永賴清明之化
成人見五臣十人之治獨異于古而不知
舜武相遇之難有如此者故由周而前大
禹承舜禪之後一時共治之臣固當時同
事于虞廷者也雖謂爲有夏之盛焉可也
===
迨夫成湯不憚三聘之煩而伊尹奏阿衡
之勳高宗信帝賚之夢而傳說成鹽梅之
治向使成湯以五就疏尹而高宗以版築
棄說欲其成伐夏中興之業其可得乎由
周而後當列國分爭之餘秦以戎狄承之
當時諸臣要皆權術遊說之客也雖謂之
無才焉可也迨夫高祖得三傑而以之興
漢昭烈得孔明而以之三分向使高祖以
刀筆棄蕭以跨下棄韓以亡命棄張昭烈
punctuated:
宜生、太顛、閎夭、呂望諸臣，爲之疏附，爲之先後，爲之奔走禦侮，以弼成清明之化，古今言才之盛者莫加焉。夫上有舜、武之爲君，而後下有五臣、十人爲之佐；下有五臣、十人爲之佐，而後永賴清明之化成。人見五臣、十人之治獨異于古，而不知舜、武相遇之難有如此者。故由周而前，大禹承舜禪之後，一時共治之臣，固當時同事于虞廷者也，雖謂爲有夏之盛焉可也。
迨夫成湯不憚三聘之煩，而伊尹奏阿衡之勳；高宗信帝賚之夢，而傳說成鹽梅之治。向使成湯以五就疏尹，而高宗以版築棄說，欲其成伐夏、中興之業，其可得乎？由周而後，當列國分爭之餘，秦以戎狄承之，當時諸臣要皆權術遊說之客也，雖謂之無才焉可也。迨夫高祖得三傑而以之興漢，昭烈得孔明而以之三分。向使高祖以刀筆棄蕭，以跨下棄韓，以亡命棄張，昭烈
translation_en:
…Yisheng—that is, San Yisheng—Tai Dian, Hong Yao, Lü Wang, and the other ministers drew men close to him, assisted him before and behind, hastened about in his service, and resisted aggression, helping him bring about enlightened and orderly government. Among those celebrated throughout history for their abundance of talent, none surpassed them. Only when there were rulers above such as Shun and King Wu were there the five ministers and the ten worthy men below to assist them; only with those five ministers and ten men as assistants could a lasting legacy of enlightened and orderly government be achieved. People see that the government of these five ministers and ten men was exceptional even in antiquity, but do not understand how difficult it was for such ministers to encounter rulers like Shun and King Wu. Looking back before the Zhou, after Yu the Great succeeded through Shun’s abdication, the ministers who shared in governing were indeed those who had served together at the court of Yu, under Shun. It is therefore also fitting to speak of this as an abundance of talent under the Xia.
Then Cheng Tang did not shrink from the trouble of extending three invitations, and Yi Yin rendered meritorious service as Chief Minister (Aheng). Gaozong trusted his dream of a gift from the Lord on High, and Fu Yue [written 傳說 here; ?] achieved harmonious government, like salt and sour plums blended in seasoning. Had Cheng Tang distanced himself from Yi Yin because of his five occasions of entering service, or Gaozong rejected Fu Yue because he had worked building rammed-earth walls, could they have accomplished the conquest of Xia and the restoration of their dynasty? Looking beyond the Zhou, after the contending states had fought among themselves, Qin, with its Rong and Di character, succeeded them. Its ministers were essentially all practitioners of political manipulation and itinerant persuasion; one might fittingly say that it had no worthy talent. Later, Gaozu obtained the Three Heroes and through them established the Han; Zhaolie obtained Kongming and through him secured a share in the threefold division of the realm. Had Gaozu rejected Xiao He for his clerk’s knife and brush, Han Xin for having crawled between another man’s legs, or Zhang Liang for having been a fugitive, and had Zhaolie…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以草莽惜三顧欲成一統三分之業其可
得乎故論才于三代之上者當以才之大
小爲優劣不當以數之多寡爲盛衰彼五
臣者以一人而當億兆人者也盛之盛也
十人者以一人而當千百人者也盛之次
也不然孔子嘆才難而曰唐虞之際于斯
爲盛豈非有見于此哉其論人才于三代
之下者當究其遭時所遇之主而不當以
成敗爲優劣彼三傑之于漢高也遇也孔
===
明之于昭烈也不遇也使三傑當昭烈之
時而孔明遭漢高之主烏知不易地皆然
哉況乎人才各有所長譬則規可以爲圓
而不可以爲方矩可以爲方而不可以爲
圓是物理且然人才可知矣雖在唐虞聞
稷以教稼穡矣而未聞兼乎教與刑也聞
禹以平水土矣而未聞兼乎益也是聖臣
且然其下可知矣故用才盡其所長則以
靈公之無道而王孫賈仲叔圉祝鮀之徒
punctuated: 以草莽惜三顧，欲成一統三分之業，其可得乎？故論才于三代之上者，當以才之大小爲優劣，不當以數之多寡爲盛衰。彼五臣者，以一人而當億兆人者也，盛之盛也；十人者，以一人而當千百人者也，盛之次也。不然，孔子嘆才難而曰：「唐虞之際，于斯爲盛。」豈非有見于此哉？其論人才于三代之下者，當究其遭時所遇之主，而不當以成敗爲優劣。彼三傑之于漢高也，遇也；孔明之于昭烈也，不遇也。使三傑當昭烈之時，而孔明遭漢高之主，烏知不易地皆然哉？況乎人才各有所長，譬則規可以爲圓，而不可以爲方；矩可以爲方，而不可以爲圓。是物理且然，人才可知矣。雖在唐虞，聞稷以教稼穡矣，而未聞兼乎教與刑也；聞禹以平水土矣，而未聞兼乎益也。是聖臣且然，其下可知矣。故用才盡其所長，則以靈公之無道，而王孫賈、仲叔圉、祝鮀之徒
translation_en:
…had begrudged making three visits because the man lived in rustic obscurity, could they have achieved their respective enterprises of unifying the realm and establishing one of its three kingdoms? Thus, in assessing talent in the Three Dynasties and earlier, one should judge superiority and inferiority by the magnitude of people’s abilities, rather than judge abundance and scarcity by their numbers. Each of those five ministers was a match for countless millions: this was abundance at its highest. Each of the ten was a match for hundreds or thousands: this was abundance of the next order. Otherwise, when Confucius lamented how difficult talent was to find and said, “In the age of Tang and Yu, talent was most abundant at this time,” was he not recognizing this very point?

In assessing talented men after the Three Dynasties, one should investigate the times they encountered and the rulers they served, rather than judge their superiority or inferiority by success or failure. The Three Heroes serving Gaozu of Han had favorable circumstances; Kongming serving Zhaolie did not. Had the Three Heroes lived in Zhaolie’s time, and had Kongming encountered a ruler like Gaozu of Han, how can we know that, exchanging places, they would not each have fared just as the others did?

Moreover, talented men each have their own strengths. A compass, for example, can make a circle but cannot make a square; a carpenter’s square can make a square but cannot make a circle. Since this holds even for the properties of things, we can understand how it applies to human talent. Even in the age of Tang and Yu, we hear of Ji teaching sowing and reaping, but not of his also taking charge of moral instruction and punishments. We hear of Yu bringing the waters and lands into order, but not of his also taking on Yi’s duties. Since this was true even of sage ministers, we can understand how it applies to those beneath them. Thus, when employing talent fully realizes each person’s strengths, even under a ruler as devoid of the Way as Duke Ling, men such as Wangsun Jia, Zhongshu Yu, and Zhu Tuo…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
猶足以存衛苟用矣而信之不篤則以箕
子比干微子之仁而不能以延商用不用
之間而國之存亡以之孰謂人才無關于
治忽哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奮迹南服迅掃腥羶奉
天命以行天討悲人窮以順人心取天下于戎
濁之秋不啻比迹湯武而已然義旗一揮
而豪傑雲集如徐中山之征討四方智勇
超絶常開平之克復中原戰勝攻取鄧寧
===
河湯東甌之撫定八州所至無敵沐黔寧
李岐陽之討平諸夷所向有功他如胡大
海趙德勝桑世傑張德勝耿再成俞通海
諸臣著勳勞于督戰之日又如劉基之運
籌決勝宋濂之學貫天人章溢之忠孝兩
盡吳訥之臣僚讓德固皆一代佐命之元
勳視十人之廓清弘化何以異哉自非我
聖祖求之有道而信之不疑使之以器而任之
不貳其何以收削平之功乎逮我
punctuated: 猶足以存衛。苟用矣，而信之不篤，則以箕子、比干、微子之仁，而不能以延商。用不用之間，而國之存亡以之，孰謂人才無關于治忽哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝奮迹南服，迅掃腥羶，奉天命以行天討，悲人窮以順人心，取天下于戎濁之秋，不啻比迹湯武而已。然義旗一揮，而豪傑雲集，如徐中山之征討四方，智勇超絶；常開平之克復中原，戰勝攻取；鄧寧河、湯東甌之撫定八州，所至無敵；沐黔寧、李岐陽之討平諸夷，所向有功。他如胡大海、趙德勝、桑世傑、張德勝、耿再成、俞通海諸臣，著勳勞于督戰之日；又如劉基之運籌決勝，宋濂之學貫天人，章溢之忠孝兩盡，吳訥之臣僚讓德，固皆一代佐命之元勳，視十人之廓清弘化，何以異哉？自非我聖祖求之有道，而信之不疑，使之以器，而任之不貳，其何以收削平之功乎？逮我
translation_en:
…were still sufficient to preserve Wei. If worthy men are employed but not fully trusted, then even men with the benevolence of Jizi, Bigan, and Weizi cannot prolong the life of Shang. Whether such men are employed determines the survival or destruction of the state. Who would say that talented men have no bearing on order and disorder?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao rose in the southern lands and swiftly swept away the foul barbarian presence. Upholding Heaven’s mandate, he carried out Heaven’s punishments; pitying the people’s distress, he accorded with their hearts. He won All under Heaven in an age of barbarian defilement, doing more than merely matching the achievements of Tang and Wu. Once he raised the banner of righteousness, heroes gathered like clouds. Xu, Prince of Zhongshan, campaigned in all four directions, displaying surpassing wisdom and courage; Chang, Prince of Kaiping, recovered the Central Plain, winning battles and taking all he attacked. Deng, Prince of Ninghe, and Tang, Prince of Dong’ou, pacified the eight regions, meeting no match wherever they went. Mu, Prince of Qianning, and Li, Prince of Qiyang, subdued the various non-Chinese peoples, achieving success wherever they turned. Other ministers, including Hu Dahai, Zhao Desheng, Sang Shijie, Zhang Desheng, Geng Zaicheng, and Yu Tonghai, rendered distinguished service while directing battles. Then there were Liu Ji, whose strategic planning secured victory; Song Lian, whose learning encompassed Heaven and humanity; Zhang Yi, who fulfilled both loyalty and filial devotion; and Wu Ne, to whose virtue his fellow ministers deferred [?]. These were all foremost founding ministers who assisted the dynasty in receiving its mandate. How did they differ from the ten men who cleared the realm and extended its transforming influence? Had our sagely founder not sought them by the proper means, trusted them without suspicion, employed them according to their abilities, and entrusted them with responsibility without wavering, how could he have achieved the conquest and pacification of the realm? When it came to our …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
列聖光紹景命旁招俊彥可謂先後一揆矣而
海內者碩之士靡不向風景附雖不越乎
吏議之常而去古未遠辟召屢行眞才接
踵而出有由然哉我
皇上嗣登大寶撫有成業謂明良交而德業成
則敦禮耆舊輔弼之臣信之必專謂賢才
輔而天下治則博開登崇俊良之門而立
之無方謂野有遺賢也而辟舉之政行焉
謂遺佚可錄也而起用之
===
詔下焉方今賢俊滿朝而寸長片善之必錄忠
良顯遂而一才一藝無不庸宜乎用有餘
才官不乏人矣夫何頃者邊陲多事南北
騷然當事之臣試之寡效司銓者將愼選
以充而臨事恒致有乏才之嘆此執事所
以欲得跅弛之才以佐成亨嘉之會也自
今言之天生一代之才自周一代之用未
聞藉才於異代者也必也在廊廟之上則
于公孤之才而隆其禮焉時勤訪問如古
punctuated:
列聖光紹景命，旁招俊彥，可謂先後一揆矣。而海內者碩之士，靡不向風景附。雖不越乎吏議之常，而去古未遠，辟召屢行，眞才接踵而出，有由然哉！我皇上嗣登大寶，撫有成業，謂明良交而德業成，則敦禮耆舊輔弼之臣，信之必專；謂賢才輔而天下治，則博開登崇俊良之門，而立之無方；謂野有遺賢也，而辟舉之政行焉；謂遺佚可錄也，而起用之詔下焉。方今賢俊滿朝，而寸長片善之必錄；忠良顯遂，而一才一藝無不庸。宜乎用有餘才，官不乏人矣。夫何頃者邊陲多事，南北騷然，當事之臣試之寡效，司銓者將愼選以充，而臨事恒致有乏才之嘆？此執事所以欲得跅弛之才，以佐成亨嘉之會也。
自今言之，天生一代之才，自周一代之用，未聞藉才於異代者也。必也在廊廟之上，則于公孤之才而隆其禮焉，時勤訪問，如古
translation_en:
…the successive sage emperors gloriously continued the great mandate and sought outstanding men far and wide: their guiding principle, earlier and later alike, may be called one and the same. Throughout the realm, men of eminent stature [?] all turned toward their influence and attached themselves like shadows. Although appointments remained within the customary procedures of official deliberation, these practices were not far removed from antiquity: invitations to serve were repeatedly issued, and men of true ability emerged one after another. Surely there was a reason for this!
Our Emperor succeeded to the throne and took possession of an established imperial undertaking. Holding that virtue and achievement are perfected through the accord of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, he treats veteran ministers and senior advisers with generous courtesy and places undivided trust in them. Holding that the realm is well governed with the assistance of worthy talent, he opens wide the avenues for advancing outstanding and good men, appointing them without fixed restrictions. Holding that worthy men remain overlooked outside office, he implements measures to summon and recommend them. Holding that those left in obscurity deserve consideration, he issues edicts calling them into service. Today, worthy and outstanding men fill the court, yet even the slightest strength or merit is sure to receive recognition; loyal and good men enjoy distinction and advancement, yet no talent or skill goes unused. There ought, then, to be talent to spare for service and no shortage of men for office. Why, then, have the recent troubles on the frontiers thrown both north and south into turmoil, while the ministers responsible have achieved little when put to the test? Those in charge of appointments seek to fill the posts through careful selection, yet whenever affairs demand action, there are invariably laments over the shortage of talent. This is why you, sir, wish to obtain men of unrestrained talent, to help bring about a flourishing convergence of worthy men.
Speaking of the present, Heaven produces the talent of each age sufficient to meet that age’s needs; never have we heard of borrowing talent from another age. Surely, at the imperial court, men with the capacity to serve as the Three Dukes and Three Junior Dukes should be accorded the fullest ceremonial respect, and frequently and diligently consulted, as in antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之都俞吁咈于一堂而伊傅周召之才端
可見矣在邊陲之遠則于封疆之臣而盡
其能焉責之以成功而不束以文法則李
郭韓范之才端可見矣于郡邑之吏而重
其任焉假以歲月期以成績如漢之贈金
增秩則不必寤寐循良而龔黃卓魯之才
有不可見乎于將師之臣而優其權焉厚
供餽以恤其私貸小過以圖其大如古之
謗書盈篋而不惑則不必拊髀思將而頗
===
牧起剪之才有不復見乎制科善矣而空
言無補不有鄉舉里選之遺意可兼舉乎
大比校藝之外俾有司錄其德誼之實與
夫才之所優而參考之則德成而上藝成
而下眞才有不輩出焉否也養道豫矣而
記誦徒勤不有三物之教蘇湖治事之遺
法可兼舉乎月省歲會之餘而又必任其
才之所宜志之所欲如星曆戰陣營田水
利之類士以此而優劣官以此而殿最眞
punctuated:
之都俞吁咈于一堂，而伊傅周召之才端可見矣。在邊陲之遠，則于封疆之臣而盡其能焉，責之以成功，而不束以文法，則李郭韓范之才端可見矣。于郡邑之吏而重其任焉，假以歲月，期以成績，如漢之贈金增秩，則不必寤寐循良，而龔黃卓魯之才有不可見乎？于將師之臣而優其權焉，厚供餽以恤其私，貸小過以圖其大，如古之謗書盈篋而不惑，則不必拊髀思將，而頗牧起剪之才有不復見乎？
制科善矣，而空言無補，不有鄉舉里選之遺意可兼舉乎？大比校藝之外，俾有司錄其德誼之實，與夫才之所優而參考之，則德成而上，藝成而下，眞才有不輩出焉否也？養道豫矣，而記誦徒勤，不有三物之教、蘇湖治事之遺法可兼舉乎？月省歲會之餘，而又必任其才之所宜、志之所欲，如星曆、戰陣、營田、水利之類。士以此而優劣，官以此而殿最，眞
translation_en:
…with the assent and dissent of ancient deliberations voiced together in one hall, men with the talents of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao will surely emerge. In the distant borderlands, enable the officials charged with defending the frontiers to exercise their abilities fully. Hold them responsible for success without binding them with administrative regulations, and men with the talents of Li Guang, Guo Ziyi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan will surely emerge. Give greater weight to the responsibilities of prefectural and county officials; allow them time and expect accomplishments from them, rewarding them with gold and increases in rank as under the Han. Then, without yearning day and night for upright and capable administrators, could one fail to find men with the talents of Gong Sui, Huang Ba, Zhuo Mao, and Lu Gong? Grant military commanders ample authority; provide generous supplies to relieve their personal concerns, and pardon minor faults in pursuit of great achievements. Follow the ancient example of remaining undeceived even when slanderous letters filled a chest. Then, without slapping one’s thigh in longing for a general, could men with the talents of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wu Qi, and Wang Jian fail to appear again?
The examination system is good, yet empty words bring no benefit. Could we not also adopt something of the surviving intent of recommending men from the townships and selecting them from the villages? Beyond assessing literary accomplishment at the triennial examination, have the responsible officials record concrete evidence of candidates’ virtue and righteousness, together with their particular talents, and consider these jointly. If those accomplished in virtue are ranked above those accomplished in literary skills, could true talent fail to emerge in abundance? Provision has been made for nurturing talent, yet effort is spent fruitlessly on memorization and recitation. Could we not also adopt the teaching of the Three Categories and the surviving methods of instruction in practical affairs used at Suzhou and Huzhou? Beyond monthly inspections and annual assessments, men must also be assigned work suited to their abilities and aspirations, in such fields as astronomy and calendrical calculation, military formations, agricultural development, and water management. Let scholars be judged superior or inferior on this basis, and officials receive their lowest or highest performance ratings on this basis; true…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
才有不豫養焉否也至于犇逸不羈之才
冥飛遯舉之士有不囿于庠序之所養制
科之可羅者則載之于垂綸可也起之于
築巖可也三聘而陟阿衡之任一舉而登
大將之壇亦可也雖然求才固有其道而
用才尤有其本又必純心以任之則讒諂
不得以亂正而貴德之義盡夫然後可以
感會風雲以翊成
昌熙之治以比隆唐虞三代之盛矣故曰純心
===
要矣用賢爲
第四問
閻應儒
同考試官教諭孟　批〔裕財需效於久制究先務其大義對雅達政源且探事獻說言中肯綮而復標以顯義約以〕
考試官教諭張　批〔正詞所謂治練而文工者也楚珠桂櫝斯爲允稱宜冠諸作贍裁深剴詞識遠猷隱然見〕
考試官學正高　批〔於言外蓋其詞婉其旨遂者也宜式多士敷敘閎於藝藉匠畫超乎意表〕
punctuated:
才有不豫養焉否也？至于犇逸不羈之才、冥飛遯舉之士，有不囿于庠序之所養、制科之可羅者，則載之于垂綸可也，起之于築巖可也，三聘而陟阿衡之任，一舉而登大將之壇，亦可也。雖然，求才固有其道，而用才尤有其本，又必純心以任之，則讒諂不得以亂正，而貴德之義盡。夫然後可以感會風雲，以翊成昌熙之治，以比隆唐虞三代之盛矣。故曰：「純心要矣，用賢爲。」
第四問
閻應儒
同考試官教諭孟批〔裕財需效於久，制究先務其大義。對雅達政源，且探事獻說，言中肯綮，而復標以顯義，約以〕
考試官教諭張批〔正詞，所謂治練而文工者也。楚珠桂櫝，斯爲允稱，宜冠諸作。贍裁深剴，詞識遠猷，隱然見〕
考試官學正高批〔於言外，蓋其詞婉，其旨遂者也。宜式多士，敷敘閎於藝藉，匠畫超乎意表〕
translation_en:
…could talent then fail to be nurtured in advance? As for talents that race freely beyond restraint, and men who soar into obscurity and withdraw from view, some lie beyond the nurturing scope of the schools and the reach of the established examinations. Such men may be taken aboard while fishing with a line, or summoned from building walls among the crags. They may also, after three invitations, be raised to the office of Aheng, chief minister, or at a single stroke ascend the platform of a general-in-chief.
Yet while seeking talent certainly has its proper methods, employing talent has an even more fundamental requirement. One must entrust responsibilities to worthy men with a pure heart. Then slanderers and flatterers cannot confound what is right, and the obligation to honor virtue is fully discharged. Only then can ruler and ministers meet in auspicious accord, like wind and cloud, to help bring about flourishing and peaceful government, rivaling the splendor of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Thus it is said: “Purity of heart is essential; employing the worthy is…” [? The closing words appear out of order in the transcription.]
Fourth Policy Question
Yan Yingru
Associate Examiner Meng, Instructor, comments: 〔To make financial resources abundant, results must be sought over the long term; in examining institutions, first attend to their larger principles [?]. This answer displays an accomplished understanding of the foundations of government. It also investigates affairs and offers proposals, its words striking the crucial points. Furthermore, it sets out illuminating principles and gives concise expression through…〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔…correct language. This is what is meant by being practiced in government and accomplished in composition. Pearls of Chu in a cassia-wood casket: this is indeed a fitting description. It deserves to rank first among all the essays. Its ample composition is deeply incisive; discernment and far-reaching plans are discernible…〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔…beyond the words themselves. Its language is graceful and its meaning fully conveyed. It should serve as a model for the many scholars. Its exposition ranges broadly through the classical writings [?], and its ingenious design surpasses expectation.〕

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天下有事若反而相濟言若迂而實切者
固衆人之所疑而達者之所信善謀國者
不可以弗辨也今夫足國之道固貴乎竭
智畢慮以拯一時之急尤貴乎深思長顧
以爲攸久之圖然人情喜于欲速而厭于
持久則未有不以一時爲切而持久爲迂
者也殊不知國之病財譬人之病瘍也瘍
有瘵之以峻削則悅有告以藤艾元和則
咈然怒曰此庸醫也曾何足以謀吾瘍卒
===
之瘍愈劇而元和日耗其曷能及乎易有
之曰何以聚人曰財書八政一曰食二曰
貨此財用民食天下國家之大計也在昔
成周兵以私田而不餉士大夫以公田而
不廩歲時經費不越乎祭祀宴饗服輿匪
頒好用數者而已周公方且憂之總其權
于家宰而又有司會司書職幣職歲以防
其微有參互日要歲會以考其成是周之
所以理財者理其財之出而已非以理其
punctuated: 天下有事若反而相濟，言若迂而實切者，固衆人之所疑而達者之所信，善謀國者不可以弗辨也。今夫足國之道，固貴乎竭智畢慮以拯一時之急，尤貴乎深思長顧以爲攸久之圖。然人情喜于欲速而厭于持久，則未有不以一時爲切而持久爲迂者也。殊不知國之病財，譬人之病瘍也。瘍有瘵之以峻削則悅，有告以藤艾元和則咈然怒曰：「此庸醫也，曾何足以謀吾瘍！」卒之瘍愈劇而元和日耗，其曷能及乎？《易》有之，曰：「何以聚人？曰財。」《書》八政，一曰食，二曰貨。此財用民食，天下國家之大計也。在昔成周，兵以私田而不餉，士大夫以公田而不廩，歲時經費不越乎祭祀、宴饗、服輿、匪頒、好用數者而已。周公方且憂之，總其權于家宰，而又有司會、司書、職幣、職歲以防其微，有參互、日要、歲會以考其成。是周之所以理財者，理其財之出而已，非以理其
translation_en:
There are affairs in the world that seem opposed yet complement one another, and statements that seem impractical yet are truly pertinent. These are precisely what ordinary people doubt and discerning people trust; those skilled in planning for the state must distinguish them. The way to make the state’s resources sufficient certainly requires exhausting one’s intelligence and deliberation to relieve an immediate emergency, but still more it requires deep reflection and a distant view to devise a lasting plan. Yet human nature delights in quick results and tires of sustained effort. Thus people invariably regard immediate measures as pertinent and enduring ones as impractical. They fail to realize that a state afflicted by financial difficulties resembles a person afflicted by sores. If someone treats the sores with drastic purging [?], the patient is pleased; if someone advises treatment involving vines and mugwort and the restoration of vital harmony [?], he angrily protests: “This is an incompetent physician! How could he possibly treat my sores?” In the end the sores grow worse and his vital harmony dwindles daily. How could any remedy then come in time?

The Book of Changes says: “By what means are people gathered together? Wealth.” Among the eight concerns of government in the Book of Documents, the first is food and the second is goods. Financial resources and the people’s sustenance are thus fundamental concerns of governing the realm and the state. In the days of the accomplished Zhou order, soldiers supported themselves from private fields and received no military provisions; officers and grandees supported themselves from public fields and received no grain stipends. Regular annual expenditure extended only to sacrifices, banquets, clothing and carriages, distributions, and gifts and discretionary expenses [?]. Even so, the Duke of Zhou remained concerned. He concentrated authority over these matters in the Grand Steward, while also establishing the offices of Manager of Accounts, Manager of Documents, Manager of Monetary Resources, and Manager of Annual Accounts to guard against the slightest abuses. There were cross-checks, daily summaries, and annual accounts to assess results. Thus the Zhou managed their finances by regulating the outflow of their resources alone, rather than by regulating their …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
財之入也理之于上者不欲虐取之于下
而已非固屑屑然如役役不憚煩也自是茅
茨之風遠而土木繁興禮讓之俗易而征
役不息此財用之所以日詘而徵輸之所
以日亟也逮漢之文帝玄默躬脩仁厚待
下非無所事財也然惜中人之產以罷露
臺業上書之囊以爲帷幕歲蠲田租輒復
除去與天下生養而休息之雖賈誼之建
議禮樂未遑而當時海內殷阜府庫充溢
===
史稱其漢家享國長久皆文帝所留有由
然矣至于武帝聰察彊毅喜于有爲非不
知重民也然泰時作而禱祀頻瀆兵革黷
而工役紛擾仁義外施多慾內存舉天下
之力而盡敝之雖其任用桑弘羊之徒算
及商車而得不償失海內虛耗史謂其蠹
國罷民靡費元氣不爲虛語矣夫文帝不
有其利而財用以贏譬則箕裘之子雖無
所獻爲而恪守節儉故業自有餘裕也武
punctuated:
財之入也。理之于上者，不欲虐取之于下而已，非固屑屑然如役役不憚煩也。自是茅茨之風遠，而土木繁興；禮讓之俗易，而征役不息。此財用之所以日詘，而徵輸之所以日亟也。逮漢之文帝，玄默躬脩，仁厚待下，非無所事財也。然惜中人之產以罷露臺，業上書之囊以爲帷幕，歲蠲田租，輒復除去，與天下生養而休息之。雖賈誼之建議禮樂未遑，而當時海內殷阜，府庫充溢。史稱其漢家享國長久，皆文帝所留，有由然矣。
至于武帝，聰察彊毅，喜于有爲，非不知重民也。然泰時作而禱祀頻瀆，兵革黷而工役紛擾，仁義外施，多慾內存，舉天下之力而盡敝之。雖其任用桑弘羊之徒，算及商車，而得不償失，海內虛耗。史謂其蠹國罷民，靡費元氣，不爲虛語矣。夫文帝不有其利，而財用以贏，譬則箕裘之子，雖無所獻爲，而恪守節儉，故業自有餘裕也。武
translation_en:
…the inflow of wealth. Those who managed it above sought only to avoid extracting it cruelly from those below; they were not simply fussing over details, as though toiling away without shrinking from troublesome tasks. Thereafter, the ethos of thatched-roof simplicity receded, and building projects proliferated; customs of ritual propriety and deference changed, and levies and labor service became incessant. Thus financial resources dwindled daily, while demands for tax payments grew ever more urgent.
When Emperor Wen of the Han came to rule, he quietly cultivated his own conduct and treated those below with benevolence and generosity. It was not that he had no occasion to expend wealth. Yet, reluctant to spend the equivalent of an ordinary household’s property, he abandoned the construction of the Dew Terrace; he used the bags in which memorials were submitted to make curtains [?]. He remitted the land tax in successive years and repeatedly abolished exactions, allowing the people of the realm to sustain themselves, raise their families, and rest. Although he had not found time to implement Jia Yi’s proposals concerning rites and music, the realm then prospered, and the treasuries and granaries overflowed. Historical accounts say that the Han dynasty’s long tenure of the realm was entirely a legacy of Emperor Wen. There was good reason for this judgment.
As for Emperor Wu, he was perceptive, strong-willed, and fond of undertaking great things. It was not that he failed to recognize the importance of the people. Yet “Tai” was undertaken at intervals [?], and prayers and sacrifices became so frequent as to be irreverent; warfare was pursued recklessly, and construction and labor service caused widespread turmoil. Benevolence and righteousness were displayed outwardly, while numerous desires remained within. He mobilized the strength of the entire realm and utterly exhausted it. Although he employed men such as Sang Hongyang and extended taxation even to merchants’ carts, the gains did not compensate for the losses, and the realm was depleted. The historians’ assertion that he undermined the state, exhausted the people, and squandered its vital energies was no empty statement.
Emperor Wen did not claim the profits for himself, and financial resources consequently became abundant. He was like a son carrying on his family’s craft: although he made no particular contribution [?], he scrupulously maintained frugality, so that the inherited estate naturally remained more than sufficient. Emperor Wu…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
帝以利爲利而國事日蹙譬則鉅積之室
雖善于摧㩲而驕奢亡度故難與長守富
也是則節與不節之間而崇本逐末之效
已昭然矣唐之財賦有劉晏以司度支而
又有裴肅以刺史進蕭綬以判官進裴延
齡皇甫鎛以聚斂進要之專利于上爲國
之蠹孰若李翱所謂人知厚斂之可以富
國而不知薄斂之爲富愈大爲有見哉宋
之財賦有陳恕以董磨勘而又有景德會
===
計錄皇祐會計錄治平會計錄雖皆所以
總括邦計孰若蘇轍之元祐錄其要主于
節用以厚民生爲有得哉肆我
聖祖當順天革命之初而蠲民田租之令無歲
不下然國無廢典民有餘貲是我
聖祖之所以結人心而凝天命者端有在矣我
列聖承重熙累洽之運而任土作賦之外一無
所括然賦不加增而用不加損是我
列聖之所以撫
punctuated: 帝以利爲利，而國事日蹙。譬則鉅積之室，雖善于摧㩲，而驕奢亡度，故難與長守富也。是則節與不節之間，而崇本逐末之效已昭然矣。唐之財賦，有劉晏以司度支，而又有裴肅以刺史進、蕭綬以判官進、裴延齡皇甫鎛以聚斂進。要之，專利于上，爲國之蠹。孰若李翱所謂「人知厚斂之可以富國，而不知薄斂之爲富愈大」爲有見哉？宋之財賦，有陳恕以董磨勘，而又有《景德會計錄》《皇祐會計錄》《治平會計錄》，雖皆所以總括邦計，孰若蘇轍之《元祐錄》，其要主于節用以厚民生爲有得哉？肆我聖祖當順天革命之初，而蠲民田租之令無歲不下，然國無廢典，民有餘貲。是我聖祖之所以結人心而凝天命者，端有在矣。我列聖承重熙累洽之運，而任土作賦之外，一無所括，然賦不加增，而用不加損。是我列聖之所以撫
translation_en:
…Emperor Wu took profit itself as his aim, and the affairs of state grew daily more straitened. This was like a household with vast accumulated wealth: though skilled at financial manipulation [?], its arrogance and boundless extravagance made it difficult to preserve its riches for long. Thus, in the distinction between frugality and its absence, the consequences of honoring the fundamental or pursuing the peripheral are already plain.

In the fiscal administration of the Tang, Liu Yan supervised revenue and expenditure; there were also Pei Su, who advanced as a prefect, Xiao Shou, who advanced as an administrative assistant, and Pei Yanling and Huangfu Bo, who advanced through fiscal exactions. In essence, they monopolized profit for those above and became parasites upon the state. How could they match the insight of Li Ao’s statement: “People know that heavy taxation can enrich the state, but do not know that light taxation produces still greater wealth”? In the fiscal administration of the Song, Chen Shu supervised the auditing of accounts. There were also the Jingde Fiscal Accounts, the Huangyou Fiscal Accounts, and the Zhiping Fiscal Accounts. Although all these comprehensively surveyed state finances, how could they match the understanding shown in Su Zhe’s Yuanyou Record, whose essential principle was to economize on expenditure so as to improve the people’s livelihood?

Thus, when our sagely founder first obeyed Heaven and changed the dynasty, not a year passed without an edict remitting the people’s land tax. Yet no established state observance was neglected, and the people had wealth to spare. There was indeed a sound basis for our sagely founder’s winning the people’s hearts and securing Heaven’s Mandate. Our successive sage emperors inherited an age of accumulating prosperity and enduring harmony. Beyond assessing tribute according to the land’s resources, they exacted nothing further; yet taxation did not increase, and expenditure did not diminish. This was how our successive sage emperors sustained…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
鴻業而致盛治者必有道矣恭惟我
皇上踐阼五位保有萬方當
臨御之始首罷不急之役大黜非經之科
登極有詔
建儲有詔一則曰天下生民十分困窮一則曰
朕加意節省用自有餘
蠲田租
停閒架凡所以征諸民者可謂薄矣夫何頃
歲以來閭閻一歉遂至相食邊鎮告急�森
===
欲脫巾大司農贍度無策時稱匱乏之至
請下廷臣條爲理財集議一書檄行天下各陳
所見無非廣忠益集衆思求所以爲足國
裕民之計也今觀其書曰錢法曰山礦曰
屯鹽曰增稅凡以闢財之源者至矣曰清
邊費曰計經費曰裁宂費凡以節財之流
者至矣爲謀不同而同于籌
國家之用籌用不一而一于紓目前之急然
自今言之田有履畝之租户有丁口之役
punctuated: 鴻業而致盛治者，必有道矣。恭惟我皇上踐阼五位，保有萬方。當臨御之始，首罷不急之役，大黜非經之科。登極有詔，建儲有詔，一則曰：「天下生民十分困窮。」一則曰：「朕加意節省，用自有餘。」蠲田租，停閒架，凡所以征諸民者，可謂薄矣。夫何頃歲以來，閭閻一歉，遂至相食；邊鎮告急，�森欲脫巾；大司農贍度無策，時稱匱乏之至。請下廷臣，條爲《理財集議》一書，檄行天下，各陳所見，無非廣忠益、集衆思，求所以爲足國裕民之計也。今觀其書，曰錢法，曰山礦，曰屯鹽，曰增稅，凡以闢財之源者至矣；曰清邊費，曰計經費，曰裁宂費，凡以節財之流者至矣。爲謀不同，而同于籌國家之用；籌用不一，而一于紓目前之急。然自今言之，田有履畝之租，户有丁口之役，
translation_en:
…there must have been a way by which they sustained their magnificent enterprise and brought about flourishing government. We reverently reflect that Our Emperor has ascended the throne to the sovereign position [?] and holds dominion over all regions. At the beginning of his reign, he first abolished nonessential labor services and extensively eliminated irregular levies. An edict marked his accession, and another the designation of the heir apparent. One declared: “The people throughout the realm are in utter distress and poverty.” The other declared: “If I devote greater attention to economy, there will naturally be more than enough for expenditure.” He remitted land taxes and suspended the tax on rooms and structures. The exactions imposed upon the people could thus be called light. Why, then, in recent years has a single poor harvest reduced ordinary households to eating one another? The frontier garrisons report emergencies; [?] wish to cast off their official caps; and the Minister of Revenue has no plan for meeting expenses, repeatedly reporting the utmost shortage.

Proposals were referred to the court officials and arranged into a book, Collected Deliberations on Managing Finances, while official dispatches circulated throughout the realm, inviting everyone to state their views. All this was intended to draw more widely upon loyal counsel and pool collective judgment, seeking a means to provide adequately for the state and bring prosperity to the people. Examining this book now, we find sections on currency regulations, mountain mines, agricultural colonies and salt administration, and increased taxation: the means of opening sources of revenue have been pursued to the utmost. There are sections on putting frontier expenditure in order, calculating regular expenditure, and cutting superfluous expenditure: the means of restricting the outflow of funds have likewise been pursued to the utmost. The proposals differ, but all share the aim of providing for the state's expenses. Their ways of doing so vary, but all seek to relieve the immediate emergency. Yet, speaking of present conditions, land bears taxes assessed by the mu, and households bear service obligations assessed by their registered persons…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
門有事產之徵商有行貨之稅昔人所謂
兵役興而邊民困賦役煩而農民困鹽鐵
筭緡而商民困貴爵免罪而富民困入財
爲郎而世家困今皆有之誠有如
天語所謂天下十分困窮者也其諸繰絲者非
特見蛹將併其蛹食之矣其諸漁者非特
絶魚將併其澤�italic之矣昔魯哀公以年饑
爲憂而孔子告之以薄斂彼聖人豈固好
反其所見而爲是迂闊之論哉無亦深探
===
其本而導以利之大者乎至如魏文侯于
賀增賦者則以爲貪其賦稅而不愛人是
虞人反裘負薪而不知皮盡毛將安附也
彼文侯豈不欲專利自殖而爲是矯飾之
言哉無亦有見于國本所在而有不可斁者
乎今之言曰邊餉有定額
朝廷有定費
宗室有常祿官廩有常供此而益之猶患不
給賦而不加其何以濟愚竊以爲不然蓋
punctuated: 門有事產之徵，商有行貨之稅。昔人所謂兵役興而邊民困，賦役煩而農民困，鹽鐵筭緡而商民困，貴爵免罪而富民困，入財爲郎而世家困，今皆有之。誠有如天語所謂天下十分困窮者也。其諸繰絲者非特見蛹，將併其蛹食之矣；其諸漁者非特絶魚，將併其澤�italic之矣。昔魯哀公以年饑爲憂，而孔子告之以薄斂。彼聖人豈固好反其所見而爲是迂闊之論哉？無亦深探其本而導以利之大者乎？至如魏文侯，于賀增賦者，則以爲貪其賦稅而不愛人，是虞人反裘負薪而不知皮盡毛將安附也。彼文侯豈不欲專利自殖而爲是矯飾之言哉？無亦有見于國本所在而有不可斁者乎？今之言曰：「邊餉有定額，朝廷有定費，宗室有常祿，官廩有常供。此而益之，猶患不給；賦而不加，其何以濟？」愚竊以爲不然，蓋
translation_en:
…households face levies on their property [?], and merchants face taxes on goods in transit. The conditions described by men of old are all present today: military service expands and the frontier population suffers; taxes and labor services multiply and farmers suffer; salt and iron levies and taxes on mercantile wealth burden merchants; the costly purchase of rank and remission of punishment burdens the wealthy; and contributions of wealth to obtain appointments as court gentlemen burden established families. It is indeed as the imperial words declare: “All under Heaven is utterly impoverished.” Those reeling silk, one might say, are not merely exposing the pupae but are about to eat them as well; those fishing are not merely exhausting the fish but are about to [drain?] their marshes too [text corrupt].

Formerly, Duke Ai of Lu was troubled by famine, and Confucius advised him to reduce taxation. Could that sage really have delighted in contradicting what he saw and offering such impractical advice? Was it not rather that he probed deeply into the root of the matter and guided the duke toward the greater benefit? Likewise, when someone congratulated Marquis Wen of Wei on increased tax receipts, he considered greed for taxes without love for the people to be like a woodsman carrying firewood with his fur coat turned inside out, unaware that, once the hide was worn away, the fur would have nothing to cling to. Could Marquis Wen have had no desire to monopolize profit and enrich himself, and merely have spoken these words for show? Was it not rather that he understood where the foundation of the state lay and that it must not be ruined?

People today say: “Frontier military provisions have a fixed quota; the court has fixed expenses; the imperial clan has regular stipends; and official granaries have regular supplies to furnish. Even if these allocations are increased, we still fear they will be insufficient. Unless taxes are raised, how can we meet these needs?” In my humble judgment, this is not so, for…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
常觀之行者策疲羸之馬于千里之途策
愈急而疲愈甚曾不知少休焉將不至于
蹶不止也今民之將蹶亦久矣可不思所
以少息乎爲今之計田之正額不可省也
而塞下之荒屯郡國之蕪田可不任民所
墾乎今誠使民曰不清丈不起科行之數
年將中外無不墾之田矣中外無不墾之
田則粟米狼戾邊人得以倍食游民得有
常業是不轉餉而餉自足不賑貸而民無
===
失所也況地闢則人聚將又有不待召募
僑增而邊戍户口有餘裕矣當年之賦不
可已也而均徭之提編逋税之帶徵可不
輟而蠲乎今誠示民曰民間一歲所入止
有此數其可忍併徵以盡人財如此則所
紓民力皆國之力所裕民財皆國之財也
況新稅不逋則歲有常盈前者不加則後
者可繼矣至如鈔法者
國家所以操利權于上而不制于天不聽于
punctuated: 常觀之：行者策疲羸之馬于千里之途，策愈急而疲愈甚，曾不知少休焉，將不至于蹶不止也。今民之將蹶亦久矣，可不思所以少息乎？爲今之計，田之正額不可省也，而塞下之荒屯、郡國之蕪田，可不任民所墾乎？今誠使民曰：「不清丈，不起科。」行之數年，將中外無不墾之田矣。中外無不墾之田，則粟米狼戾，邊人得以倍食，游民得有常業，是不轉餉而餉自足，不賑貸而民無失所也。況地闢則人聚，將又有不待召募僑增，而邊戍户口有餘裕矣。當年之賦不可已也，而均徭之提編、逋税之帶徵，可不輟而蠲乎？今誠示民曰：「民間一歲所入，止有此數，其可忍併徵以盡人財？」如此，則所紓民力皆國之力，所裕民財皆國之財也。況新稅不逋，則歲有常盈；前者不加，則後者可繼矣。至如鈔法者，國家所以操利權于上，而不制于天、不聽于
translation_en:
…I have often observed this: when a traveler whips an exhausted, emaciated horse along a thousand-li journey, the more urgently he whips it, the more exhausted it becomes. If he never thinks to let it rest a little, he will not stop until it collapses. The people have long been on the verge of collapse. Can we fail to consider how to give them a little respite?

For present purposes, the regular land-tax quota cannot be reduced. But should we not allow the people to cultivate abandoned military-colony lands along the frontier and waste fields in the prefectures and other jurisdictions? If we truly told the people, “There will be no cadastral resurvey and no new tax assessment,” and maintained this policy for several years, no land would remain uncultivated, either in the interior or along the frontier. With no land left uncultivated, grain would abound; frontier inhabitants would have twice as much to eat, and people without settled livelihoods would gain regular occupations. Military provisions would thus suffice without transporting supplies, and the people would retain their livelihoods without relief distributions or loans. Moreover, opening up land would attract settlers. Without waiting for recruitment or an increase through migration [?], the frontier garrisons would have households and population to spare.

The current year's taxes cannot be suspended. But could we not halt the advance assessment of equalized labor-service levies and remit the collection of tax arrears alongside current dues? Let us truly make this clear to the people: “The people's annual income amounts to only so much. How could we bear to collect these dues together and exhaust their resources?” In this way, whatever strength we spare the people is strength preserved for the state; whatever wealth we leave the people is wealth preserved for the state. Moreover, if current taxes do not fall into arrears, there will be a regular abundance each year. If earlier dues are not added on, subsequent payments can be sustained.

As for the paper-currency system, it is the means by which the state retains control over economic advantage at the top, without being constrained by Heaven or subject to…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人者也此法廢而財源始聽命于下矣今
之鈔法既不可復可不通其變而易之爲
泉布乎鹽法者
國家所以因地之利以代飛輓以充軍實者
也自鈔法廢而餘鹽不輸于官私鹽日益
廣矣今泉布可舉則可不復其
舊制而厚償以收其餘乎謂
宗室爲天潢所宜厚是矣然爵不可降而祿
與時宜在
===
太祖初年已議裁省今法其意而因世以定殺
可也謂社倉爲荒政之義舉是矣然以官
强之則不勝其騷然在昔家給人足興發
自藉令任其便而勿煩其政令可也不但
已也蘇軾所謂三冗其在于今非亾所當
去者乎其曰冗吏非特郡邑佐幕丞使之
微所當裁也由丞幕而上凡中外卿大夫
武廕常侍之屬試職
祖宗之列簿而考之不有所當議乎其曰冗兵
punctuated:
人者也。此法廢，而財源始聽命于下矣。今之鈔法既不可復，可不通其變而易之爲泉布乎？鹽法者，國家所以因地之利，以代飛輓，以充軍實者也。自鈔法廢，而餘鹽不輸于官，私鹽日益廣矣。今泉布可舉，則可不復其舊制，而厚償以收其餘乎？謂宗室爲天潢所宜厚，是矣。然爵不可降，而祿與時宜，在太祖初年已議裁省。今法其意，而因世以定殺，可也。謂社倉爲荒政之義舉，是矣。然以官强之，則不勝其騷然。在昔家給人足，興發自藉，令任其便而勿煩其政令，可也。
不但已也。蘇軾所謂三冗，其在于今非亾所當去者乎？其曰冗吏，非特郡邑佐幕丞使之微所當裁也。由丞幕而上，凡中外卿大夫、武廕常侍之屬，試職祖宗之列簿而考之，不有所當議乎？其曰冗兵，
translation_en:
…other people. Once this system was abolished, control over the sources of revenue began to pass to those below. Since the paper-currency system cannot now be restored, should we not adapt it to changed circumstances and replace it with coinage? The salt system is the means by which the state draws upon the benefits of the land to replace the rapid transport of provisions and replenish military supplies. Since the abolition of the paper-currency system, surplus salt has ceased to be delivered to the authorities, and illicit salt has become increasingly widespread. If coinage can now be put into use, should we not restore the old arrangements and offer generous compensation to collect the surplus salt? It is right to say that members of the imperial clan, as descendants of the imperial line, deserve generous treatment. Yet although their noble ranks cannot be lowered, their stipends should suit the circumstances of the time. Reductions were already discussed in the early years of Taizu’s reign. We may now follow the intent of those measures and determine graduated reductions according to the generation. It is right to say that community granaries are a benevolent undertaking for famine relief. Yet if officials impose them by force, the resulting disturbance becomes unbearable. In former times, households were well provided for and people had enough; the establishment of such granaries drew upon their own resources [?]. It would be appropriate to let people proceed as convenient and avoid troubling them with administrative commands.
Nor is this all. As for what Su Shi called the three redundancies, are there not instances today that ought to be eliminated? By redundant officials, he did not mean that only the minor assistant officials, staff officials, vice magistrates, and commissioners [?] in prefectures and counties should be cut. From vice magistrates and staff officials upward, among all the high officials at court and in the provinces, those holding military appointments through hereditary privilege, and regular attendants, if we were to consult [?] the registers of the imperial ancestors and examine them, would there not be matters deserving deliberation? As for what he called redundant soldiers…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者非特郡國之兵所當抑也內而宿衛之
士外而邊陲之徒試取
國家之尺籍而檢之不有所當汰乎其曰冗
食非特闤闠僭侈不經所當禁也由內外
百司庶府之所需以至于無名徵誅掊克
之所括有不可裁者乎夫如是為之在我
者既以制節謹度不為耗利之端施之在
上者又以導利于民而不為專利之計是
雖不足以給目前一時之急而民富則國
===
不至于獨貧實所以為萬世悠久之利也
此在吾
君吾相一心以為天下而不為自便之圖凡謀
有合于遠大勿嫌于更張言有裨于
社稷勿遺于芻蕘然後君倡羣力之畢集而足
國足民之道或庶幾矣愚生狂瞽之見如
此執事其勿以為迂焉
第五問
戴廷禮
punctuated:
者，非特郡國之兵所當抑也。內而宿衛之士，外而邊陲之徒，試取國家之尺籍而檢之，不有所當汰乎？其曰冗食，非特闤闠僭侈不經所當禁也。由內外百司庶府之所需，以至于無名徵誅、掊克之所括，有不可裁者乎？夫如是為之，在我者既以制節謹度，不為耗利之端；施之在上者，又以導利于民，而不為專利之計。是雖不足以給目前一時之急，而民富則國不至于獨貧，實所以為萬世悠久之利也。此在吾君吾相，一心以為天下，而不為自便之圖。凡謀有合于遠大，勿嫌于更張；言有裨于社稷，勿遺于芻蕘。然後君倡羣力之畢集，而足國足民之道或庶幾矣。愚生狂瞽之見如此，執事其勿以為迂焉！

第五問
戴廷禮
translation_en:
…it is not only the troops of the prefectures and regions whose numbers should be restrained. From the palace guards within to the soldiers on the frontiers without, take up the state's military registers and examine them: are there not some who should be discharged? As for what he calls redundant consumption, it is not only the presumptuous extravagance and improper expenditure of the marketplaces that should be prohibited. From the requirements of the many offices and treasuries in the capital and the provinces, down to what is gathered through unauthorized levies and oppressive extraction, is there anything that cannot be curtailed?

If we proceed in this way, in our own conduct we will exercise restraint and carefully observe due limits, avoiding practices that waste resources; in administering affairs from above, we will direct benefits toward the people rather than devise ways to monopolize them. Although this may not suffice to meet the immediate emergency, if the people are prosperous, the state will not alone be left impoverished. This is truly the means to secure enduring benefit for ten thousand generations.

This depends upon our ruler and our chief ministers devoting themselves single-mindedly to all under Heaven, rather than planning for their own convenience. Whenever a proposal accords with far-reaching aims, let them not object to changing established arrangements; whenever words benefit the altars of soil and grain, let them not disregard them because they come from grass-cutters and wood-gatherers. Then, with the ruler calling forth the combined efforts of all [?], the way to provide adequately for both state and people may perhaps be within reach. Such are this foolish student's rash and unenlightened views. May you, honored examiners, not regard them as impractical!

Fifth Question
Dai Tingli

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭謝　批　〔時論邊事何多竟之無當于用凡以襲浮談無實見也子能考古任將馭兵之〕
〔舊與今儲將足兵之宜起弊振頹切中機要其先天下之憂者乎宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭張　批　〔博古宏才切時確見氣骨之雄偉文詞之藻贍不暇論也佳士佳士〕
考試官學正高　批　〔論馭將兵之道條悉古今籌運終始執此以往邊方足備矣有月中數萬甲兵當於子亦云〕
竊聞易之蠱曰先甲三日後甲三日說者
謂前事將壞當自新以謹其後後事方始
===
當丁寧以監其失夫今之邊事蠱已極矣
所恃自新丁寧以爲善後之謀者必上有
安攘之誠而後法有所主下有負荷之忠
而後治有可圖蓋人情狃于故常而憚於
紛更况法立而行有未善又因以究其所
繇則利害懸焉自非上不規規于因仍下
不屑屑于利害其曷以爲振蠱之永圖哉
夫夷狄之爲中國患雖在盛世能使天地
之平成而不能亡徂征之師能致海內之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭謝批〔時論邊事何多，竟之無當于用，凡以襲浮談、無實見也。子能考古任將馭兵之〕〔舊與今儲將足兵之宜，起弊振頹，切中機要，其先天下之憂者乎！宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭張批〔博古宏才，切時確見，氣骨之雄偉、文詞之藻贍，不暇論也。佳士！佳士！〕
考試官學正高批〔論馭將兵之道，條悉古今，籌運終始。執此以往，邊方足備矣。有月中數萬甲兵，當於子亦云。〕
竊聞《易》之《蠱》曰：「先甲三日，後甲三日。」說者謂：「前事將壞，當自新以謹其後；後事方始，當丁寧以監其失。」夫今之邊事，蠱已極矣。所恃自新丁寧以爲善後之謀者，必上有安攘之誠，而後法有所主；下有負荷之忠，而後治有可圖。蓋人情狃于故常而憚於紛更，况法立而行有未善，又因以究其所繇，則利害懸焉。自非上不規規于因仍，下不屑屑于利害，其曷以爲振蠱之永圖哉？夫夷狄之爲中國患，雖在盛世，能使天地之平成，而不能亡徂征之師；能致海內之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔How much discussion there is nowadays of frontier affairs! Yet in the end [?] it proves of no practical use, entirely because people repeat empty talk and lack substantive insight. You have examined ancient precedents for appointing generals and directing troops〕〔alongside suitable measures today for cultivating a reserve of generals and ensuring sufficient troops. Your proposals remedy abuses and arrest decline, striking precisely at the essentials. Are you not one who worries before all others under Heaven? This deserves to be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Wide knowledge of antiquity, ample talent, and sound insights directly relevant to the times—I have scarcely time to discuss the grandeur of your writing’s spirit and structure or the richness of its language. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕
Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing the way to direct generals and troops, you systematically examine past and present and plan their deployment from beginning to end. Proceeding on this basis, the frontiers could be adequately defended. “Having tens of thousands of armored troops within the moon” [?]—this saying should apply to you as well.〕
I have humbly heard that the Book of Changes, in the hexagram Gu (Decay), says: “Three days before jia; three days after jia.” Commentators explain: “When an earlier undertaking is about to fall into decay, one should renew oneself so as to exercise care over what follows; when a subsequent undertaking is just beginning, one should issue earnest admonitions so as to guard against errors.” Now decay in our frontier affairs has already reached its utmost extent. If we are to rely on renewal and earnest admonition to devise measures for setting matters right, those above must sincerely intend to secure peace within and repel threats without; only then will policies have a guiding purpose. Those below must loyally shoulder their responsibilities; only then can good government be sought. Human nature is accustomed to established routines and recoils from repeated changes. Moreover, when a policy has been established but its implementation remains imperfect, further investigation into the causes brings interests and harms into the balance. Unless those above cease clinging narrowly to inherited practices and those below cease preoccupying themselves with personal advantage and disadvantage, how can a lasting plan be made to remedy decay?
As for the troubles that the Yi and Di peoples cause the Central Realm, even in an age of flourishing rule one may bring Heaven and Earth into harmony yet still be unable to dispense with armies sent on campaigns; one may bring all within the seas to…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
嚮風而不能亡蒋代之役其所賴以爲克
敵制勝之本者寧有要于兵將哉在昔文
武一而已矣無事則將歸卿列有事則卿
莅戎行故召虎以文德而平淮夷方叔以
元老而征荊蠻無專將也兵農一而已矣
居常則負耒而耕遇變則荷戈而戰故居
有積倉行有裹糧無養兵之費也厥後有
智將賢將儒將才將千萬人之將所貴乎
求之廣者世胄可使也而穰苴以典司馬
===
因罄可使也而夷吾以佐九合仇讎可使
也而雍齒封于列侯行伍可使也而李廣
起于都尉良家子可使也而奉世拜以光
祿亡命可使也而馬援授以大中俘虜可
使也而敬德納于幕下武科可使也而子
儀薦位中令老可使也而非熊以之興周
稚可使也而甘羅以之佐秦吏可使也而
蕭何拜以相漢儒可使也而馮異封以應
國貧可使也而齊王起于淮陰賤可使也
punctuated: 嚮風而不能亡蒋代之役，其所賴以爲克敵制勝之本者，寧有要于兵將哉？在昔文武一而已矣，無事則將歸卿列，有事則卿莅戎行，故召虎以文德而平淮夷，方叔以元老而征荊蠻，無專將也。兵農一而已矣，居常則負耒而耕，遇變則荷戈而戰，故居有積倉，行有裹糧，無養兵之費也。厥後有智將、賢將、儒將、才將、千萬人之將，所貴乎求之廣者，世胄可使也，而穰苴以典司馬；因罄可使也，而夷吾以佐九合；仇讎可使也，而雍齒封于列侯；行伍可使也，而李廣起于都尉；良家子可使也，而奉世拜以光祿；亡命可使也，而馬援授以大中；俘虜可使也，而敬德納于幕下；武科可使也，而子儀薦位中令；老可使也，而非熊以之興周；稚可使也，而甘羅以之佐秦；吏可使也，而蕭何拜以相漢；儒可使也，而馮異封以應國；貧可使也，而齊王起于淮陰；賤可使也，
translation_en:
…to turn toward their civilizing influence, yet could not dispense with military campaigns [?]. As for the foundation on which they relied to defeat the enemy and secure victory, could anything be more essential than soldiers and generals? In antiquity, civil and military service were one. When there was no trouble, generals returned to the ranks of the ministers; when trouble arose, ministers took charge of the armies. Thus Shao Hu pacified the Huai Yi through civil virtue, and Fang Shu, as a senior statesman, campaigned against the Jing Man. There were no exclusively military commanders. Soldiers and farmers were likewise one. In ordinary times they carried ploughs and cultivated the fields; when disturbances arose, they shouldered weapons and fought. Thus, at home they had grain stored in granaries, and on the march they carried provisions. There was no expense for maintaining a standing army.

In later ages there were wise generals, worthy generals, scholarly generals, capable generals, and generals commanding thousands or tens of thousands. What mattered was to seek them widely. Men of hereditary lineage could be employed: Rangju was accordingly put in charge as Minister of War. Prisoners [?] could be employed: Yiwu accordingly assisted in the nine assemblies of the lords. Enemies could be employed: Yong Chi was enfeoffed among the ranked marquises. Men from the ranks could be employed: Li Guang rose to become a Commandant. Sons of respectable families could be employed: Fengshi was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Fugitives could be employed: Ma Yuan was appointed Grand Master of the Palace [?]. Captives could be employed: Jingde was taken onto the commander's staff. Graduates of the military examinations could be employed: Ziyi rose through successive promotions to Director of the Secretariat. The old could be employed: Feixiong thereby brought about the rise of Zhou. The young could be employed: Gan Luo thereby assisted Qin. Clerks could be employed: Xiao He was appointed to serve as Chancellor of Han. Scholars could be employed: Feng Yi was enfeoffed with the domain of Ying [?]. The poor could be employed: the King of Qi rose from Huaiyin. The lowly could be employed …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而衛青發于人奴凡所以求之者不旣廣
乎然求之旣廣而任之不專則亞夫以抗
命疎何以平七國之反郭進以誣訟棄何
以釋北顧之憂任專矣而儲之不豫緩急
將何賴焉故霍去病之以侍中甘延壽之
以羽林郎皆其所嘗試而素識者也此古
之所以任將者則然耳而所以駕馭倡導
之術不存焉至于兵之爲制有六軍三軍
二軍一軍之分初皆自爲之食至漢之三
===
變唐之三變以及民兵募兵義勇之設而
其食皆仰給于官矣歷代所以優其養者
鹽筴可資也而管仲以富青齊轉漕可資
也而相國以給關中入粟可資也而鼂錯
以實塞下屯種可資也而充國以成金城
委積可資也而食其以守成臯市租可資
也而魏尚以給雲中田稅可資也而寇恂
以移屬縣糴粟可資也而耿中丞以給湟
中貿易可資也而張詠以給益州充羡可
punctuated:
而衛青發于人奴。凡所以求之者，不旣廣乎？然求之旣廣，而任之不專，則亞夫以抗命疎，何以平七國之反？郭進以誣訟棄，何以釋北顧之憂？任專矣，而儲之不豫，緩急將何賴焉？故霍去病之以侍中、甘延壽之以羽林郎，皆其所嘗試而素識者也。此古之所以任將者則然耳，而所以駕馭倡導之術不存焉。
至于兵之爲制，有六軍、三軍、二軍、一軍之分，初皆自爲之食。至漢之三變、唐之三變，以及民兵、募兵、義勇之設，而其食皆仰給于官矣。歷代所以優其養者，鹽筴可資也，而管仲以富青齊；轉漕可資也，而相國以給關中；入粟可資也，而鼂錯以實塞下；屯種可資也，而充國以成金城；委積可資也，而食其以守成臯；市租可資也，而魏尚以給雲中；田稅可資也，而寇恂以移屬縣；糴粟可資也，而耿中丞以給湟中；貿易可資也，而張詠以給益州；充羡可
translation_en:
…and Wei Qing rose from slavery. Were not the means of seeking such men broad indeed? Yet if the search is broad but commanders are not entrusted with sole authority—if Yafu is estranged for resisting orders—how could the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms be quelled? If Guo Jin is dismissed because of false accusations, how could anxiety over the northern frontier be relieved? Even if commanders are entrusted with sole authority, unless men have been prepared in reserve beforehand, on whom can one rely in an emergency? Thus Huo Qubing, serving as Palace Attendant, and Gan Yanshou, serving as Gentleman of the Feathered Forest Guard, were both men whose abilities had already been tested and long known. Such were the ways in which the ancients appointed commanders; the techniques for controlling, encouraging, and guiding them are not included here.
As for military organization, there were distinctions between six armies, three armies, two armies, and one army. Initially, all provided their own food. With the three transformations under the Han and the three under the Tang, and the establishment of militia, recruited troops, and volunteer forces, however, their provisions came entirely from the government. Successive dynasties provided generously for their maintenance in various ways. Salt revenues could be drawn upon: Guan Zhong used them to enrich Qing and Qi. Grain transport could be drawn upon: the Chancellor used it to supply Guanzhong. Contributions of grain could be drawn upon: Chao Cuo used them to fill the frontier stores. Military agricultural colonies could be drawn upon: Chongguo used them to secure Jincheng. Stockpiled provisions could be drawn upon: Yiji used them to hold Chenggao. Market taxes could be drawn upon: Wei Shang used them to supply Yunzhong. Land taxes could be drawn upon: Kou Xun used them to make transfers to subordinate counties. Grain purchases could be drawn upon: Vice Censor-in-Chief Geng used them to supply Huangzhong. Trade could be drawn upon: Zhang Yong used it to supply Yizhou. Surplus funds could …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
資也而左藏以發饑饉錦綺可資也而慶
曆歲出百萬珍珠可資也而寶元以市軍
儲進獻可資也而許玄豹以充邊餉中禁
可資也而內侍省以贍軍旅凡所以養之
者不既厚乎然養之既厚而擇之不精則
車下虎士何以勝合淝之役丹陽青巾何
以收陷堅之功選精矣而練之不熟則節
制將安恃焉故春夏舉以蒐苗秋冬舉以
獮狩皆所以振旅而服習者也此古之馭
===
兵者則然耳而所以推赤感動之道不存
焉要之將者兵之統兵者將之衛均之所
當重也而將爲要蓋天下無必勝之兵而
有不可敗之將不然李信以二十萬而不
勝王翦以六十萬而勝獨非秦士哉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝應天順人闢
乾坤于腥穢之餘而漠北一掃我
成祖文皇帝靖難定鼎揭
punctuated:
資也，而左藏以發饑饉；錦綺可資也，而慶曆歲出百萬；珍珠可資也，而寶元以市軍儲；進獻可資也，而許玄豹以充邊餉；中禁可資也，而內侍省以贍軍旅。凡所以養之者，不既厚乎？然養之既厚，而擇之不精，則車下虎士何以勝合淝之役？丹陽青巾何以收陷堅之功？選精矣，而練之不熟，則節制將安恃焉？故春夏舉以蒐苗，秋冬舉以獮狩，皆所以振旅而服習者也。此古之馭兵者則然耳，而所以推赤感動之道不存焉。要之，將者兵之統，兵者將之衛，均之所當重也，而將爲要。蓋天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將。不然，李信以二十萬而不勝，王翦以六十萬而勝，獨非秦士哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝應天順人，闢乾坤于腥穢之餘，而漠北一掃。我成祖文皇帝靖難定鼎，揭
translation_en:
…could also provide resources, and the Left Treasury disbursed funds to relieve famine. Brocades and figured silks could provide resources, and during the Qingli reign period a million were issued annually. Pearls could provide resources, and during the Baoyuan reign period they were used to purchase military supplies. Offerings presented to the throne could provide resources, and Xu Xuanbao [?] used them to replenish provisions for the frontier troops. The inner palace could provide resources, and the Palace Domestic Service supported the armies. Were not all these means of sustaining the troops already generous? Yet if their support was generous but their selection insufficiently exacting, how could the fierce warriors serving beneath the commander's carriage have won the battle of Hefei? How could the blue-turbaned troops of Danyang have achieved the feat of breaching strong positions? Even if the men selected were excellent, if their training was not thorough, what could be relied upon to maintain command and discipline? Thus troops were mustered for the spring and summer hunts, sou and miao, and for the autumn and winter hunts, xian and shou. All these served to marshal the troops and give them practice. Such, however, were merely the methods by which the ancients controlled soldiers; the way of extending heartfelt sincerity to move them was absent. In essence, the general commands the soldiers, and the soldiers protect the general. Both must be valued, but the general is the crucial element. For there are no armies in the world certain to win, yet there are generals who cannot be defeated. Otherwise, when Li Xin failed with two hundred thousand men and Wang Jian succeeded with six hundred thousand, were not both armies made up of soldiers of Qin?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao responded to Heaven and accorded with the people, opening up Heaven and Earth amid the remnants of foul corruption and sweeping clean the lands north of the desert. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen quelled the disturbances and established the seat of rule, raising …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
日月于繼明之後而虜庭三犁當時所以鼓舞
一世之豪傑綱維仁義之師旅固非特比
跡湯武而已我
列聖相承撫者定之業際亨嘉之運歸馬放牛
韜弓戢戈武備之不講久矣狂虜抵隙投
間非特肆侮寧一朝一夕之故哉頃歲東
潰薊垣西蹦鴈代焚戮之慘致厪
九重西顧之憂于是
詔下廷臣上陳經略之方又
===
遣使行邊以求邊臣所不敢言所不能爲之
事一時條具封事凡馭將論兵之策誠有
如執事所云者及輔臣陳
大閱之典以爲積弊之餘非
聖天子躬率于其上不足以爲多方之表我
皇上欣然嘉納乃
躬御戎服
親駕六飛率勳戚大小臣工以講武事殆遠追
瞻洛之盛而陋馳射上林于不足言矣風
punctuated: 日月于繼明之後，而虜庭三犁。當時所以鼓舞一世之豪傑，綱維仁義之師旅，固非特比跡湯武而已。我列聖相承，撫者定之業，際亨嘉之運，歸馬放牛，韜弓戢戈，武備之不講久矣。狂虜抵隙投間，非特肆侮，寧一朝一夕之故哉？頃歲東潰薊垣，西蹦鴈代，焚戮之慘，致厪九重西顧之憂。于是詔下廷臣，上陳經略之方，又遣使行邊，以求邊臣所不敢言、所不能爲之事。一時條具封事，凡馭將論兵之策，誠有如執事所云者。及輔臣陳大閱之典，以爲積弊之餘，非聖天子躬率于其上，不足以爲多方之表。我皇上欣然嘉納，乃躬御戎服，親駕六飛，率勳戚大小臣工，以講武事。殆遠追瞻洛之盛，而陋馳射上林于不足言矣。風
translation_en: …the sun and moon following the succession to enlightened rule, and thrice plowed through the enemy’s court. The means by which he then inspired the outstanding men of an entire age and held together armies of benevolence and righteousness certainly did more than merely match the achievements of Tang and Wu. Our successive sage sovereigns inherited the established work of pacification [?] and encountered an age of prosperity and auspicious concord. Horses were returned to pasture and oxen released; bows were sheathed and weapons put away. Military preparedness has long gone unattended. The reckless northern foes have exploited gaps and seized opportunities, going beyond mere insolence. Could this situation have arisen in a single morning or evening? In recent years, defenses collapsed in the east at Ji, while in the west Yan and Dai were breached [?]. The horrors of burning and slaughter caused His Majesty, within the innermost palace, anxious concern as he looked westward. An edict therefore instructed the court officials to submit proposals for strategic management. Envoys were also dispatched to inspect the frontier and seek out matters that frontier officials dared not speak of or were unable to undertake. For a time, sealed memorials presented itemized proposals; among their plans for managing commanders and discussing military affairs, there were indeed proposals such as you have mentioned. Then the grand secretaries proposed the ceremony of a grand military review, arguing that, after so many accumulated abuses, only the Sage Son of Heaven’s personal leadership from above could provide a model for all regions. Our Emperor gladly approved and accepted this proposal. He personally donned military dress and rode in his six-horse imperial carriage, leading the nobles of hereditary merit, imperial relatives, and officials of every rank in military exercises. This surely recalled the ancient splendor of the royal inspection at Luo, making mounted archery in Shanglin Park seem too insignificant even to mention. The influence…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聲所感固宜將懷敵愾之心士增踴躍之
氣內有以銷奸宄之萌外有以落腥膻之
膽而廓清之績乃猶未見焉無亦因襲之
弊未易卒更乎夫以虜之爲患昔也止于
秋防今四時並禦矣昔間數歲一犯今歲
以爲常矣昔止于野掠未攻堡也今不特
攻堡而攻州郡矣昔所得止于芻畜布帛
今則寶玉綺繡無所不掠矣大入則大利
小入則小利未聞一遭挫焉竊恐犬羊之
===
性易逞而谿壑之欲未艾其或妄肆䖵茹
則可慮孰大于是哉顧吾所以禦之者尚
復狃于故常而無肯能任其責其諸病者
日損月削坐視其困而莫一投劑焉此賈
生所謂可爲長太息者也自愚言之欲捄
弊者不可不窮其源欲證今者不可不求
諸古以言乎馭將古者推轂而寄以閫外
授劒而許以副將今之將有不行于士矣
矧偏裨乎古者將有便宜置吏收市租于
punctuated:
聲所感，固宜將懷敵愾之心，士增踴躍之氣，內有以銷奸宄之萌，外有以落腥膻之膽，而廓清之績乃猶未見焉。無亦因襲之弊未易卒更乎？夫以虜之爲患，昔也止于秋防，今四時並禦矣；昔間數歲一犯，今歲以爲常矣；昔止于野掠，未攻堡也，今不特攻堡而攻州郡矣；昔所得止于芻畜布帛，今則寶玉綺繡無所不掠矣。大入則大利，小入則小利，未聞一遭挫焉。竊恐犬羊之性易逞，而谿壑之欲未艾，其或妄肆䖵茹，則可慮孰大于是哉？顧吾所以禦之者，尚復狃于故常，而無肯能任其責。其諸病者日損月削，坐視其困，而莫一投劑焉，此賈生所謂可爲長太息者也。
自愚言之，欲捄弊者不可不窮其源，欲證今者不可不求諸古。以言乎馭將，古者推轂而寄以閫外，授劒而許以副將；今之將有不行于士矣，矧偏裨乎？古者將有便宜置吏，收市租于
translation_en:
…under the influence of this example, commanders should surely cherish the resolve to confront the enemy, and soldiers grow more eager for action. Within, it should extinguish the beginnings of treachery and disorder; without, it should strike terror into those rank-smelling barbarians. Yet achievements in clearing away the enemy have still not appeared. Is this perhaps because the abuses perpetuated by habitual practice cannot readily be changed all at once? As for the trouble caused by these raiders, formerly defense was needed only in autumn; now they must be resisted in all four seasons. Formerly they invaded once every few years; now invasion is an annual occurrence. Formerly they merely plundered the countryside without attacking forts; now they attack not only forts but prefectures and counties as well. Formerly their booty consisted only of fodder, livestock, cloth, and silk; now they plunder everything, including precious stones, jade, patterned silks, and embroideries. A major incursion brings them great profit, and a minor incursion brings them lesser profit; we have never heard of their suffering even a single reverse. I fear that their dog-and-sheep nature is easily indulged, while their appetite, as bottomless as a ravine, remains unsated. If they should recklessly give free rein to their devouring [?], what could be more alarming?
Yet our methods of resisting them remain bound by accustomed practice, and no one is both willing and able to shoulder the responsibility. It is as though a sick person were wasting away day after day and month after month, while we sat watching his distress without administering a single dose of medicine. This is what Master Jia called grounds for a long, deep sigh.
In my humble view, anyone wishing to remedy abuses must trace them to their source, and anyone wishing to assess the present must seek guidance in antiquity. To speak of directing commanders: in antiquity, the ruler pushed the wheels of a departing commander's carriage and entrusted him with affairs beyond the capital's gates; he bestowed a sword and granted authority over deputy commanders [?]. Today's commanders sometimes cannot make their authority effective even among the rank and file, much less among subordinate commanders! In antiquity, commanders had discretionary authority to appoint subordinate officials and collect market taxes in…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
幕府不問所出矣今稽餉之使交馳于道
矣况置吏乎古有軍中不奉詔而天子按
轡者今事機在邊陲而文法由中制矣古
有日擊牛饗士而大破匈奴者今不以爲
玩愒則咎以靡費矣古者賞不踰時罪疑
惟輕本以示勸也今經歲而功罪不決可
乎古有終日鞭七人貫三人耳而知敗有
試以婦人寵臣而知成今之教習有是嚴
焉否耶古有十六年而屯青州十七年而
===
守關西今之任將有是久焉否耶今之督
撫非古卿士脩我戎乎旣命以節制一方
矣爲其可信也乃功罪不信以爲功罪必
察焉出納不信以爲出納必察焉古郡守
之不如是猶貿而已矣夫以馭將之道寢
不如古而欲求功業之無前胡可得哉以
言乎馭兵古者天子之于戍士出則歌采
薇以遣之歸則歌杕杜以勞之今且不恤
于有司矣安望其上優于
punctuated:
幕府，不問所出矣。今稽餉之使交馳于道矣，况置吏乎？古有軍中不奉詔而天子按轡者，今事機在邊陲而文法由中制矣。古有日擊牛饗士而大破匈奴者，今不以爲玩愒，則咎以靡費矣。古者賞不踰時，罪疑惟輕，本以示勸也。今經歲而功罪不決，可乎？古有終日鞭七人、貫三人耳而知敗，有試以婦人寵臣而知成，今之教習有是嚴焉否耶？古有十六年而屯青州、十七年而守關西，今之任將有是久焉否耶？今之督撫，非古卿士脩我戎乎？旣命以節制一方矣，爲其可信也。乃功罪不信，以爲功罪必察焉；出納不信，以爲出納必察焉。古郡守之不如，是猶貿而已矣。夫以馭將之道寢不如古，而欲求功業之無前，胡可得哉？
以言乎馭兵，古者天子之于戍士，出則歌《采薇》以遣之，歸則歌《杕杜》以勞之。今且不恤于有司矣，安望其上優于
translation_en:
…the military headquarters, without being questioned about the source of the revenues. Now envoys inspecting military provisions pass one another in haste along the roads; how much less could a commander appoint his own officers? In antiquity there were commanders who declined to obey an imperial command within their camps, and the Son of Heaven reined in his horse. Now the critical circumstances are on the frontier, but documentary procedures and regulations are dictated from the center. In antiquity there were commanders who slaughtered cattle daily to feast their soldiers and then inflicted great defeats on the Xiongnu. Today such conduct, if not condemned as idle indulgence, would be blamed as extravagance. In antiquity rewards were not delayed beyond their proper time, and doubtful offenses received lighter penalties: the purpose was to encourage men. Can it be acceptable now to let a year pass without settling questions of merit and guilt? In antiquity there was a case in which defeat could be foreseen from a commander’s flogging seven men and piercing the ears of three over the course of a day; there were also cases in which success could be foreseen from trials involving women and favored courtiers. Is military training today so strict? In antiquity there were commanders stationed in Qingzhou for sixteen years and guarding Guanxi for seventeen. Are commanders today retained in their posts for so long? Are today’s supreme commanders and grand coordinators not like the high ministers of antiquity who “put our forces in order”? They have already been entrusted with military authority over a region because they are considered trustworthy. Yet their judgments of merit and guilt are distrusted, on the grounds that these must invariably be investigated; their receipts and disbursements are distrusted, on the grounds that these too must invariably be investigated. They are accorded less trust than the commandery governors of antiquity: this is simply muddleheadedness [?]. When our methods of directing generals grow ever inferior to those of antiquity, how can we hope to achieve deeds without precedent?
As for directing soldiers, in antiquity, when the Son of Heaven sent garrison soldiers out, “Gathering Ferns” (Cai wei) was sung to see them off; when they returned, “The Solitary Pear Tree” (Di du) was sung to honor their service. Today they receive no care even from the responsible officials. How can they hope for generous treatment higher up, at…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝乎古將帥之于士卒未食不先飯未臥不
先寢今視之如犬馬矣安望其共甘苦乎
古士飽馬騰而後可以利戰今一斛之粟
將不免于枵腹矣古畏我而不畏敵今紀
律亡素退則有生之望矣古者秦以銳士
强齊以技擊勝今則有不辨金鼓之節幟
文之度矣可乎古者帶甲千人則有明習
占候通曉夷情扛鼎超關健步巧詞可爲
先鋒嚮諜者今之部曲動以萬計不知備
===
此數者否耶古有養以國士則報以國士
養以衆人則報以衆人今則一切視之且
無選鋒之養矣而一旦臨敵不知有能奮
勇前驅否耶入衛之兵非延寧之勁卒乎
然千里裹甲經歲始還困敝憔悴人所共
知而徒以憚其撤兵之嫌無肯力任其責
而主之者是土苴而已矣夫以馭兵之道
寖不如古而欲求安攘之攸賴胡可得哉
此
punctuated: 朝乎？古將帥之于士卒，未食不先飯，未臥不先寢。今視之如犬馬矣，安望其共甘苦乎？古士飽馬騰而後可以利戰，今一斛之粟，將不免于枵腹矣。古畏我而不畏敵，今紀律亡素，退則有生之望矣。古者秦以銳士强，齊以技擊勝，今則有不辨金鼓之節、幟文之度矣，可乎？古者帶甲千人，則有明習占候、通曉夷情、扛鼎超關、健步巧詞，可爲先鋒嚮諜者。今之部曲，動以萬計，不知備此數者否耶？古有養以國士則報以國士，養以衆人則報以衆人。今則一切視之，且無選鋒之養矣，而一旦臨敵，不知有能奮勇前驅否耶？入衛之兵，非延寧之勁卒乎？然千里裹甲，經歲始還，困敝憔悴，人所共知，而徒以憚其撤兵之嫌，無肯力任其責而主之者，是土苴而已矣。夫以馭兵之道，寖不如古，而欲求安攘之攸賴，胡可得哉？此
translation_en: …at court? In antiquity, generals would not eat before their soldiers had eaten, nor sleep before their soldiers had lain down. Today they treat them like dogs and horses: how can one expect them to share hardship and comfort? In antiquity, only when the soldiers were well fed and the horses vigorous could they fight to advantage. Today, even with a hu of grain, the soldiers will still be unable to escape empty bellies. In antiquity, soldiers feared their own commanders rather than the enemy. Today, discipline has not been established through regular practice, and retreat offers hope of survival. In antiquity, Qin grew strong through its picked troops, and Qi prevailed through its skilled fighters. Today there are even men who cannot distinguish the signals of gongs and drums or the prescribed markings of banners. Can this be acceptable? In antiquity, among a thousand armored soldiers there would be men well versed in divination and the observation of signs, thoroughly familiar with the circumstances of foreign peoples, able to lift tripods and leap barriers, swift of foot and clever of speech—men fit to serve as vanguard troops, guides, and spies. Today, military units readily number in the tens of thousands; I wonder whether they possess men with these several abilities. In antiquity, those supported as outstanding men of the realm would repay their patrons as outstanding men of the realm; those supported as ordinary men would repay them as ordinary men. Today, all are treated alike, and there is not even special provision for picked assault troops. When suddenly confronted with the enemy, I wonder whether any can courageously press forward into the van. Are the troops brought in for the capital’s defense not the stalwart soldiers of Yan and Ning? Yet they carry their armor a thousand li and return only after a year has passed. Their exhaustion and emaciation are known to all. Merely from fear of incurring blame for withdrawing troops, however, no one is willing to shoulder the responsibility and take charge of the matter. This is simply to treat them as worthless refuse. With methods of commanding soldiers growing ever inferior to those of antiquity, how can one hope to secure a dependable means of maintaining peace within and repelling enemies without? This…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
明諭所謂邊臣不敢言不能爲之事意者其在
兹乎或曰將必試戰而後可知也其誰與
儲今內地衛士且分番以戍邊矣則中外
百夫長以上可無分番習戰于諸邊之慕
乎或曰客兵尚不足用也而撤之其誰與
防今土著之兵視客兵旣不侔矣則附邊
州縣可無易而爲衛所抽之以分戍乎雖
然儲將足兵固所以爲振蠱之圖而其要
尤莫切于理財其本尤莫先于務實善乎
宋臣蘇轍有言曰苟無其財雖聖賢不能
自致于跬步苟有其財雖庸人可以一日
而千里方今
===
聖天子賢寧執圖夜圖惟化理所以爲籌邊之
計者可謂有務實之心矣乃司事者可不
思爲體
國之忠而應之以實乎愚生密邇邊陲竊嘗
有概于中而不能以自達敢僭言之以爲
明問復
punctuated: 明諭所謂邊臣不敢言、不能爲之事，意者其在兹乎？或曰：「將必試戰而後可知也，其誰與儲？」今內地衛士且分番以戍邊矣，則中外百夫長以上，可無分番習戰于諸邊之慕乎？或曰：「客兵尚不足用也，而撤之，其誰與防？」今土著之兵視客兵旣不侔矣，則附邊州縣可無易而爲衛所，抽之以分戍乎？雖然，儲將足兵固所以爲振蠱之圖，而其要尤莫切于理財，其本尤莫先于務實。善乎，宋臣蘇轍有言曰：「苟無其財，雖聖賢不能自致于跬步；苟有其財，雖庸人可以一日而千里。」方今聖天子賢寧執圖夜圖，惟化理，所以爲籌邊之計者，可謂有務實之心矣。乃司事者可不思爲體國之忠，而應之以實乎？愚生密邇邊陲，竊嘗有概于中，而不能以自達，敢僭言之，以爲明問復。
translation_en:
…might this be what the enlightened instruction means by matters that frontier officials dare not speak of and cannot carry out? Some may say: “A commander’s abilities can be known only after he has been tested in battle. Whom, then, can we hold in reserve?” Now even guardsmen from the interior take turns serving on the frontier. Should there not, then, be a plan [?] for officers commanding a hundred men and above, both within and outside the capital, to take turns gaining combat experience along the various frontiers? Some may say: “Even the troops brought in from elsewhere are insufficient. If they are withdrawn, who will defend the frontier?” Yet the treatment of locally settled troops already differs from that of troops brought in from elsewhere. Could not the subprefectures and counties adjoining the frontier be converted into guards and battalions, and men drawn from them for garrison duty at different posts?

Nevertheless, maintaining a reserve of commanders and ensuring sufficient troops are certainly means of remedying decay, but nothing is more urgently essential than managing finances, and nothing takes greater precedence as their foundation than attending to practical realities. Well did the Song official Su Zhe say: “Without financial resources, even sages and worthies cannot advance half a pace; with financial resources, even an ordinary person can cover a thousand li in a day.” Today our sage Son of Heaven attends to governance and good order—the preceding wording, 賢寧執圖夜圖, is unclear [?]—and his plans for the frontier may indeed be said to reflect a commitment to practical realities. Should not those responsible for these affairs therefore seek to show loyalty by making the concerns of the state their own, and respond with substantive action?

I, an unworthy student, live very near the frontier. I have long felt deep concern within, yet have been unable to make my views heard. I venture presumptuously to set them forth in reply to your enlightened question.

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
隆慶四年秋八月陝西當大
比所部士維時廵按監察御
史郭〔庭梧〕祗率百司共服厥
役綜理內外纖悉周毖始七
日癸卯鎖院越甲子告竣事
凡二十有二日御史躬執扃
鑰蚤夜罔或暇逸錄成將報
之
===
天府〔師載〕得有言于後用諗厥多
士曰〔師載〕不敏竊聞之虞庭
納言必試功而後庸周官言
揚必任事而後祿夫言之不
易取在盛世已然矣今〔師載〕
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

隆慶四年秋八月，陝西當大比所部士。維時廵按監察御史郭〔庭梧〕祗率百司，共服厥役，綜理內外，纖悉周毖。始七日癸卯鎖院，越甲子告竣事，凡二十有二日。御史躬執扃鑰，蚤夜罔或暇逸。錄成，將報之天府，〔師載〕得有言于後，用諗厥多士曰：「〔師載〕不敏，竊聞之，虞庭納言，必試功而後庸；周官言揚，必任事而後祿。夫言之不易取，在盛世已然矣。今〔師載〕
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the fourth year of Longqing (1570), Shaanxi was due to hold the triennial examination for the scholars under its jurisdiction. At that time, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Guo Tingwu, respectfully led the various officials in carrying out their duties, overseeing affairs within and without, with meticulous care for every detail. The examination compound was sealed on the seventh day, guimao, and proceedings were declared complete on jiazi, twenty-two days in all. The Censor personally held the keys to the gates, allowing himself no leisure or ease, early or late. Once the record was completed and was about to be submitted to the imperial repository, I, Shizai, was given the opportunity to append some words, with which to address the assembled scholars:

“I, Shizai, am untalented, but have heard that when the court of Yu accepted a man's words, it first tested his accomplishments before employing him; and under the Offices of Zhou, when a man was recommended for his words, he first had to undertake duties before receiving a stipend. Thus, even in ages of flourishing government, men were not readily accepted on their words alone. Now I, Shizai, …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所爲試爾與爾所自爲見揚
旣咸惟其言而所謂功與事
者又在爾多士他日非吾所
能與焉〔師〕〔載〕 曷言哉矧茲西
土山川炳靈古帝王所更居
賢喆挺出歷我
明二百有餘歲道化旁浹人文宣
===
朗士生其間涵育漸被策動
茂實以淩軼前碩自制科以
還章章明備〔師〕〔載〕 又何言哉
雖然事有出于習見而可以
相證者君子恒藉以反觀焉
請以余道途所感藉以爲諭
可乎始余之發渭水也屬時
punctuated:
所爲試爾與爾所自爲見揚，旣咸惟其言，而所謂功與事者，又在爾多士他日，非吾所能與焉。〔師〕〔載〕曷言哉？矧茲西土，山川炳靈，古帝王所更居，賢喆挺出。歷我明二百有餘歲，道化旁浹，人文宣朗。士生其間，涵育漸被，策動茂實，以淩軼前碩，自制科以還，章章明備。〔師〕〔載〕又何言哉？

雖然，事有出于習見而可以相證者，君子恒藉以反觀焉。請以余道途所感，藉以爲諭，可乎？始余之發渭水也，屬時
translation_en:
…what I use to examine you and what you yourselves use to gain recognition both depend entirely on words. As for the achievements and practical service just mentioned, these await you scholars in the days to come; they are not matters in which I can take part. What can I, Shizai, say? Moreover, here in this western land, the mountains and rivers manifest their numinous powers. Ancient emperors and kings dwelt here in succession, and worthy and wise men have risen preeminent. Throughout the more than two hundred years of our Ming dynasty, moral transformation has spread everywhere, and literary culture has shone brightly. Scholars born here, nurtured and gradually imbued with these influences, have spurred themselves to substantial accomplishments, surpassing the eminent scholars of earlier times. Since the establishment of the examination system, clear and abundant evidence of this has been manifest. What more can I, Shizai, say?

Nevertheless, familiar occurrences can serve to illuminate other matters, and the gentleman constantly draws on them to examine himself. May I take what struck me on my journey and use it as an illustration? When I first set out from the Wei River, it was a time when…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
秋陽歒烈鬱暑蒸炎塵囂紛
沓縈紆閃爍求片雲之覆一
雹清澍不可得也迨膏車叩
關西南望見終南太白之巔
煙嵐四塞觸石蓬起竊心欣
然以為將雨之候也少焉飄
飄掀揭而杲然日出矣詰朝
===
渡潼津跋華山之麓褰帷四
望其雲猶是也已而頹颩怒
號冰雹蕩薄脫木偃禾惟民
之災又明日顧瞻豐原雲峯
千疊氤氳瀰漫余為此懼方
將戒徒疾馳而霡霂漸零寔
稱甘霖嗟乎天下事幻化曷
punctuated: 秋陽歒烈，鬱暑蒸炎，塵囂紛沓，縈紆閃爍，求片雲之覆、一雹清澍不可得也。迨膏車叩關，西南望見終南太白之巔，煙嵐四塞，觸石蓬起，竊心欣然，以為將雨之候也。少焉，飄飄掀揭，而杲然日出矣。詰朝渡潼津，跋華山之麓，褰帷四望，其雲猶是也。已而頹颩怒號，冰雹蕩薄，脫木偃禾，惟民之災。又明日，顧瞻豐原，雲峯千疊，氤氳瀰漫，余為此懼，方將戒徒疾馳，而霡霂漸零，寔稱甘霖。嗟乎！天下事幻化曷
translation_en:
…the autumn sun blazed fiercely [?]; oppressive heat steamed and seethed, while dust and tumult crowded upon us, swirling and shimmering. Not even the shelter of a scrap of cloud or a single refreshing shower [?] could be had. When we had greased the carriage and reached the pass, I looked southwest and saw the summits of Zhongnan and Taibai. Mist and mountain vapors filled every quarter, billowing up where they touched the rocks. Inwardly delighted, I took this as a sign of impending rain. Before long, however, they drifted and lifted away, and the sun emerged shining brightly.

The following morning, we crossed the Tong ford and traversed the foot of Mount Hua. Raising the carriage curtain and looking in every direction, I saw clouds just as before. Soon violent gusts roared furiously, and hail swept and battered everything, stripping the trees and flattening the grain—a calamity for the people. The next day, looking toward Fengyuan, I saw clouds piled like peaks in a thousand layers, their vapors spreading everywhere. This frightened me. Just as I was about to order my attendants to hurry onward, a fine rain began gradually to fall: this truly deserved to be called a welcome rain. Alas! The affairs of the world shift and change—how…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
常疑信亡從獨雲乎哉易曰
雲從龍京房易飛候占曰西
方有大雲五色下有賢人甚
矣雲之象類吾賢也抑余又
聞終南太白盤亙西極崑崙
爾多士非鍾諸山之秀而毓
者耶始余讀子所爲文見其
===
詞鋒絢爛耀然奪目者則以
爲景雲敷華揚采郁郁紛紛
者則以爲卿雲磅礴雄渾一
瀉千里者則以爲有渰之雲
至和所發縱横昭回足以爲
文治之光者則以爲慶雲紆
徐龐雅潤澤春容者則以爲
punctuated: 常？疑信亡從，獨雲乎哉？《易》曰：「雲從龍。」京房《易飛候占》曰：「西方有大雲，五色，下有賢人。」甚矣，雲之象類吾賢也！抑余又聞終南、太白盤亙，西極崑崙，爾多士非鍾諸山之秀而毓者耶？始余讀子所爲文，見其詞鋒絢爛、耀然奪目者，則以爲景雲；敷華揚采、郁郁紛紛者，則以爲卿雲；磅礴雄渾、一瀉千里者，則以爲有渰之雲；至和所發、縱横昭回、足以爲文治之光者，則以爲慶雲；紆徐龐雅、潤澤春容者，則以爲
translation_en:
…ever constant? With nothing to guide doubt or belief, can this be true of clouds alone? The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon.” Jing Fang’s Divination of Flying Phenomena through the Changes [?] says: “In the west there are great clouds of five colors; beneath them is a worthy man.” How closely the forms of clouds resemble our worthy scholars! Moreover, I have heard that Zhongnan and Taibai stretch in great mountain masses, reaching westward as far as Kunlun. Were you many scholars not nurtured by the concentrated excellence of these mountains?
