Policy Essay
First Question
Xing Fengmao
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔He adduces the classics to explain〕 the imperial teachings, fully displaying learning grounded in deep scholarly traditions. His exposition is clear and comprehensive; his long-range plans for carrying on and preserving the inheritance, and his proposed measures, are earnest and sincere. Upon opening the essay, one finds it suffused with loyal devotion. Accept it.
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔He frames his argument around the great foundation and great wisdom, developing it with refinement〕 and depth. His assessments are all commendable [?].

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正高　批〔敷陳明切具見忠愛〕
人君之世守鴻業也有保天下之大本而
後可以盡仁孝之實有周天下之大智而
後可以成繼述之功何則天人無二理仁
孝無二道人君之事天也猶乎其事親也
未有不實其心而能悅乎親者則亦未有
不實其心而能格乎天者也其法祖也猶
乎其法天也未有不達乎理而能法乎天
者則亦未有不達乎理而能法乎祖者也
===
故心以誠立則動爲實事而所以祈天永
命者有其本理以智研則事無膠固而所
以嗣大歷服者有其具夫然敬不假于靡
文之飾孝有得夫化裁之妙有不足以保
天下于可久綿世業于無疆也哉竊聞詩
大明有曰明明在下赫赫在上假樂曰不
愆不忘率由舊章斯二者以言乎創守則
均也而君子獨歸之守成蓋首出之君備
歷艱苦則憂勤之心必至固有不待敬而
punctuated:
考試官學正高，批〔敷陳明切，具見忠愛。〕

人君之世守鴻業也，有保天下之大本，而後可以盡仁孝之實；有周天下之大智，而後可以成繼述之功。何則？天人無二理，仁孝無二道。人君之事天也，猶乎其事親也。未有不實其心而能悅乎親者，則亦未有不實其心而能格乎天者也。其法祖也，猶乎其法天也。未有不達乎理而能法乎天者，則亦未有不達乎理而能法乎祖者也。故心以誠立，則動爲實事，而所以祈天永命者有其本；理以智研，則事無膠固，而所以嗣大歷服者有其具。夫然，敬不假于靡文之飾，孝有得夫化裁之妙，有不足以保天下于可久、綿世業于無疆也哉？竊聞《詩》〈大明〉有曰：「明明在下，赫赫在上。」〈假樂〉曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」斯二者，以言乎創守則均也，而君子獨歸之守成。蓋首出之君，備歷艱苦，則憂勤之心必至，固有不待敬而
translation_en:
Examiner Gao, an Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition is clear and incisive, fully revealing loyalty and devotion.〕

For a ruler to preserve his dynasty’s great undertaking through successive generations, he must possess the great foundation for safeguarding all under Heaven; only then can he fully realize benevolence and filial piety. He must possess the great wisdom that comprehends all under Heaven; only then can he accomplish the work of inheriting and carrying forward his predecessors’ achievements. Why is this? Heaven and humanity do not follow two different principles; benevolence and filial piety do not follow two different Ways. A ruler’s service to Heaven is like his service to his parents. No one whose heart is insincere can please his parents; likewise, no one whose heart is insincere can move Heaven. His emulation of his ancestors is like his emulation of Heaven. No one who fails to comprehend principle can emulate Heaven; likewise, no one who fails to comprehend principle can emulate his ancestors.

Thus, when the heart is established through sincerity, every action becomes a substantive deed, and there is a foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. When principle is investigated through wisdom, affairs are handled without rigid adherence, and there are means to inherit the great dynastic mandate. In this way, reverence does not depend upon elaborate ceremonial embellishments, and filial piety grasps the subtle art of adapting inherited practices to changing circumstances. Could this fail to safeguard all under Heaven for ages to come and perpetuate the dynastic undertaking without end?

I have humbly heard that “Great Brightness” (Daming) in the Book of Odes says: “Brightly shining below; gloriously radiant above.” “Admirable Joy” (Jiale) says: “Neither transgressing nor forgetting, following the ancient statutes.” These two sayings apply equally to founding a dynasty and preserving it, yet the gentleman assigns them particularly to preserving established achievements. For a founding ruler has experienced hardships to the full, and so his concern and diligence must reach their utmost; indeed, even without deliberately cultivating reverence …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
于撫已成之業在長君猶不可必而況于
當富有之年此夏商之所以不可及而肖
稱之所以爲無媿也自是以還漢之文帝
玄默恭儉而海內殷富似矣然禮樂則未
遑唐之高宗尊禮大臣而庶幾貞觀似矣
然覆霜則弗戒迄有宋眞宗寬仁慈愛帝
王之量似矣然矯誣上天而祖德亦隳曾
何以望有周之萬一哉肆我
太祖高皇帝受
===
命啓
運混一區宇嘗
諭輔臣曰人心乘氣機出入操存爲難又曰朕
上畏天地兢兢業業不敢自逸于是錄
存心以着敬天而又思所以爲燕詒之訓乃
採歷代諸王善可爲法惡可爲戒者輯爲
嗣君昭鑑錄以教
諸王其所以謹天命而垂典則視古帝王之
用心何異哉我
punctuated:
于撫已成之業，在長君猶不可必，而況于當富有之年？此夏商之所以不可及，而肖稱之所以爲無媿也。自是以還，漢之文帝玄默恭儉，而海內殷富，似矣，然禮樂則未遑；唐之高宗尊禮大臣，而庶幾貞觀，似矣，然覆霜則弗戒；迄有宋眞宗，寬仁慈愛，帝王之量，似矣，然矯誣上天，而祖德亦隳。曾何以望有周之萬一哉？
肆我太祖高皇帝受命啓運，混一區宇，嘗諭輔臣曰：「人心乘氣機出入，操存爲難。」又曰：「朕上畏天地，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」于是錄存心以着敬天，而又思所以爲燕詒之訓，乃採歷代諸王善可爲法、惡可爲戒者，輯爲《嗣君昭鑑錄》，以教諸王。其所以謹天命而垂典則，視古帝王之用心何異哉？我
translation_en:
…as for preserving an already established enterprise, even a mature ruler cannot be counted upon to do so—how much less one in the fullness of youth? This is why the Xia and Shang could not equal it, and why the designation of a worthy successor [?] was deserved without shame. Thereafter, Emperor Wen of the Han was quiet and reserved, respectful and frugal, and the realm was prosperous: he seemed comparable, yet he had no leisure for rites and music. Emperor Gaozong of the Tang honored and treated his great ministers with ceremony, nearly matching the Zhenguan reign: he seemed comparable, yet he failed to heed the warning of “treading on frost”—the first sign of impending danger. Later, Emperor Zhenzong of the Song was generous, humane, compassionate, and loving, with the magnanimity of a true sovereign: he seemed comparable, yet he falsely invoked Heaven and thereby also undermined his ancestors’ virtue. How could any of them hope to attain even a ten-thousandth of the Zhou’s achievement?
Thus our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate, inaugurated a new dynastic age, and united the realm. He once instructed his assisting ministers: “The human mind comes and goes with the workings of vital energy; holding fast to it and preserving it is difficult.” He also said: “Above, I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth. Vigilant and conscientious, I dare not indulge in ease.” Accordingly, he recorded teachings on preserving the mind to make manifest reverence for Heaven [?]. He also considered how to provide instruction that would secure the well-being of his descendants. He therefore selected, from the princes of successive dynasties, good deeds worthy of emulation and evil deeds that could serve as warnings, compiling them into the Record of Clear Admonitory Examples for Succeeding Rulers (Sijun zhaojian lu), with which to instruct the princes. In thus attending reverently to Heaven’s mandate and transmitting authoritative standards, how did his intentions differ from those of the emperors and kings of antiquity? Our…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝奉
天纘序統御方夏嘗自謂天之視聽相爲感通
人心之敬忽有間則天命之去留無常于是
因
存心錄爲
聖學心法而又謂
繼世之君謹守
祖法則
世祚延長乃
===
命儒臣集爲
文華寶鑑以貽世範其所以殷敬畏而裕
後昆視我
太祖之宏規寧有二哉我
列聖相繼揆符主鬯上有以順
皇天鑒佑之心遠有以追
二祖德業之盛率是道也暨我
世宗肅皇帝
聖神文武欽明允恭位彌久而道彌隆德愈盛
punctuated: 成祖文皇帝奉天纘序，統御方夏，嘗自謂：「天之視聽，相爲感通；人心之敬忽有間，則天命之去留無常。」于是因《存心錄》爲《聖學心法》，而又謂：「繼世之君謹守祖法，則世祚延長。」乃命儒臣集爲《文華寶鑑》，以貽世範。其所以殷敬畏而裕後昆，視我太祖之宏規，寧有二哉？我列聖相繼，揆符主鬯，上有以順皇天鑒佑之心，遠有以追二祖德業之盛，率是道也。暨我世宗肅皇帝，聖神文武，欽明允恭，位彌久而道彌隆，德愈盛
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, Chengzu, obeyed Heaven and continued the imperial succession, ruling over the Chinese realm. He once declared: “Heaven’s seeing and hearing respond in mutual communion with human beings. When the human heart alternates between reverence and heedlessness, Heaven’s mandate cannot remain constant in its departure or retention.” Accordingly, he drew upon the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu) to produce the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). He further declared: “If a ruler who succeeds to the throne carefully preserves his ancestors’ laws, the dynasty’s tenure will endure.” He therefore ordered Confucian officials to compile the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian), leaving a model for successive generations. In deepening reverence and awe and providing generously for his descendants, how could his purpose have differed from the grand designs of our Taizu?
Our successive sage emperors, whose guiding principles accorded with one another and who presided over the ancestral sacrifices, thereby fulfilled August Heaven’s intent to watch over and protect them above, and emulated the flourishing virtue and achievements of the two ancestral founders of the distant past. All followed this Way. Coming down to our Emperor Su, Shizong, he was sagely and inspired, accomplished in civil and military affairs, reverent and discerning, truly respectful. The longer he occupied the throne, the more exalted his Way became; the more abundant his virtue…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而化愈光以昭事上帝嘗
諭羣臣有曰知所尊以尊焉凡一言一動以至
于予賞刑罰不敢私一已之欲于是
欽天有頌
敬一有箴凡可以奉天則謹天戒者蓋匪徒託
之空言而已也以繩
祖武則又曰知所親以親焉凡出入語默以及
于民彛物則不敢作纖毫之惡于是
祖德有詩謌
陵有述所謂繼序思不忘者真有一舉足而不
敢懈也至于去
昊天之名恭上
皇天上帝尊號發
皇祖所未發也祀
皇祖于
圜丘宗
皇考于
明堂備
punctuated: 而化愈光。以昭事上帝，嘗諭羣臣有曰：「知所尊以尊焉，凡一言一動，以至于予賞刑罰，不敢私一已之欲。」于是欽天有頌，敬一有箴，凡可以奉天則、謹天戒者，蓋匪徒託之空言而已也。以繩祖武，則又曰：「知所親以親焉，凡出入語默，以及于民彛物則，不敢作纖毫之惡。」于是祖德有詩，謌陵有述，所謂「繼序思不忘」者，真有一舉足而不敢懈也。至于去昊天之名，恭上皇天上帝尊號，發皇祖所未發也；祀皇祖于圜丘，宗皇考于明堂，備
translation_en:
…and his transforming influence grew ever more radiant. In illustriously serving the Lord on High, he once instructed his assembled ministers: “Know whom to revere and revere him. In every word and action, extending to the granting of rewards and the imposition of punishments, I dare not indulge my own selfish desires.” Thus there was a eulogy on revering Heaven and an admonition on reverently maintaining oneness. All that served to uphold Heaven’s norms and heed Heaven’s warnings was surely more than empty words.

As for following in his ancestors’ footsteps, he further said: “Know whom to hold dear and hold them dear. In going out and coming in, in speech and silence, extending to the constant principles of human relations and the norms governing things, I dare not commit the slightest evil.” Thus there were poems on ancestral virtue and an account concerning “ge ling” [?]. What is meant by “continuing the succession, mindful never to forget” was truly realized in his not daring to relax his efforts even for a single step.

As for removing the designation “Vast Heaven” and reverently presenting the exalted title “August Heaven, Lord on High,” he initiated what his imperial ancestor had not initiated. In sacrificing to his imperial ancestor at the Circular Mound and honoring his deceased imperial father as an ancestor in the Hall of Light, he provided…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
皇祖所未備也有保天下之大本而又有周天
下之大智此其所以度越成周而卓然擅
中興之美豈偶然哉我
皇上聰明
天啓
聖學日新爰自
踐祚以及
今日
經筵無資于啓沃
===
萬幾不憚乎
躬親饗
帝饗
親則務竭乎誠信大政大禮則動求乎
成法禱旱而甘澍時若荷天心之感應不啻速
也因澇而問粜免稅務損上以益下惠何
渥也若此者成王之訪落陟降無以尚矣
乃者災沴頻疏于四方治效未臻于咸亨
此明問之所由發也然自愚言之古人君
punctuated: 皇祖所未備也。有保天下之大本，而又有周天下之大智，此其所以度越成周，而卓然擅中興之美，豈偶然哉！我皇上聰明天啓，聖學日新。爰自踐祚以及今日，經筵無資于啓沃，萬幾不憚乎躬親。饗帝饗親，則務竭乎誠信；大政大禮，則動求乎成法。禱旱而甘澍時若，荷天心之感應，不啻速也。因澇而問粜免稅，務損上以益下，惠何渥也！若此者，成王之訪落陟降，無以尚矣。乃者災沴頻疏于四方，治效未臻于咸亨，此明問之所由發也。然自愚言之，古人君
translation_en:
…what the imperial ancestor had not completed. He possessed the great foundation for preserving All under Heaven, together with the great wisdom to encompass it. These enabled him to surpass the accomplished Zhou dynasty and stand preeminent in the glory of dynastic revival. Could this have been mere chance?

Our Emperor’s intelligence is enlightened by Heaven, and his sagely learning is renewed daily. From his accession down to the present day, he has had no need of instruction to enrich his understanding at the Classics Colloquium, yet has never shrunk from personally attending to the myriad affairs of government. In offering sacrifices to the Lord on High and to his imperial forebears, he strives to show the utmost sincerity and good faith; in great affairs of government and great rites, he invariably seeks established precedents. He prayed during drought, and welcome rain fell in due season: Heaven’s gracious response was exceedingly swift. In response to flooding, he inquired into grain sales [?] and remitted taxes, striving to diminish what accrued to those above so as to benefit those below. How abundant his benevolence! Even King Cheng’s seeking counsel at the beginning of his reign and his reverent conduct could not surpass such deeds.

Recently, however, reports of calamities and baleful disturbances have come repeatedly from every quarter, and the results of government have not yet attained universal prosperity. This is what prompted your discerning question. Yet, in my humble view, the rulers of antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之保天下者其心嘗自思曰天下者天之
所以子我祖之所以燕翼我者也天之所
以子我則不可不務脩德以爲承藉之地
祖之所以燕翼我則不可不務法守以爲
永保之圖又嘗自思曰保天下之道有情
有文有經有權人而不惟其情惟其文不
惟其權惟其經是膠柱而鼓瑟也故謂燔
柴燎望敬天在是矣而致嚴于圭璧祝史
之間如漢武之泰畤西畤非不虔也而或
===
以爲瀆焉謂不改其道法祖在是矣而不
達乎因陋襲舊之弊如唐睿宗之用斜封
非不述事也而或以爲過焉至于理所當
因則守王季之舊而不爲執理所當革則
攻文王之德而不爲變不然孔子豈以達
孝私一武周哉故君人者有保治之實心
而又有研幾之大智其敬天也非特文之
而已必也昊天曰明而無敢馳驅昊天曰
旦而無敢戲豫天道好生而不殺天道恒
punctuated: 之保天下者，其心嘗自思曰：「天下者，天之所以子我、祖之所以燕翼我者也。天之所以子我，則不可不務脩德，以爲承藉之地；祖之所以燕翼我，則不可不務法守，以爲永保之圖。」又嘗自思曰：「保天下之道，有情有文，有經有權。人而不惟其情惟其文，不惟其權惟其經，是膠柱而鼓瑟也。」故謂燔柴燎望，敬天在是矣，而致嚴于圭璧祝史之間，如漢武之泰畤、西畤，非不虔也，而或以爲瀆焉；謂不改其道，法祖在是矣，而不達乎因陋襲舊之弊，如唐睿宗之用斜封，非不述事也，而或以爲過焉。至于理所當因，則守王季之舊而不爲執；理所當革，則攻文王之德而不爲變。不然，孔子豈以達孝私一武周哉？故君人者，有保治之實心，而又有研幾之大智。其敬天也，非特文之而已，必也昊天曰明，而無敢馳驅；昊天曰旦，而無敢戲豫。天道好生而不殺，天道恒
translation_en:
…who preserved All under Heaven would reflect in their hearts: “All under Heaven is what Heaven has bestowed upon me as its son, and what my ancestors have provided to secure the welfare of their descendants. Since Heaven has thus treated me as its son, I must diligently cultivate virtue as the foundation for receiving and sustaining this gift. Since my ancestors have thus provided for their descendants, I must diligently uphold their established institutions as a means of preserving it forever.” They would also reflect: “The way to preserve All under Heaven has both substance and outward form, both constant principles and discretionary adaptation. To attend only to outward form and not to substance, only to constant principles and not to discretionary adaptation, is like gluing down the bridges of a zither and then trying to play it.”

Thus, some say that reverence for Heaven consists in burning firewood as an offering and performing burnt offerings and sacrifices to distant powers. They exercise the utmost solemnity over jade tablets and discs and the work of invocators and scribes. Emperor Wu of Han’s sacrifices at the Tai and Western Altars were certainly devout, yet some considered them a desecration. Others say that following one’s ancestors consists in not changing their ways, yet fail to recognize the harm in perpetuating inadequate practices and simply following precedent. Emperor Ruizong of Tang’s use of irregular appointments issued in slant-sealed documents certainly continued earlier practice, yet some considered it a fault.

Where principle requires continuity, one may preserve the old practices of Wang Ji without being obstinate; where principle requires reform, one may build upon [?] the virtue of King Wen without being a disruptive innovator. Otherwise, would Confucius, in speaking of universally exemplary filial piety, have singled out King Wu and the Duke of Zhou merely out of partiality? Thus, a ruler must have a sincere commitment to preserving good government, together with the great wisdom to discern the subtle beginnings of events. His reverence for Heaven must go beyond outward observance. He must recognize that “August Heaven is clear-sighted” and dare not rush about heedlessly; that “August Heaven is watchful” and dare not indulge in amusement and ease. The Way of Heaven cherishes life rather than killing; the Way of Heaven endures…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
久而有常天以大虛爲體而法之爲翕受
天以行健爲用而法之爲自强五材天所
生也制爲取用之節四氣天所序也律爲
時措之宜因福善以親賢懲禍淫以遠姦
發號施令罔有不藏一天之風霆雨露各
當其可也左右前後罔匪正人一天之衆
星旋繞罔不順軌也自深宫大內以至接
禮賢士大夫之際儼乎大祭之是承由嚮
晦宴息以至禮樂刑政之大昭乎上帝之
臨汝夫然則一敬達于上下而天人一致
===
所謂下有明明之德斯上有赫赫之命在
我矣有不足以安天下乎其法祖也非特
守之而已必也祖考以憂勤開基而不遑
暇逸祖考以敬義憲天而邁種厥德祖有
功而繼序其功焉宗有德而作求其德焉
心法可考用之爲直內之方身法可鑒資
之爲飭躬之準納諫咈咈祖德之舍己也
而法之爲虛己望道未見祖德之謙己也
punctuated:
久而有常。天以大虛爲體，而法之爲翕受；天以行健爲用，而法之爲自强。五材，天所生也，制爲取用之節；四氣，天所序也，律爲時措之宜。因福善以親賢，懲禍淫以遠姦。發號施令，罔有不藏，一天之風霆雨露各當其可也；左右前後，罔匪正人，一天之衆星旋繞罔不順軌也。自深宫大內以至接禮賢士大夫之際，儼乎大祭之是承；由嚮晦宴息以至禮樂刑政之大，昭乎上帝之臨汝。夫然，則一敬達于上下，而天人一致。所謂「下有明明之德，斯上有赫赫之命」，在我矣，有不足以安天下乎？
其法祖也，非特守之而已。必也祖考以憂勤開基，而不遑暇逸；祖考以敬義憲天，而邁種厥德。祖有功，而繼序其功焉；宗有德，而作求其德焉。心法可考，用之爲直內之方；身法可鑒，資之爲飭躬之準。納諫咈咈，祖德之舍己也，而法之爲虛己；望道未見，祖德之謙己也。
translation_en:
…enduring and constant. Heaven takes the great void as its substance; emulate this through all-embracing receptivity. Heaven takes vigorous movement as its operation; emulate this through self-strengthening. The five materials are produced by Heaven: establish limits on their acquisition and use. The four seasonal influences are ordered by Heaven: regulate actions so that they suit their proper times. Follow Heaven’s blessing of the good by drawing close to the worthy; heed its punishment of the wicked by distancing the treacherous. Let every proclamation and command be good [?], just as Heaven’s winds, thunder, rain, and dew are each appropriate to their occasion. Let those to the left and right, before and behind, all be upright men, just as Heaven’s myriad stars revolve without departing from their courses. From life within the secluded palace to occasions of receiving worthy scholar-officials with due courtesy, remain solemn as though conducting a great sacrifice. From resting as darkness falls to the great affairs of rites, music, punishments, and government, remain clearly conscious that the Lord on High watches over you. Thus a single reverence pervades above and below, and Heaven and humanity are united. What is meant by “Where there is resplendent virtue below, there is a glorious mandate above” will then be realized in oneself. Could this be insufficient to bring peace to all under Heaven?
As for emulating the ancestors, this is more than merely preserving their legacy. The ancestral forebears laid the foundations through anxious diligence: one must allow oneself no idle ease. They took Heaven as their model through reverence and righteousness: one must vigorously cultivate their virtue. Where the founding ancestors achieved merit, carry that merit forward in due succession; where their successors possessed virtue, seek to realize that virtue. Their methods of cultivating the mind can be examined: use them as a means of making the inner self upright. Their examples of personal conduct can serve as a mirror: draw upon them as standards for disciplining oneself. Accepting forthright remonstrance exemplified the ancestors’ virtue of setting aside their own wishes; emulate this by becoming receptive and humble. Looking toward the Way as though they had yet to perceive it exemplified the ancestors’ virtue of humility…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而法之以戒盈以其所以應天者而祈乎
天以其所以順人者而安乎人敬以事神
和以接物一肅肅雍雍之遺也不狃近利
惟�french
punctuated: 而法之以戒盈，以其所以應天者而祈乎天，以其所以順人者而安乎人。敬以事神，和以接物，一肅肅雍雍之遺也。不狃近利，惟�french
translation_en: …and emulate this by guarding against complacency. Pray to Heaven through the means by which the ancestors responded to Heaven; bring peace to the people through the means by which they accorded with the people. Serve the spirits with reverence and engage with others in harmony: all this is the legacy of their solemn reverence and harmonious dignity. Do not become attached to immediate gain; only [the remaining text, �french, is corrupt and unintelligible: ?]…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道體之全推其義以盡裁成之妙此天地
聖人相待以成而後天地有全能聖人有
全功矣請因明問而敬陳之夫道何爲而
始也由天地而始也道何爲而終也由聖
人而終也易大傳曰河出圖洛出書聖人
則之蓋昔者庖犧氏之繼天而王也有龍
馬負圖出于河其文一六居北二七居南
三八居東四九居西五十居中本天地自
然生成之數也伏犧于其一三五七九而
===
識其爲奇也陽也天道也于其二四六八
十而識其爲耦也陰也地道也于是則之
以畫卦陰陽錯綜而乾兌離震巽坎艮坤
立焉此天地之化育所由肇也大禹之治
水功成也有神龜載書出于洛其文戴九
履一左三右七二四爲肩六八爲足本天
地自然貞勝之數也大禹于其一三五七
九而識其爲奇贏也陽當有餘也人所宜
扶也于其二四六八而識其爲耦乏也陰
punctuated:
道體之全，推其義以盡裁成之妙。此天地、聖人相待以成，而後天地有全能，聖人有全功矣。請因明問而敬陳之。夫道何爲而始也？由天地而始也。道何爲而終也？由聖人而終也。《易大傳》曰：「河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」蓋昔者庖犧氏之繼天而王也，有龍馬負圖出于河，其文一六居北，二七居南，三八居東，四九居西，五十居中，本天地自然生成之數也。伏犧于其一三五七九而識其爲奇也、陽也、天道也；于其二四六八十而識其爲耦也、陰也、地道也。于是則之以畫卦，陰陽錯綜，而乾、兌、離、震、巽、坎、艮、坤立焉。此天地之化育所由肇也。
大禹之治水功成也，有神龜載書出于洛，其文戴九履一，左三右七，二四爲肩，六八爲足，本天地自然貞勝之數也。大禹于其一三五七九而識其爲奇贏也，陽當有餘也，人所宜扶也；于其二四六八而識其爲耦乏也，陰
translation_en:
…the completeness of the substance of the Way, extending its principles to realize fully the subtle work of shaping and completing creation. Thus Heaven and Earth and the sage depend upon one another for fulfillment; only then do Heaven and Earth exercise their full capacity and the sage achieve his full accomplishment. Allow me respectfully to expound upon this in response to your illuminating question. Where does the Way begin? It begins with Heaven and Earth. Where does the Way reach completion? It reaches completion through the sage. The Great Commentary on the Book of Changes says: “The Yellow River brought forth the Diagram, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as their models.” In ancient times, when Paoxi succeeded Heaven as king, a dragon-horse emerged from the Yellow River bearing the Diagram. In its pattern, one and six occupied the north, two and seven the south, three and eight the east, four and nine the west, and five and ten the center. These were inherently the numbers by which Heaven and Earth naturally generate and complete things. Fuxi recognized its one, three, five, seven, and nine as odd numbers, as yang, and as the Way of Heaven; he recognized its two, four, six, eight, and ten as even numbers, as yin, and as the Way of Earth. He accordingly took this as his model in drawing the trigrams. Through the interweaving and combination of yin and yang, Qian, Dui, Li, Zhen, Xun, Kan, Gen, and Kun were established. This was how the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth began.
When Yu the Great completed his work of bringing the waters under control, a divine tortoise emerged from the Luo River bearing the Writing. Its pattern bore nine above and one below, three on the left and seven on the right, two and four as shoulders, and six and eight as feet. These were inherently the numbers of the natural alternation of ascendancy in Heaven and Earth. Yu the Great recognized that its one, three, five, seven, and nine constituted a preponderance of odd numbers: yang ought to have a surplus, and people ought to support it. He recognized that its two, four, six, and eight constituted a deficiency of even numbers: yin …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當不足也人所宜抑也于是則之以第疇
因天責人而五行五事八政五紀皇極三
德稽疑庶徵福極陳焉此天地之化育所
由成也夫圖本無卦也而卦之理已寓書
本無疇也而疇之理已存伏犧則圖以畫
卦大禹則書以敘疇孔安國劉向父子非
無見也苟謂圖以龍馬而制則龍馬所載
爲何圖書以洛龜而成則洛龜所負爲何
象無乃以易言伏犧仰觀俯察以畫卦不
===
言龍馬而因以例書乎然安知龍馬非俯
察之一事也河圖呈于伏犧而十以揭其
全體洛書錫于神禹而九以著其大用關
子明邵堯夫諸人未爲無見也苟謂以九
爲河圖則洩其秘于先者何以不舉其全
以十爲洛書則闡其用于後者何以反益
以十無乃以圖書互藏其用而託言于陳
希夷以爲二者皆出于伏犧乎然不知圖
書數各有定而理有攸當也要之圖書殊
punctuated: 當不足也，人所宜抑也。于是則之以第疇，因天責人，而五行、五事、八政、五紀、皇極、三德、稽疑、庶徵、福極陳焉。此天地之化育所由成也。夫圖本無卦也，而卦之理已寓；書本無疇也，而疇之理已存。伏犧則圖以畫卦，大禹則書以敘疇，孔安國、劉向父子非無見也。苟謂圖以龍馬而制，則龍馬所載爲何圖？書以洛龜而成，則洛龜所負爲何象？無乃以《易》言伏犧仰觀俯察以畫卦，不言龍馬，而因以例書乎？然安知龍馬非俯察之一事也？河圖呈于伏犧，而十以揭其全體；洛書錫于神禹，而九以著其大用。關子明、邵堯夫諸人未爲無見也。苟謂以九爲河圖，則洩其秘于先者何以不舉其全？以十爲洛書，則闡其用于後者何以反益以十？無乃以圖書互藏其用，而託言于陳希夷，以爲二者皆出于伏犧乎？然不知圖書數各有定，而理有攸當也。要之，圖書殊
translation_en:
…ought to be deficient, and are what people should restrain. Accordingly, he took this as his model in arranging the categories, holding people accountable by reference to Heaven. Thus were set forth the Five Phases, the Five Activities, the Eight Affairs of Government, the Five Calendrical Regulators, the Royal Ultimate, the Three Virtues, the Resolution of Doubts, the Various Signs, and Blessings and Calamities. Through these, the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth was brought to completion.

The Chart originally contained no trigrams, yet the principles of the trigrams were already implicit in it; the Writing originally contained no categories, yet the principles of the categories were already present in it. Fuxi took the Chart as his model in drawing the trigrams; the Great Yu took the Writing as his model in arranging the categories. Kong Anguo, Liu Xiang, and Liu Xiang’s son were not without insight. If one claims that the Chart was fashioned from the dragon-horse, then what chart did the dragon-horse carry? If the Writing was formed from the Luo River tortoise, then what configuration did that tortoise bear? Could this claim arise because the Book of Changes says that Fuxi looked upward and examined things below to draw the trigrams, without mentioning the dragon-horse, and this account is then extended by analogy to the Writing? Yet how can one know that the dragon-horse was not among the things he examined below?

The River Chart appeared to Fuxi, with ten revealing its complete structure; the Luo Writing was bestowed upon the divine Yu, with nine manifesting its great operation. Guan Ziming, Shao Yaofu, and others were not without insight. If one identifies the configuration of nine as the River Chart, why did the earlier revelation of its mysteries not display it in its entirety? If one identifies the configuration of ten as the Luo Writing, why did the later exposition of its operation instead increase the number to ten? Could it be that, because the Chart and the Writing each conceal the operation of the other, people attributed to Chen Xiyi the assertion that both originated with Fuxi? Yet this fails to recognize that the Chart and the Writing each have their fixed numbers, and that their principles each have their appropriate correspondence. In essence, the Chart and the Writing differ …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
時而列數其象不能以不異圖書本數以
載理其究不能以不同故自其異者而觀
之河圖天數五地數五一陰一陽之道也
積之則天數二十五地數三十而五十有
五具焉天地之常陽不足而陰有餘也洛
書天數五地數四陽以統陰之義也積之
則天數二十五地數二十而四十有五具
焉天地之變陰宜消而陽宜長也河圖以
五生數統五成數同處其位陰陽合而後
生道備獨陽不生獨陰不成也洛書以五
奇數統四耦數而各處其方陰陽錯雜而
後有制陽得以兼陰陰不得以兼陽也河
圖運行之序始東次南次中次西次北左
旋一周而復起于東木火土金水生生之
本然也此兩儀四象八卦而六十四而四
千九十六萬事萬物之所從出也故曰天
地之大德曰生洛書推行之序始北次西
南次東南次東次中次西北次西次東北
punctuated: 時而列數，其象不能以不異；圖書本數以載理，其究不能以不同。故自其異者而觀之，河圖天數五，地數五，一陰一陽之道也。積之，則天數二十五，地數三十，而五十有五具焉。天地之常，陽不足而陰有餘也。洛書天數五，地數四，陽以統陰之義也。積之，則天數二十五，地數二十，而四十有五具焉。天地之變，陰宜消而陽宜長也。河圖以五生數統五成數，同處其位，陰陽合而後生道備，獨陽不生，獨陰不成也。洛書以五奇數統四耦數，而各處其方，陰陽錯雜而後有制，陽得以兼陰，陰不得以兼陽也。河圖運行之序，始東，次南，次中，次西，次北，左旋一周而復起于東，木火土金水生生之本然也。此兩儀、四象、八卦，而六十四，而四千九十六，萬事萬物之所從出也。故曰：「天地之大德曰生。」洛書推行之序，始北，次西南，次東南，次東，次中，次西北，次西，次東北，
translation_en: …at different times and array their numbers, so their configurations necessarily differ; yet the River Chart and the Luo Writing use numbers as the basis for conveying principle, so their ultimate purport necessarily accords. Thus, viewed in terms of their differences, the River Chart has five heavenly numbers and five earthly numbers: this is the Way of alternation between yin and yang. Added together, the heavenly numbers total twenty-five and the earthly numbers thirty, making fifty-five in all. This is the constant condition of Heaven and Earth: yang is insufficient, while yin is in surplus. The Luo Writing has five heavenly numbers and four earthly numbers: this expresses the principle that yang governs yin. Added together, the heavenly numbers total twenty-five and the earthly numbers twenty, making forty-five in all. This is the transformation of Heaven and Earth: yin should wane and yang should wax. In the River Chart, the five generating numbers govern the five completing numbers, sharing their positions. Only when yin and yang unite is the Way of generation complete: yang alone cannot generate, and yin alone cannot bring to completion. In the Luo Writing, the five odd numbers govern the four even numbers, each occupying its own direction. Only when yin and yang intermingle is there regulation: yang may encompass yin, but yin may not encompass yang. The River Chart’s sequence of circulation begins in the east, proceeds south, then to the center, then west, then north; turning left through a full circuit, it begins again in the east. This is the inherent order of the ceaseless generation of wood, fire, earth, metal, and water. From this proceed the Two Modes, the Four Images, the Eight Trigrams, then the sixty-four hexagrams, then the four thousand and ninety-six combinations—the source from which the myriad affairs and things emerge. Hence it is said: “The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called generation.” The Luo Writing’s sequence of progression begins in the north, then proceeds southwest, southeast, east, to the center, northwest, west, and northeast…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
右旋一周而復究于南水火金木土相制
之妙用也此一消一長一闔一闢一進一
退四時日月所以相禪于無窮也故曰無
昜則乾坤幾乎息矣河圖以六七八九附
于生數之外以盡陰陽進退饒乏之正而
其九者生于一三五之積六者生于二四
之積七者九之自西而南八者六之自北
而東蓋至是而陰陽老少互藏之變備矣
洛書以七八六九縱横十五以盡陰陽消
===
長之理而其虛五分十則以一含九以二
含八以三含七以四含六蓋至是而陰陽
參伍錯綜之妙舉矣是固圖書之所以異
也而異者未始不同自其同者而觀之河
圖之一二三四各奠其方而常居內六七
八九各以其類而附于外是以內者爲主
而外爲客也洛書之一三七九各本其氣
而正其位二四六八各從其合而附于側
是以正者爲主而側爲客也此圖之未始
punctuated:
右旋一周而復究于南，水火金木土相制之妙用也。此一消一長，一闔一闢，一進一退，四時日月所以相禪于無窮也。故曰：「無昜則乾坤幾乎息矣。」河圖以六七八九附于生數之外，以盡陰陽進退饒乏之正。而其九者，生于一三五之積；六者，生于二四之積；七者，九之自西而南；八者，六之自北而東。蓋至是而陰陽老少互藏之變備矣。洛書以七八六九縱横十五，以盡陰陽消長之理。而其虛五分十，則以一含九，以二含八，以三含七，以四含六。蓋至是而陰陽參伍錯綜之妙舉矣。
是固圖書之所以異也，而異者未始不同。自其同者而觀之，河圖之一二三四，各奠其方而常居內；六七八九，各以其類而附于外，是以內者爲主而外爲客也。洛書之一三七九，各本其氣而正其位；二四六八，各從其合而附于側，是以正者爲主而側爲客也。此圖之未始
translation_en:
…rotating to the right through a complete circuit and returning to end in the south: this is the wondrous operation by which water, fire, metal, wood, and earth restrain one another. This alternation of waning and waxing, closing and opening, advancing and retreating is how the four seasons, the sun, and the moon succeed one another without end. Thus it is said: “Without change, Qian and Kun would almost cease to function.” The River Chart (Hetu) places six, seven, eight, and nine outside the generating numbers, thereby fully expressing the regular pattern of yin and yang advancing and retreating, in abundance and deficiency. Its nine arises from the sum of one, three, and five; its six arises from the sum of two and four. Seven is nine moving from west to south; eight is six moving from north to east. At this point, the transformations through which old and young yin and yang contain one another are complete. The Luo Writing (Luoshu) arranges seven, eight, six, and nine so that the horizontal and vertical sums are fifteen, thereby fully expressing the principle of yin and yang waning and waxing. Setting aside the central five and dividing ten into pairs, it has one contain nine, two contain eight, three contain seven, and four contain six. At this point, the subtleties of the interweaving and coordination of yin and yang are fully displayed.
These are indeed the ways in which the Chart and the Writing differ; yet their differences have never excluded their similarities. Viewed in terms of their similarities, one, two, three, and four in the River Chart each occupy their allotted direction and always lie within; six, seven, eight, and nine each attach themselves outside according to their kind. Thus those within are the hosts, and those outside are the guests. In the Luo Writing, one, three, seven, and nine each take their own qi as their basis and occupy the principal positions; two, four, six, and eight each follow their corresponding partner and attach themselves at the sides. Thus those in the principal positions are the hosts, and those at the sides are the guests. This shows that the Chart has never…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不抑陰而書之未始不尊陽也河圖之以
五居中也五生數之象實在焉下則天一
之象也上則地二之象也左則天三之象
也右則地四之象也中則天五之象也洛
書之以五居中也五奇數之象實在焉下
亦天一之象也左亦天三之象也中亦天
五之象也右亦天七之象也上則天九之
象也此圖之虛中而太極以立卽書之虛
中而五氣以萃也圖之一六同宗而位乎
===
北二七爲朋而位乎南三八同道而位乎
東四九爲友而位乎西五十相守而位乎
中生成五位之相得也其五獨居中而分
十者則外陰之義耳書之一正乎北而六
從之七正乎西而二附之三正乎東而八
隨之九正乎南而四因之是奇耦之各有
合也其五獨正乎中而黜十者則滅陰之
義耳此圖之生成未始不爲書之奇耦書
之正側未始不爲圖之內外也圖之虛五
punctuated: 不抑陰，而書之未始不尊陽也。河圖之以五居中也，五生數之象實在焉：下則天一之象也，上則地二之象也，左則天三之象也，右則地四之象也，中則天五之象也。洛書之以五居中也，五奇數之象實在焉：下亦天一之象也，左亦天三之象也，中亦天五之象也，右亦天七之象也，上則天九之象也。此圖之虛中而太極以立，即書之虛中而五氣以萃也。圖之一六同宗而位乎北，二七爲朋而位乎南，三八同道而位乎東，四九爲友而位乎西，五十相守而位乎中，生成五位之相得也。其五獨居中而分十者，則外陰之義耳。書之一正乎北而六從之，七正乎西而二附之，三正乎東而八隨之，九正乎南而四因之，是奇耦之各有合也。其五獨正乎中而黜十者，則滅陰之義耳。此圖之生成未始不爲書之奇耦，書之正側未始不爲圖之內外也。圖之虛五
translation_en:
…never fails to restrain yin, while the Luo Writing never fails to honor yang. In the River Chart (Hetu), five occupies the center, and the configurations of the five generating numbers are indeed present within it: below is the configuration of Heaven’s one; above, that of Earth’s two; to the left, that of Heaven’s three; to the right, that of Earth’s four; and in the center, that of Heaven’s five. In the Luo Writing (Luoshu), five occupies the center, and the configurations of the five odd numbers are indeed present within it: below, too, is the configuration of Heaven’s one; to the left, that of Heaven’s three; in the center, that of Heaven’s five; to the right, that of Heaven’s seven; and above, that of Heaven’s nine. Thus, leaving the center of the Chart vacant so that the Supreme Ultimate is established corresponds to leaving the center of the Writing vacant so that the five vital energies converge there.

In the Chart, one and six share a common lineage and occupy the north; two and seven are companions and occupy the south; three and eight follow the same way and occupy the east; four and nine are friends and occupy the west; and five and ten keep company and occupy the center. These are the generating and completing numbers fitting together in the five positions. That five alone occupies the center while ten is divided expresses merely the principle of placing yin outside. In the Writing, one occupies the principal position in the north and six follows it; seven occupies the principal position in the west and two attaches itself to it; three occupies the principal position in the east and eight follows it; nine occupies the principal position in the south and four adheres to it. Thus the odd and even numbers each have their pairing. That five alone occupies the principal position in the center while ten is excluded expresses merely the principle of eliminating yin. Thus the generating and completing numbers of the Chart are invariably the odd and even numbers of the Writing, while the principal and lateral positions of the Writing are invariably the inner and outer positions of the Chart. The Chart’s setting aside of five…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
與十者太極也奇數二十耦數二十者兩
儀也以一二三四合六七八九者四象也
析四方之合以爲乾坤坎離補四隅之缺
以爲兌震巽艮者八卦也義固有所在矣
而書之虛五其中者是亦太極也奇偶各
居二十者兩儀也一二三四五合六七八
九縱橫十五爲七八九六者四象也以四
方之正爲乾坤離坎以四隅之偏爲兌震
巽艮者亦八卦也是圖之體未始不含書
之用而書之用未始不具圖之體也此固
===
圖書之所以同也而同者不能以無殊易
曰顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同
憂天道也河圖之所由出也裁成天地之
道輔相天地之宜以左右民人道也此洛
書之所以爲有憂也後之儒者有見于其
同則謂圖書皆出于伏犧有見于其異則
謂洪範不由于洛書他如楊雄之太玄關
朗之洞極司馬之潛虛延壽之訓詁京房
punctuated: 與十者，太極也；奇數二十、耦數二十者，兩儀也；以一二三四合六七八九者，四象也；析四方之合以爲乾坤坎離，補四隅之缺以爲兌震巽艮者，八卦也。義固有所在矣。而書之虛五其中者，是亦太極也；奇偶各居二十者，兩儀也；一二三四五合六七八九，縱橫十五，爲七八九六者，四象也；以四方之正爲乾坤離坎，以四隅之偏爲兌震巽艮者，亦八卦也。是圖之體未始不含書之用，而書之用未始不具圖之體也。此固圖書之所以同也，而同者不能以無殊。《易》曰：「顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」天道也，河圖之所由出也。「裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」人道也，此洛書之所以爲有憂也。後之儒者，有見于其同，則謂圖書皆出于伏犧；有見于其異，則謂洪範不由于洛書。他如楊雄之《太玄》、關朗之《洞極》、司馬之《潛虛》、延壽之訓詁、京房
translation_en: …and ten: these constitute the Supreme Ultimate. The odd numbers totaling twenty and the even numbers totaling twenty constitute the Two Modes. Pairing one, two, three, and four with six, seven, eight, and nine constitutes the Four Images. Separating the pairs at the four cardinal positions to form Qian, Kun, Kan, and Li, and filling the gaps at the four corners to form Dui, Zhen, Xun, and Gen, constitutes the Eight Trigrams. These arrangements certainly have their meaning. In the Luo Writing, leaving out the five at its center likewise constitutes the Supreme Ultimate. The odd and even numbers each totaling twenty constitute the Two Modes. Combining one, two, three, four, and five with six, seven, eight, and nine, so that the vertical and horizontal sums are fifteen, and deriving seven, eight, nine, and six, constitutes the Four Images [?]. Taking the four cardinal positions as Qian, Kun, Li, and Kan, and the four intermediate corner positions as Dui, Zhen, Xun, and Gen, likewise constitutes the Eight Trigrams. Thus the substance of the River Chart always contains the functioning of the Luo Writing, while the functioning of the Luo Writing always embodies the substance of the River Chart. This, indeed, is why the Chart and the Writing are alike; yet their likeness cannot mean that they have no differences. The Book of Changes says: “Manifested in benevolence and concealed in its functioning, it quickens the myriad things without sharing the sage’s anxieties.” This is the Way of Heaven, from which the River Chart issues. “To shape and complete the Way of Heaven and Earth, to assist what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby to guide the people”: this is the human Way, and this is why the Luo Writing entails anxiety. Later Confucian scholars, perceiving their likeness, claimed that the Chart and the Writing both originated with Fuxi; perceiving their differences, they claimed that the Great Plan did not derive from the Luo Writing. Other examples include Yang Xiong’s Supreme Mystery (Taixuan), Guan Lang’s Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), Sima’s Hidden Void (Qianxu), Yanshou’s textual exegesis, and Jing Fang’s…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之氣數王弼之理致皆穿鑿附會而造化
自然之功用始紛然不可窮矣大抵理一
而已有天地之造化有聖人之造化天地
之造化鬼神生成之本也聖人之造化酬
酢有相之道也不觀天地之化則無以見
聖人之道有所本不觀聖人之道則無以
見天地之化有所終故天無二日民無二
王陰晴治亂君子小人多寡之不齊者天
地之常也聖人以其常而通其變撥亂而
反之正尊君卑臣進君子退小人內中國
外夷狄所以扶陽抑陰贊天地之化育也
是故明此而帝堯舜之所以闢洪荒奠求
賴去四凶進元凱則治統立而道統以正
明此而師則周孔之所以象易繫辭擴天
理戒人欲因河圖之體本洛書之義則道
統明而治統以彰蓋天地以無心而成化
聖人雖有心而無爲無爲者非一無所爲
也盡人以合天也至于盡人以合天則亦
punctuated:
之氣數、王弼之理致，皆穿鑿附會，而造化自然之功用始紛然不可窮矣。大抵理一而已，有天地之造化，有聖人之造化。天地之造化，鬼神生成之本也；聖人之造化，酬酢有相之道也。不觀天地之化，則無以見聖人之道有所本；不觀聖人之道，則無以見天地之化有所終。故天無二日，民無二王。陰晴治亂、君子小人多寡之不齊者，天地之常也。聖人以其常而通其變，撥亂而反之正，尊君卑臣，進君子退小人，內中國外夷狄，所以扶陽抑陰，贊天地之化育也。
是故明此而帝，堯舜之所以闢洪荒、奠求賴、去四凶、進元凱，則治統立而道統以正；明此而師，則周孔之所以象易繫辭、擴天理、戒人欲，因河圖之體，本洛書之義，則道統明而治統以彰。蓋天地以無心而成化，聖人雖有心而無爲。無爲者，非一無所爲也，盡人以合天也。至于盡人以合天，則亦
translation_en:
…the configurations and numerical patterns of qi, and Wang Bi’s interpretations of principle—all are strained explanations and forced associations, which have made the spontaneous workings of creation and transformation bewilderingly complex and impossible to exhaust.
Broadly speaking, principle is one and nothing more; yet there is the creative transformation of Heaven and Earth, and there is the creative transformation of the sages. The creative transformation of Heaven and Earth is the foundation of the spirits’ generation and completion of things; that of the sages is the Way of responding to things and providing assistance. Unless we observe the transformations of Heaven and Earth, we cannot see that the sages’ Way has a foundation; unless we observe the sages’ Way, we cannot see that the transformations of Heaven and Earth have their fulfillment. Thus Heaven has no two suns, and the people have no two kings. The uneven alternation of overcast and clear skies, order and disorder, and the differing numbers of exemplary and petty men are constant features of Heaven and Earth. Through these constants, the sages comprehend change: they quell disorder and restore what is right, exalt the ruler and subordinate his ministers, advance exemplary men and dismiss petty men, treat the Central States as the inner realm and the Yi and Di peoples as the outer. By these means they support yang and restrain yin, assisting Heaven and Earth in transforming and nurturing all things.
Thus, understanding this and acting as sovereigns, Yao and Shun opened up the primordial wilderness, established a basis of reliance [?], expelled the Four Malefactors, and advanced the Yuan and Kai worthies. The succession of rightful governance was thereby established, and the succession of the Way set right. Understanding this and acting as teachers, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius furnished the Changes with images and appended statements, extended heavenly principle, and warned against human desires. They followed the structure of the River Chart and grounded themselves in the meaning of the Luo Writing. The succession of the Way was thereby clarified, and the succession of rightful governance made manifest. Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intention; the sages, though possessing conscious intention, act without contrivance. Acting without contrivance does not mean doing nothing at all: it means fulfilling human effort so as to accord with Heaven. When human effort is fully realized so as to accord with Heaven, then this too…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天道之無爲而天下國家可坐而理矣執
事策士以研理之學無亦欲其究圖書之
旨歸以求盡夫聖神功化之極乎顧愚何
足以及此
第三問
周策
同考試官教諭彭　批〔人才之盛衰係于時而所以致多才者亢係于用至于純心焉要矣作者見未逹此率亦未有定論〕
〔子具涵達有要者可以觀才矣〕
考試官教諭張　批〔考論古今人才及用人之法甚〕
===
考試官教諭張　批〔用人要務得子有確見矣宜錄〕
〔篇開爲且有要論可採錄之〕
考試官學正高　批
〔以爲式〕
執事有感于
廟堂需才之議以古今人才下策末學而欲
得卓犖雄渾之才以拔出魁壘用佐我
聖天子昌熙之運意甚隆也顧愚才未脫乎椽
桷形未超乎驪黃曷足以與于此哉雖然
punctuated:
天道之無爲，而天下國家可坐而理矣。執事策士以研理之學，無亦欲其究圖書之旨歸，以求盡夫聖神功化之極乎？顧愚何足以及此！

第三問
周策
同考試官教諭彭　批〔人才之盛衰係于時，而所以致多才者亢係于用，至于純心焉，要矣。作者見未逹此，率亦未有定論。〕〔子具涵達有要者，可以觀才矣。〕
考試官教諭張　批〔考論古今人才及用人之法甚〕
考試官教諭張　批〔用人要務，得子有確見矣，宜錄。〕〔篇開爲且有要論可採，錄之。〕
考試官學正高　批〔以爲式。〕

執事有感于廟堂需才之議，以古今人才下策末學，而欲得卓犖雄渾之才，以拔出魁壘，用佐我聖天子昌熙之運，意甚隆也。顧愚才未脫乎椽桷，形未超乎驪黃，曷足以與于此哉？雖然，
translation_en:
…the nonaction of the Way of Heaven, and all under Heaven, the state, and the family can be brought to order without effort. You, honored examiners, have set candidates a policy question on the learning that investigates principle. Is your intention perhaps that they should fathom the ultimate purport of the River Chart and the Luo Writing, seeking to comprehend fully the utmost achievements and transforming influence of the sages and divine men? Yet how could someone as foolish as I attain this?

Third Question
Zhou Ce

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor: 〔The flourishing or decline of talent depends on the times, while bringing forth many talented men depends on their employment [?]. As for purity of heart, that is essential. The writer’s understanding has not reached this point, and on the whole he has arrived at no settled judgment.〕 〔Your treatment is comprehensive and penetrating and has essential points [?]; from it one can discern your talent.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔His examination and discussion of talented men, past and present, and of methods of employing men is very …〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔On the essential business of employing men, you have firm insights. This should be selected.〕 〔The essay’s opening [?] also contains important arguments worth adopting. Select it.〕
Comment by Examiner Gao, School Instructor: 〔Use it as a model.〕

Moved by the court’s discussion of its need for talent, you, honored examiners, have set a policy question about talented men of past and present for us humble students. You wish to find men of outstanding and vigorous ability, singling out the exceptional to assist the flourishing and harmonious reign of our sagely Son of Heaven. Your intention is indeed lofty. Yet my poor talent has not risen above that of mere rafters, nor has my outward form transcended the black or yellow coloring of a horse. How could I be worthy of inclusion among such men?
