title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
竊聞之漢史有云蓋有非常之功必有非
常之人然而非常之人其功率弘于草昧
之初何哉蓋草昧之初法制未定才將則
將焉才相則相焉無所謂例簿也而開創
之君惟其賢不惟其迹惟其稱不惟其資
無所謂牽制也若夫承平既久則規格科
條森然昭布而守文之世雖欲郤例顯庸
如吏議何知乎此則古今人才之盛衰始
有可言者矣易曰雲從龍風從虎聖人作
===
而萬物覩言君臣感應之不忒也詩曰鳳
凰鳴矣于彼高岡梧桐生矣于彼朝陽菶
菶萋萋雝雝喈喈言人才感召之有道也
粵稽古有虞以重華之德膺帝堯之禪當
時相與共治者有禹稷契皐陶伯益爲之
平水土敎稼穡明人倫飭五刑烈山澤以
翊成萬世永賴之功古今稱才之盛者莫
加焉迨至有周本執競之德爲弔伐之舉
當時相與興事者有周公召公南宮适散
punctuated:
竊聞之，漢史有云：「蓋有非常之功，必有非常之人。」然而非常之人，其功率弘于草昧之初，何哉？蓋草昧之初，法制未定，才將則將焉，才相則相焉，無所謂例簿也。而開創之君，惟其賢，不惟其迹；惟其稱，不惟其資，無所謂牽制也。若夫承平既久，則規格科條森然昭布，而守文之世，雖欲郤例顯庸，如吏議何？知乎此，則古今人才之盛衰始有可言者矣。《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」言君臣感應之不忒也。《詩》曰：「鳳凰鳴矣，于彼高岡；梧桐生矣，于彼朝陽。菶菶萋萋，雝雝喈喈。」言人才感召之有道也。
粵稽古，有虞以重華之德膺帝堯之禪，當時相與共治者，有禹、稷、契、皐陶、伯益，爲之平水土、敎稼穡、明人倫、飭五刑、烈山澤，以翊成萬世永賴之功，古今稱才之盛者莫加焉。迨至有周，本執競之德，爲弔伐之舉，當時相與興事者，有周公、召公、南宮适、散
translation_en:
…I have heard that the History of the Han says: “Extraordinary achievements surely require extraordinary men.” Yet why do extraordinary men generally accomplish their greatest deeds at the unsettled beginnings of an age? At such beginnings, laws and institutions are not yet fixed: those with the talent to command are made generals, and those with the talent to serve as chief ministers are made chief ministers. There are no registers of precedents to speak of. Founding rulers consider a man’s worth rather than his past record, and his fitness rather than his seniority. There are no such restraints. Once peace has endured for a long time, however, regulations and statutory provisions stand arrayed in imposing clarity. In an age devoted to preserving inherited institutions, even if a ruler wishes to set aside precedents and raise men to prominent service, what can he do about the objections of officials? Only by understanding this can we begin to discuss the flourishing and decline of talent throughout history. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all things behold him.” This speaks of the unfailing mutual response between ruler and ministers. The Book of Odes says: “The phoenix cries upon that high ridge; the wutong tree grows on that sunward slope. Lush and luxuriant is its foliage; harmonious and melodious are the birds’ cries.” This speaks of the proper way to attract and summon talented men.
Looking back into antiquity, the ruler of Yu, Shun, possessed the virtue of Chonghua, ‘Renewed Splendor,’ and received the throne upon Emperor Yao’s abdication. Those who then governed together with him included Yu, Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Bo Yi. For him they brought the waters and lands into order, taught sowing and harvesting, clarified human relationships, regulated the five punishments, and cleared the mountains and marshes by fire. Thus they helped accomplish deeds upon which myriad generations would forever depend. Among the flourishing assemblies of talent celebrated throughout history, none surpassed these. Later, the Zhou, drawing upon vigorous virtue, undertook campaigns to succor the suffering and punish the guilty. Those who then joined in establishing its enterprise included the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, Nangong Kuo, and San…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宜生太顛閎夭呂望諸臣爲之疏附爲之
先後爲之奔走禦侮以弼成清明之化古
今言才之繼舜而盛者莫加焉夫上有舜
武之爲君而後下有五臣十人爲之佐下
有五臣十人爲之佐而後永頼淸明之化
成人見五臣十人之治獨與于古而不知
舜武相遇之難有如此者故由周而前大
禹承舜禪之後一時共治之臣固當時同
事于虞廷者也雖謂爲有夏之盛焉可也
迨夫成湯不憚三聘之煩而伊尹奏阿衡
之勳高宗信帝賚之夢而傅說成鹽梅之
治向使成湯以五就疏尹而高宗以版築
棄說欲其成伐夏中興之業其可得乎由
周而後當列國分爭之餘秦以戎狄承之
當時諸臣要皆權術遊說之客也雖謂之
無才焉可也迨夫高祖得三傑而以之興
漢昭烈得孔明而以之三分向使高祖以
刀筆棄蕭以跨下棄韓以亡命棄張昭烈
punctuated:
宜生、太顛、閎夭、呂望諸臣，爲之疏附，爲之先後，爲之奔走禦侮，以弼成清明之化，古今言才之繼舜而盛者，莫加焉。夫上有舜、武之爲君，而後下有五臣、十人爲之佐；下有五臣、十人爲之佐，而後永頼淸明之化成。人見五臣、十人之治獨與于古，而不知舜、武相遇之難有如此者。
故由周而前，大禹承舜禪之後，一時共治之臣，固當時同事于虞廷者也，雖謂爲有夏之盛焉可也。迨夫成湯不憚三聘之煩，而伊尹奏阿衡之勳；高宗信帝賚之夢，而傅說成鹽梅之治。向使成湯以五就疏尹，而高宗以版築棄說，欲其成伐夏、中興之業，其可得乎？
由周而後，當列國分爭之餘，秦以戎狄承之，當時諸臣，要皆權術遊說之客也，雖謂之無才焉可也。迨夫高祖得三傑，而以之興漢；昭烈得孔明，而以之三分。向使高祖以刀筆棄蕭，以跨下棄韓，以亡命棄張，昭烈
translation_en:
…Yisheng [completing the name San Yisheng on the preceding page], Tai Dian, Hong Yao, Lü Wang, and the other ministers drew people close to him, supported him before and behind, hastened to serve him, and defended him against affronts, thereby helping bring about enlightened government. Among those spoken of, past and present, as succeeding Shun in the flourishing of talent, none surpassed him. Only with rulers such as Shun and King Wu above could the five ministers and ten worthy men below serve as their assistants; only with these assistants could enlightened government of enduring benefit be achieved. People see the government of the five ministers and ten worthy men as something found only in antiquity, without realizing how difficult it was for such men to encounter rulers like Shun and King Wu.
Looking back before the Zhou, after Yu the Great received the throne through Shun’s abdication, the ministers who governed with him were precisely those who had served together at the court of Shun. It is therefore fair to call this a flourishing of talent under the Xia. Later, Cheng Tang did not shrink from the trouble of issuing three invitations, and Yi Yin rendered distinguished service as chief minister, the A-heng. Gaozong trusted his dream of a gift from the Lord on High, and Fu Yue achieved harmonious government, like salt and sour plums properly blended in cooking. Had Cheng Tang distanced himself from Yi Yin because he had five times entered another ruler’s service, and had Gaozong rejected Fu Yue because he worked at building rammed-earth walls, could they have accomplished the overthrow of the Xia and the restoration of their dynasty?
Looking beyond the Zhou, after the various states had struggled for supremacy, Qin, with its Rong and Di ways, succeeded them. Its ministers were, in essence, all practitioners of expedient stratagems and itinerant persuasion. It is therefore fair to say that it lacked talent. Later, Gaozu obtained the Three Heroes and through them established the Han; Zhaolie obtained Kongming and through him secured a share in the threefold division of the realm. Had Gaozu rejected Xiao because he was a clerk wielding knife and brush, Han because he had crawled beneath another man’s legs, and Zhang because he was a fugitive, and had Zhaolie…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以草莽惜三顧欲成一統三分之業其可
得乎故論才于三代之上者當以才之大
小爲優劣不當以數之多寡爲盛衰彼五
臣者以一人而當億兆人者也盛之盛也
十人者以一人而當千百人者也盛之次
也不然孔子嘆才難而曰唐虞之際于斯
爲盛豈非有見于此哉其論人才于三代
之下者當究其遭時所遇之主而不當以
成敗爲優劣彼三傑之于漢高也遇也孔
===
明之于昭烈也不遇也使三傑當昭烈之
時而孔明遭漢高之主烏知不易地皆然
哉況乎人才各有所長譬則規可以爲圓
而不可以爲方矩可以爲方而不可以爲
圓是物理且然人才可知矣雖在唐虞聞
稷以教稼穡矣而未聞兼乎教與刑也聞
禹以平水土矣而未聞兼乎益也是聖臣
且然其下可知矣故用才盡其所長則以
靈公之無道而王孫賈仲叔圉祝鮀之徒
punctuated: 以草莽惜三顧，欲成一統三分之業，其可得乎？故論才于三代之上者，當以才之大小爲優劣，不當以數之多寡爲盛衰。彼五臣者，以一人而當億兆人者也，盛之盛也；十人者，以一人而當千百人者也，盛之次也。不然，孔子嘆才難而曰：「唐虞之際，于斯爲盛。」豈非有見于此哉？其論人才于三代之下者，當究其遭時所遇之主，而不當以成敗爲優劣。彼三傑之于漢高也，遇也；孔明之于昭烈也，不遇也。使三傑當昭烈之時，而孔明遭漢高之主，烏知不易地皆然哉？況乎人才各有所長，譬則規可以爲圓，而不可以爲方；矩可以爲方，而不可以爲圓。是物理且然，人才可知矣。雖在唐虞，聞稷以教稼穡矣，而未聞兼乎教與刑也；聞禹以平水土矣，而未聞兼乎益也。是聖臣且然，其下可知矣。故用才盡其所長，則以靈公之無道，而王孫賈、仲叔圉、祝鮀之徒
translation_en:
…had begrudged making three visits because Kongming lived in rustic obscurity, could the achievements of unifying the realm and securing one of its three divisions have been attained? Thus, when discussing talent in the Three Dynasties and earlier, one should judge superiority and inferiority by the magnitude of ability, rather than flourishing or decline by the number of talented men. Each of those five ministers was a match for hundreds of millions: this was flourishing at its height. Each of the ten men was a match for hundreds or thousands: this was flourishing of a lesser order. Otherwise, when Confucius lamented how difficult it was to find talent and said, “From the time of Tang and Yu, talent flourished most at this time,” was he not perceiving this very point?

When discussing talented men after the Three Dynasties, one should investigate the times they encountered and the rulers they served, rather than judge their merits by success or failure. The Three Heroes serving Gaozu of Han met with a favorable opportunity; Kongming serving Zhaolie did not. Had the Three Heroes lived in Zhaolie’s time, and had Kongming encountered a ruler such as Gaozu of Han, how do we know that, with their positions exchanged, each would not have fared as the other did?

Moreover, talented men each have their particular strengths. A compass, for example, can make a circle but cannot make a square; a carpenter’s square can make a square but cannot make a circle. If this holds even for the properties of objects, we can understand how it applies to human talent. Even in the age of Tang and Yu, we hear of Ji teaching sowing and reaping, but not of his also taking charge of moral instruction and punishments. We hear of Yu bringing the waters and lands into order, but not of his also undertaking Yi’s duties. If even these sage ministers were so, we can understand how it was with those below them. Thus, when employing talent fully according to each person’s strengths, even with Duke Ling’s lack of the Way, men such as Wangsun Jia, Zhongshu Yu, and Zhu Tuo…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
猶足以存衛苟用矣而信之不篤則以箕
子比干微子之仁而不能以延商用不用
之間而國之存亡以之孰謂人才無關于
治忽哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奮迹南服迅掃腥羶奉
天命以行天討悲人窮以順人心取天下于戎
濁之秋不啻比迹湯武而已然義旗一揮
而豪傑雲集如徐中山之征討四方智勇
超絕常開平之克復中原戰勝攻取鄧寧
河湯東甌之撫定八州所至無敵沐黔寧
===
李岐陽之討平諸夷所向有功他如胡大
海趙德勝桑世傑張德勝耿再成俞通海
諸臣著勳勞于督戰之日又如劉基之運
籌決勝宋濂之學貫天人章溢之忠孝兩
盡吳訥之臣僚讓德固皆一代佐命之元
勳視十人之亂清弘化何以異哉自非我
聖祖求之有道而信之不疑使之以器而任之
不貳其何以收削平之功乎逮我
punctuated:
猶足以存衛。苟用矣而信之不篤，則以箕子、比干、微子之仁，而不能以延商。用不用之間，而國之存亡以之，孰謂人才無關于治忽哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝奮迹南服，迅掃腥羶，奉天命以行天討，悲人窮以順人心，取天下于戎濁之秋，不啻比迹湯武而已。然義旗一揮，而豪傑雲集，如徐中山之征討四方，智勇超絕；常開平之克復中原，戰勝攻取；鄧寧河、湯東甌之撫定八州，所至無敵；沐黔寧、李岐陽之討平諸夷，所向有功。他如胡大海、趙德勝、桑世傑、張德勝、耿再成、俞通海諸臣，著勳勞于督戰之日；又如劉基之運籌決勝，宋濂之學貫天人，章溢之忠孝兩盡，吳訥之臣僚讓德，固皆一代佐命之元勳。視十人之亂清弘化，何以異哉？自非我聖祖求之有道，而信之不疑，使之以器，而任之不貳，其何以收削平之功乎？逮我
translation_en:
…were still sufficient to preserve Wei. If men are employed but not firmly trusted, then even the benevolence of Jizi, Bi Gan, and Weizi cannot prolong the life of Shang. A state's survival or destruction thus depends upon whether men of talent are employed. Who could say that talent has no bearing on order and disorder?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao rose in the southern regions and swiftly swept away the rank and fetid foe. Upholding Heaven's mandate, he carried out Heaven's punishment; pitying the people's distress, he acted in accordance with their hearts. He won All-under-Heaven in an age of alien turmoil [?], doing more than merely matching the achievements of Tang and Wu. Once he raised the banner of righteousness, heroes gathered like clouds. Xu, Duke of Zhongshan, campaigned in all directions with surpassing wisdom and courage. Chang, Prince of Kaiping, recovered the Central Plain, victorious in battle and successful in assault. Deng, Prince of Ninghe, and Tang, Prince of Dong'ou, pacified the eight regions, meeting no worthy opponent wherever they went. Mu, Prince of Qianning, and Li, Prince of Qiyang, subdued the various non-Chinese peoples, achieving success wherever they advanced. Other ministers, including Hu Dahai, Zhao Desheng, Sang Shijie, Zhang Desheng, Geng Zaicheng, and Yu Tonghai, rendered distinguished service while directing battles. Liu Ji devised strategies that secured victory; Song Lian's learning encompassed Heaven and humanity; Zhang Yi fulfilled both loyalty and filial devotion; and Wu Ne possessed virtue to which his fellow ministers deferred [?]. All were foremost meritorious servants who assisted in founding the dynasty. How did they differ from the ten ministers who brought order and extended transforming influence [?]? Had our sagely founder not sought them by the proper means, trusted them without suspicion, employed them according to their abilities, and entrusted them with responsibility without wavering, how could he have achieved the conquest and pacification of the realm? Coming down to our …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
列聖光紹景命旁招俊彥可謂先後一揆矣而
海內者碩之士靡不向風景附雖不越乎
吏議之常而去古未遠辟召屢行眞才接
踵而出有由然哉我
皇上嗣登大寶撫有成業謂明良交而德業成
則敦禮耆舊輔弼之臣信之必專謂賢才
輔而天下治則博開登崇俊良之門而立
之無方謂野有遺賢也而辟舉之政行焉
謂遺佚可錄也而起用之
===
詔下焉方今賢俊滿朝而寸長片善之必錄忠
良顯遂而一才一藝無不庸宜乎用有餘
才官不乏人矣夫何頃者邊陲多事南北
騷然當事之臣試之寡效司銓者將愼選
以充而臨事恒致有乏才之嘆此執事所
以欲得跅弛之才以佐成亨嘉之會也自
今言之天生一代之才自周一代之用未
聞藉才於異代者也必也在廊廟之上則
于公孤之才而隆其禮焉時勤訪問如古
punctuated:
列聖光紹景命，旁招俊彥，可謂先後一揆矣。而海內者碩之士，靡不向風景附。雖不越乎吏議之常，而去古未遠，辟召屢行，眞才接踵而出，有由然哉！
我皇上嗣登大寶，撫有成業，謂明良交而德業成，則敦禮耆舊輔弼之臣，信之必專；謂賢才輔而天下治，則博開登崇俊良之門，而立之無方；謂野有遺賢也，而辟舉之政行焉；謂遺佚可錄也，而起用之詔下焉。方今賢俊滿朝，而寸長片善之必錄；忠良顯遂，而一才一藝無不庸。宜乎用有餘才，官不乏人矣。
夫何頃者邊陲多事，南北騷然，當事之臣試之寡效？司銓者將愼選以充，而臨事恒致有乏才之嘆。此執事所以欲得跅弛之才，以佐成亨嘉之會也。自今言之，天生一代之才，自周一代之用，未聞藉才於異代者也。必也在廊廟之上，則于公孤之才而隆其禮焉，時勤訪問，如古
translation_en:
…the successive sage emperors gloriously continued the great Mandate and sought outstanding men far and wide. Their guiding principle, early and late, may indeed be called one and the same. Throughout the realm, men of eminent learning [?] all turned toward their influence and attached themselves like shadows. Although this remained within the ordinary procedures of official deliberation, it was not far removed from antiquity: summonses to service were repeatedly issued, and men of genuine talent emerged one after another. Surely there was a reason for this!
Our Emperor succeeded to the imperial throne and took possession of an established enterprise. Holding that virtue and achievement are perfected through the association of an enlightened ruler with worthy ministers, he treats elderly and longstanding ministers who assist him with generous courtesy and places undivided trust in them. Holding that the realm is well governed when worthy and talented men give their aid, he opens wide the avenues for advancing outstanding men and appoints them without restriction. Holding that worthy men remain overlooked outside official service, he implements measures for summoning and recommending them. Holding that those left in obscurity deserve consideration, he issues decrees appointing them to service. Today, worthy and outstanding men fill the court, and even the smallest strength or slightest merit is sure to receive recognition. Loyal and good men attain distinction, and no talent or skill goes unused. One would therefore expect talent to be more than sufficient for employment and offices never to lack suitable men.
Why, then, have troubles lately multiplied on the frontiers, with unrest in both north and south, while the ministers responsible have achieved little when put to the test? Those responsible for personnel selection intend to choose carefully to fill the posts, yet whenever affairs arise, they repeatedly find cause to lament a shortage of talent. This is why you, honored examiners, wish to obtain men of unrestrained talent to help bring about an auspicious convergence of ruler and worthy ministers. Speaking of the present, Heaven produces the talent of each age sufficient to meet that age’s needs; never have we heard of borrowing talent from another age. Surely, at the imperial court, men with the talents of the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Dignitaries should be accorded heightened courtesy and diligently consulted from time to time, as in antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之都俞吁咈于一堂而伊傅周召之才端
可見矣在邊陲之遠則于封疆之臣而盡
其能焉責之以成功而不束以文法則李
郭韓范之才端可見矣于郡邑之吏而重
其任焉假以歲月期以成績如漢之贈金
增秩則不必寤寐循良而龔黃卓魯之才
有不可見乎于將師之臣而優其權焉厚
供餽以恤其私貸小過以圖其大如古之
謗書盈篋而不惑則不必拊髀思將而頗
===
牧起翦之才有不復見乎制科善矣而空
言無補不有鄉舉里選之遺意可兼舉乎
大比校藝之外俾有司錄其德誼之實與
夫才之所優而參考之則德成而上藝成
而下眞才有不輩出焉否也養道豫矣而
記誦徒勤不有三物之教蘇湖治事之遺
法可兼舉乎月省歲會之餘而又必任其
才之所宜志之所欲如星曆戰陣營田水
利之類士以此而優劣官以此而殿最眞
punctuated:
之都俞吁咈于一堂，而伊傅周召之才端可見矣。在邊陲之遠，則于封疆之臣而盡其能焉，責之以成功而不束以文法，則李郭韓范之才端可見矣。于郡邑之吏而重其任焉，假以歲月，期以成績，如漢之贈金增秩，則不必寤寐循良，而龔黃卓魯之才有不可見乎？于將師之臣而優其權焉，厚供餽以恤其私，貸小過以圖其大，如古之謗書盈篋而不惑，則不必拊髀思將，而頗牧起翦之才有不復見乎？

制科善矣，而空言無補，不有鄉舉里選之遺意可兼舉乎？大比校藝之外，俾有司錄其德誼之實與夫才之所優而參考之，則德成而上，藝成而下，眞才有不輩出焉否也？養道豫矣，而記誦徒勤，不有三物之教、蘇湖治事之遺法可兼舉乎？月省歲會之餘，而又必任其才之所宜、志之所欲，如星曆、戰陣、營田、水利之類，士以此而優劣，官以此而殿最，眞
translation_en:
…voicing assent and dissent together in one hall, as in antiquity; then talents like those of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao would surely appear. In the distant borderlands, allow the officials responsible for frontier defense to exercise their abilities fully. Hold them accountable for success without constraining them with legal formalities; then talents like those of Li, Guo, Han, and Fan would surely appear. Give weight to the responsibilities of prefectural and county officials, allow them time, and expect accomplishments from them, rewarding them with gold and increased rank as under the Han. Then, without having to yearn waking and sleeping for upright and capable administrators, could talents like those of Gong, Huang, Zhuo, and Lu fail to appear? Grant military commanders ample authority, provide generous supplies to attend to their personal needs, and pardon small faults with a view to their greater achievements. As in the ancient example of remaining unshaken even when slanderous letters filled a chest, there would then be no need to slap one's thigh and long for a general: could talents like those of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wu Qi, and Wang Jian fail to appear again?

The examination system is good, yet empty words bring no practical benefit. Could we not also adopt something of the old practice of recommendation from townships and selection from villages? Besides assessing literary proficiency at the triennial examination, have the responsible officials record solid evidence of candidates' virtue and proper conduct, together with their particular strengths, and consider these jointly. Then those accomplished in virtue would be placed above those accomplished in literary skills. Could true talent fail to emerge in abundance? The means of nurturing talent have been provided beforehand, yet mere memorization and recitation consume effort in vain. Could we not also adopt the teaching of the Three Things and the surviving methods of instruction in practical affairs used at Suzhou and Huzhou? In addition to monthly inspections and annual assessments, students must be assigned work suited to their abilities and aspirations, in such fields as astronomy and calendrical calculation, military formations, agricultural development, and water management. Let students be judged superior or inferior on this basis, and officials ranked lowest or highest on this basis; true…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
才有不豫養焉否也至于犇逸不羈之才
冥飛遐舉之士有不囿于庠序之所養制
科之可羅者則載之于垂綸可也起之于
築巖可也三聘而陟阿衡之任一舉而登
大將之壇亦可也雖然求才固有其道而
用才尤有其本又必純心以任之則讒諂
不得以亂正而貴德之義盡夫然後可以
感會風雲以翊成
昌熙之治以比隆唐虞三代之盛矣故曰純心
===
要矣用賢爲急焉
第四問
閻應儒
同考試官教諭孟　批
大議對雅達政源且探事獻說言中肯綮而復標以顯義約以
裕財需效於久則先先務其
考試官教諭張　批
正詞所謂治練而文工者也是珠桂璀斯爲稍稱宜冠諸作
瞻裁淹博偉識遠猷深爲嘉見
考試官學正高　批
於言外盡其詞鮑其旨遂者也宜試多士
敷敘周於藻藉區畫契人意表
punctuated:
才有不豫養焉否也？至于犇逸不羈之才、冥飛遐舉之士，有不囿于庠序之所養、制科之可羅者，則載之于垂綸可也，起之于築巖可也，三聘而陟阿衡之任，一舉而登大將之壇，亦可也。雖然，求才固有其道，而用才尤有其本，又必純心以任之，則讒諂不得以亂正，而貴德之義盡。夫然後可以感會風雲，以翊成昌熙之治，以比隆唐虞三代之盛矣。故曰：「純心要矣，用賢爲急焉。」

第四問
閻應儒

同考試官教諭孟　批
大議對雅，達政源，且探事獻說，言中肯綮，而復標以顯義，約以裕財，需效於久，則先先務其。

考試官教諭張　批
正詞，所謂治練而文工者也。是珠桂璀，斯爲稍稱，宜冠諸作。瞻裁淹博，偉識遠猷，深爲嘉見。

考試官學正高　批
於言外盡其詞，鮑其旨遂者也，宜試多士。敷敘周於藻藉，區畫契人意表。
translation_en:
…could talent then fail to be nurtured in advance? As for talents that range freely, unrestrained, and scholars who soar into the distant heights, some fall outside what the schools can nurture or the examination system can encompass. One may take such a man into one’s carriage from where he fishes, or summon him from building walls among the cliffs. One may also invite him three times and raise him to the office of chief minister (aheng), or at a single stroke bring him onto the platform of a general-in-chief. Nevertheless, although seeking talent has its proper methods, employing it has an even more fundamental basis. One must entrust responsibilities to worthy men with a pure heart; then slander and flattery cannot confound what is right, and the principle of honoring virtue is fully realized. Only then can ruler and ministers respond to one another like wind and cloud, helping to establish flourishing and glorious government that rivals the splendor of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Thus it is said: “Purity of heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent.”

Fourth policy question
Yan Yingru

Comment by Associate Examiner Meng, Instructor:
“The discussion is substantial and the response elegant [?], reaching the sources of government. It also investigates affairs and offers proposals; its words strike the crucial points. Furthermore, it sets forth and makes clear the principles, advocates economy to increase financial resources, and looks for results over the long term. Thus it gives priority to urgent tasks … [?].”

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor:
“Upright in its language: this is what is meant by mastery of government and skill in composition. These pearls and cassia gleam [?]; this may be considered somewhat fitting and deserves to stand first among the compositions. Its conception and composition are comprehensive and learned [?]; its outstanding discernment and far-reaching plans are deeply commendable.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Instructor:
“Beyond the words, it gives full expression to its language and carries through its purport [?]; it is fitting for testing the many scholars [?]. Its exposition is comprehensive in its literary embellishment [?], and its planning accords with intentions beyond what people express [?].”

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天下有事若反而相濟言若迂而實切者
固衆人之所疑而達者之所信善謀國者
不可以弗辨也今夫足國之道固貴乎竭
智畢慮以拯一時之急尤貴乎深思長顧
以爲攸久之圖然人情喜于欲速而厭于
持久則未有不以一時爲切而持久爲迂
者也殊不知國之病財譬人之病瘍也瘍
有瘵之以峻削則悅有告以蓀艾元和則
咈然怒曰此庸醫也曾何足以謀吾瘍卒
===
之瘍愈劇而元和日耗其曷能及乎易有
之曰何以聚人曰財書八政一曰食二曰
貨此財用民食天下國家之大計也在昔
成周兵以私田而不餉士大夫以公田而
不廩歲時經費不越乎祭祀宴饗服輿匪
頒好用數者而已周公方且憂之總其權
于家宰而又有司會司書職幣職歲以防
其微有參互日要歲會以考其成是周之
所以理財者理其財之出而已非以理其
punctuated:
天下有事若反而相濟，言若迂而實切者，固衆人之所疑，而達者之所信。善謀國者，不可以弗辨也。今夫足國之道，固貴乎竭智畢慮，以拯一時之急；尤貴乎深思長顧，以爲攸久之圖。然人情喜于欲速而厭于持久，則未有不以一時爲切而持久爲迂者也。殊不知國之病財，譬人之病瘍也。瘍有瘵之以峻削則悅，有告以蓀艾元和則咈然怒曰：「此庸醫也，曾何足以謀吾瘍！」卒之瘍愈劇，而元和日耗，其曷能及乎？
易有之曰：「何以聚人？曰財。」書八政，一曰食，二曰貨。此財用民食，天下國家之大計也。在昔成周，兵以私田而不餉，士大夫以公田而不廩，歲時經費不越乎祭祀、宴饗、服輿、匪頒、好用數者而已。周公方且憂之，總其權于家宰，而又有司會、司書、職幣、職歲以防其微，有參互、日要、歲會以考其成。是周之所以理財者，理其財之出而已，非以理其
translation_en:
There are affairs in the world that seem opposed yet complement one another, and proposals that seem far-fetched yet are truly pertinent. These are precisely what ordinary people doubt and discerning people trust. Those skilled in planning for the state must distinguish them. The way to make the state’s resources sufficient certainly calls for exhausting one’s intelligence and deliberation to relieve an immediate emergency; still more, it calls for deep reflection and a far-reaching view to devise enduring plans. Yet people delight in quick results and dislike sustained effort, so they invariably regard immediate measures as pertinent and enduring ones as impractical. They fail to understand that a state’s financial affliction resembles a person’s ulcer. The sufferer is pleased when someone treats it with drastic purgation [?], but if advised to use fragrant herbs and mugwort to restore his vital harmony [?], he angrily declares: “This is an incompetent physician! How could he possibly treat my ulcer?” In the end, the ulcer grows worse and his vital harmony dwindles daily. How could a remedy then come in time?
The Book of Changes says: “How are people gathered together? Through wealth.” Among the eight concerns of government in the Book of Documents, the first is food and the second is goods. Financial resources and the people’s food supply are thus great concerns of governing the realm and the state. In the former days of the Zhou, soldiers supported themselves from private fields and received no military pay; officers and grandees supported themselves from public fields and received no grain stipends. Regular annual expenditure extended only to sacrifices, banquets, clothing and carriages, distributions of provisions, and gifts. Yet the Duke of Zhou remained concerned about it. He concentrated authority over these matters in the Grand Steward (jiazai), while also appointing a Controller of Accounts (sihui), a Director of Records (sishu), an official in charge of valuables (zhibi), and an official in charge of annual expenditure (zhisui), to guard against even minute irregularities. Cross-checks, daily summaries, and annual accounts served to assess their results. Thus, the Zhou’s management of finance consisted solely in managing the outflow of its resources, rather than managing its …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
財之入也理之于上者不欲虐取之于下
而已非固屑屑然如役不憚煩也自是茅
茨之風遠而土木繁興禮讓之俗易而征
役不息此財用之所以日詘而徵輸之所
以日亟也逮漢之文帝玄默躬脩仁厚待
下非無所事財也然惜中人之産以罷露
臺集上書之囊以爲帷幕歲蠲田租輒復
除去與天下生養而休息之雖賈誼之建
議禮樂未遑而當時海內殷阜府庫充溢
===
史稱其漢家享國長久皆文帝所留有由
然矣至于武帝聰察彊毅喜于有爲非不
知重民也然泰時作而禱祀頻瀆兵革黷
而工役紛擾仁義外施多慾內存舉天下
之力而盡斂之雖其任用桑弘羊之徒筭
及商車而得不償失海內虛耗史謂其蠹
國罷民靡費元氣不爲虛語矣夫文帝不
有其利而財用以贏譬則箕裘之子雖無
所猷爲而恪守節儉故業自有餘裕也武
punctuated:
財之入也。理之于上者，不欲虐取之于下而已，非固屑屑然如役不憚煩也。自是茅茨之風遠，而土木繁興；禮讓之俗易，而征役不息。此財用之所以日詘，而徵輸之所以日亟也。逮漢之文帝，玄默躬脩，仁厚待下，非無所事財也。然惜中人之産以罷露臺，集上書之囊以爲帷幕，歲蠲田租，輒復除去，與天下生養而休息之。雖賈誼之建議禮樂未遑，而當時海內殷阜，府庫充溢。史稱其漢家享國長久，皆文帝所留，有由然矣。
至于武帝，聰察彊毅，喜于有爲，非不知重民也。然泰時作而禱祀頻瀆，兵革黷而工役紛擾，仁義外施，多慾內存，舉天下之力而盡斂之。雖其任用桑弘羊之徒，筭及商車，而得不償失，海內虛耗。史謂其蠹國罷民，靡費元氣，不爲虛語矣。
夫文帝不有其利，而財用以贏，譬則箕裘之子，雖無所猷爲，而恪守節儉，故業自有餘裕也。武
translation_en:
…the inflow of wealth. Those who managed it above sought only to avoid exacting it cruelly from those below; they were certainly not fussing over details like servants who never shrink from troublesome work. Thereafter, the spirit of living beneath thatched roofs grew remote, and building projects proliferated; customs of ritual propriety and deference changed, and levies and labor service became unceasing. This is why public resources dwindled daily, while demands for tax payments grew ever more urgent. When Emperor Wen of the Han came to rule, he quietly cultivated himself and treated his subjects with benevolence and generosity. It was not that he had no occasion to spend. Yet, out of concern for the equivalent of an ordinary household’s property, he abandoned the construction of the Dew Terrace; he collected the bags used to submit memorials and made them into curtains. He remitted the land tax for the year and repeatedly granted further exemptions, allowing all under Heaven to sustain themselves and recuperate. Although he had not yet found time to implement Jia Yi’s proposals concerning rites and music, the realm was then prosperous and its treasuries and granaries brimmed over. The historians’ assertion that the Han dynasty’s long tenure owed entirely to Emperor Wen’s legacy thus had good grounds.
As for Emperor Wu, he was discerning, forceful, and resolute, and delighted in undertaking great enterprises. It was not that he failed to understand the importance of the people. Yet the Tai altar was built [?], and prayers and sacrifices became so frequent as to be irreverent; warfare was pursued recklessly, and construction labor caused widespread disruption. Benevolence and righteousness were displayed outwardly, while numerous desires remained within. He drew upon the strength of the entire realm and exacted everything from it. Although he employed men such as Sang Hongyang and extended taxation even to merchants’ carts, the gains did not compensate for the losses, and the realm was depleted. The historians’ statement that he impoverished the state, exhausted the people, and squandered its vital energies was no empty assertion.
Emperor Wen did not appropriate the profits for himself, and public resources consequently showed a surplus. He was like an heir to a family trade: although he initiated no great undertaking, he conscientiously maintained frugality, and so the inherited estate naturally provided more than enough. Emperor Wu…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
帝以利爲利而國事日蹙譬則鉅積之室
雖善于摧権而驕奢亡度故難與長守富
也是則節與不節之間而崇本逐末之效
已昭然矣唐之財賦有劉晏以司度支而
又有裴肅以刺史進羡綬以判官進裴延
齡皇甫鎛以聚斂進要之專利于上爲國
之蠹孰若李翶所謂人知厚斂之可以富
國而不知薄斂之爲富愈大爲有見哉宋
之財賦有陳恕以董磨勘而又有景德會
計錄皇祐會計錄治平會計錄雖皆所以
總括邦計孰若蘇轍之元祐錄其要主于
節用以厚民生爲有得哉肆我
===
聖祖當順天革命之初而蠲民田租之令無歳
不下然國無廢典民有餘貲是我
聖祖之所以結人心而凝天命者端有在矣我
列聖承重熙累洽之運而任土作賦之外一無
所括然賦不加增而用不加損是我
列聖之所以撫
punctuated:
帝以利爲利，而國事日蹙。譬則鉅積之室，雖善于摧権，而驕奢亡度，故難與長守富也。是則節與不節之間，而崇本逐末之效已昭然矣。唐之財賦，有劉晏以司度支，而又有裴肅以刺史進羡，綬以判官進，裴延齡、皇甫鎛以聚斂進。要之，專利于上，爲國之蠹。孰若李翶所謂「人知厚斂之可以富國，而不知薄斂之爲富愈大」爲有見哉！宋之財賦，有陳恕以董磨勘，而又有《景德會計錄》《皇祐會計錄》《治平會計錄》，雖皆所以總括邦計，孰若蘇轍之《元祐錄》，其要主于節用以厚民生，爲有得哉！
肆我聖祖，當順天革命之初，而蠲民田租之令無歳不下。然國無廢典，民有餘貲，是我聖祖之所以結人心而凝天命者，端有在矣。我列聖承重熙累洽之運，而任土作賦之外，一無所括。然賦不加增，而用不加損，是我列聖之所以撫
translation_en:
…Emperor Wu treated profit as his objective, and the affairs of state grew daily more straitened. This was like a household with great accumulated wealth: however skilled it might be at financial manipulation [?], its boundless arrogance and extravagance made it difficult to preserve its riches for long. Thus, the consequences of honoring the root or pursuing the branches are already plainly apparent in the distinction between frugality and its absence. In the fiscal administration of the Tang, Liu Yan supervised revenue and expenditure; but there were also Pei Su, who presented surplus revenues as a prefect, Shou [?], who advanced as an administrative assistant, and Pei Yanling and Huangfu Bo, who advanced through exacting wealth. In essence, they concentrated profits in the hands of those above and became parasites upon the state. How could they match the insight of Li Ao’s statement: “People know that heavy taxation can enrich the state, but do not know that light taxation produces still greater wealth”? In the fiscal administration of the Song, Chen Shu supervised fiscal auditing, and there were also the Jingde Fiscal Accounts, the Huangyou Fiscal Accounts, and the Zhiping Fiscal Accounts. Although all these comprehensively surveyed state finances, how could they match the sound understanding of Su Zhe’s Yuanyou Records, whose central principle was to economize on expenditure in order to improve the people’s livelihood?
Thus our sagely founder, at the outset of his dynastic revolution in obedience to Heaven, issued orders remitting the people’s land taxes every year without fail. Yet no prescribed state observances were neglected, and the people had wealth to spare. Our sagely founder’s means of winning the people’s hearts and securing Heaven’s Mandate assuredly had a firm foundation. Our successive sage emperors inherited an era of accumulating prosperity and enduring harmony. Beyond levying taxes according to the productive capacity of the land, they extracted nothing further. Yet taxation did not increase, nor did expenditure diminish. Such were the means by which our successive sage emperors safeguarded…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
鴻業而致盛治者必有道矣恭惟我
皇上踐阼五位保有萬方當
臨御之始首罷不急之役大黜非經之科
登極有詔
建儲有詔一則曰天下生民十分困窮一則曰
朕加意節省用自有餘
蠲田租
停間架凡所以征諸民者可謂薄矣夫何頃
歲以來閭閻一歉遂至相食邊鎮告急恒
===
欲脫巾大司農賸度無策時稱匱乏至
請下廷臣條爲理財集議一書檄行天下各陳
所見無非廣忠益集衆思求所以爲足國
裕民之計也今觀其書曰錢法曰山礦曰
屯鹽曰增稅凡以闢財之源者至矣曰清
邊費曰計經費曰裁冗費凡以節財之流
者至矣爲謀不同而同于籌
國家之用籌用不一而一于紓目前之急然
自今言之田有履畝之租户有丁口之役
punctuated:
鴻業而致盛治者，必有道矣。恭惟我皇上踐阼五位，保有萬方。當臨御之始，首罷不急之役，大黜非經之科。登極有詔，建儲有詔：一則曰「天下生民十分困窮」，一則曰「朕加意節省，用自有餘」。蠲田租，停間架，凡所以征諸民者，可謂薄矣。夫何頃歲以來，閭閻一歉，遂至相食；邊鎮告急，恒欲脫巾；大司農賸度無策，時稱匱乏，至請下廷臣條爲《理財集議》一書，檄行天下，各陳所見，無非廣忠益、集衆思，求所以爲足國裕民之計也。
今觀其書，曰錢法，曰山礦，曰屯鹽，曰增稅，凡以闢財之源者至矣；曰清邊費，曰計經費，曰裁冗費，凡以節財之流者至矣。爲謀不同，而同于籌國家之用；籌用不一，而一于紓目前之急。然自今言之，田有履畝之租，户有丁口之役。
translation_en:
…in sustaining the grand imperial enterprise and bringing about flourishing government, they must surely have had their way. Reverently considering our Emperor, he has ascended the throne to the fifth position [?] and holds dominion over all regions. At the beginning of his reign, he first abolished nonessential labor services and swept away irregular levies. An edict marked his accession, and another the designation of the heir apparent. One declared, “The people throughout the realm are in utter hardship and poverty”; the other, “I shall give particular attention to economy, and there will naturally be enough for expenditure.” He remitted land taxes and suspended the tax assessed on the bays of buildings. The exactions imposed on the people may thus be called light. Why, then, in recent years has a single poor harvest brought ordinary communities to the point of eating one another? Why, when the frontier garrisons report emergencies, are they constantly on the verge of casting off their headcloths [?]? The Minister of Revenue has no plan for reckoning available resources [?] and repeatedly reports shortages. Matters have reached the point of requesting that the issue be referred to the court officials, whose proposals were arranged into a book, Collected Deliberations on Managing the Finances, and circulated by official dispatch throughout the realm, inviting everyone to state their views. All this was intended to broaden the benefit of loyal counsel and gather collective wisdom, seeking a plan to provide adequately for the state and enrich the people.
Looking now at this book, we find proposals on currency policy, mountain mines, agricultural colonies and salt administration, and increased taxation: every means of opening sources of revenue has been pursued to the utmost. We find proposals to scrutinize frontier expenditure, calculate regular expenditure, and cut superfluous expenditure: every means of restricting the outflow of funds has been pursued to the utmost. The proposals differ, but all seek to provide for the needs of the state; their methods of provision vary, but all seek relief from the immediate emergency. Yet, speaking of present conditions, fields bear taxes assessed by acreage, and households bear service obligations assessed by their registered persons…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
門有事產之徵商有行貨之稅昔人所謂
兵役興而邊民困賦役煩而農民困鹽鐵
算緡而商民困貴爵免罪而富民困入財
爲郎而世家困今皆有之誠有如
天語所謂天下十分困窮者也其諸繰絲者非
特見蛹將併其蛹食之矣其諸漁者非特
絕魚將併其澤枯之矣昔魯哀公以年饑
爲憂而孔子告之以薄斂彼聖人豈固好
反其所見而爲是迂闊之論哉無亦深探
其本而導以利之大者乎至如魏文侯于
賀增賦者則以爲貪其賦稅而不愛人是
虞人反裘負薪而不知皮盡毛將安附也
彼文侯豈不欲專利自殖而爲是矯飾之
言哉無亦有見于國本所在有不可斁者
乎今之言曰邊餉有定額
朝廷有定費
宗室有常祿官廩有常供此而益之猶患不
給賦而不加其何以濟愚竊以爲不然蓋
punctuated: 門有事產之徵，商有行貨之稅。昔人所謂兵役興而邊民困，賦役煩而農民困，鹽鐵算緡而商民困，貴爵免罪而富民困，入財爲郎而世家困，今皆有之。誠有如天語所謂天下十分困窮者也。其諸繰絲者非特見蛹，將併其蛹食之矣；其諸漁者非特絕魚，將併其澤枯之矣。昔魯哀公以年饑爲憂，而孔子告之以薄斂。彼聖人豈固好反其所見而爲是迂闊之論哉？無亦深探其本而導以利之大者乎？至如魏文侯，于賀增賦者，則以爲貪其賦稅而不愛人，是虞人反裘負薪，而不知皮盡毛將安附也。彼文侯豈不欲專利自殖，而爲是矯飾之言哉？無亦有見于國本所在，有不可斁者乎？今之言曰：「邊餉有定額，朝廷有定費，宗室有常祿，官廩有常供，此而益之，猶患不給；賦而不加，其何以濟？」愚竊以爲不然，蓋
translation_en:
…households face levies on business property [?], and merchants face taxes on goods in transit. Earlier writers spoke of frontier people impoverished by the mobilization of military service; farmers impoverished by burdensome taxes and labor services; merchants impoverished by salt and iron monopolies and taxes on their capital; wealthy people impoverished by purchasing costly noble ranks and remission of punishment; and hereditary families impoverished by contributing wealth to obtain appointments as gentlemen. All these conditions exist today. Truly, as the Emperor’s own words declare, all under Heaven is in utter destitution. Those reeling silk will seemingly not merely expose the pupae [?], but consume the pupae as well; those fishing will not merely exhaust the fish, but drain their marshes dry as well.

Long ago, Duke Ai of Lu was troubled by a year of famine, and Confucius advised him to reduce exactions. Did that sage really delight in contradicting what he saw and offering such impractical counsel? Was it not rather that he probed deeply into the root of the matter and guided the duke toward the greater benefit? Likewise, when someone congratulated Marquis Wen of Wei on increased tax revenues, he considered that to covet tax revenues without caring for the people was like a woodsman carrying firewood with his fur coat turned inside out, unaware that once the hide was worn away, the fur would have nothing to cling to. Was Marquis Wen unwilling to monopolize profits and enrich himself merely so that he could utter these pretentiously virtuous words? Was it not rather that he understood where the foundation of the state lay, and that it must not be ruined?

People today say: “Frontier military provisions have fixed quotas; the court has fixed expenses; members of the imperial clan have regular stipends; and official granaries have regular supplies to furnish. Even if these are increased, we still fear they will be insufficient. Unless taxes are raised, how can we meet these needs?” In my humble judgment, this is not so, for…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
常觀之行者策疲羸之馬于千里之途策
愈急而疲愈甚曾不知少休焉將不至于
蹶不止也今民之將蹶亦久矣可不思所
以少息乎爲今之計田之正額不可省也
而塞下之荒屯郡國之蕪田可不任民所
墾乎今誠使民曰不清丈不起科行之數
年將中外無不墾之田矣中外無不墾之
田則粟米狼戾邊人得以倍食游民得有
常業是不轉餉而餉自足不賑貸而民無
===
失所也況地闢則人聚將又有不待召募
僞增而邊戍戶口有餘裕矣當年之賦不
可已也而均傜之提編逋稅之帶徵可不
輟而蠲乎今誠示民曰民間一歲所入止
有此數其可忍併徵以盡人財如此則所
紓民力皆國之力所裕民財皆國之財也
況新稅不逋則歲有常盈前者不加則後
者可繼矣至如鈔法者
國家所以操利權于上而不制于天不聽于
punctuated: 常觀之，行者策疲羸之馬于千里之途，策愈急而疲愈甚，曾不知少休焉，將不至于蹶不止也。今民之將蹶亦久矣，可不思所以少息乎？爲今之計，田之正額不可省也，而塞下之荒屯、郡國之蕪田，可不任民所墾乎？今誠使民曰：「不清丈，不起科。」行之數年，將中外無不墾之田矣。中外無不墾之田，則粟米狼戾，邊人得以倍食，游民得有常業，是不轉餉而餉自足，不賑貸而民無失所也。況地闢則人聚，將又有不待召募僞增而邊戍戶口有餘裕矣。當年之賦不可已也，而均傜之提編、逋稅之帶徵，可不輟而蠲乎？今誠示民曰：「民間一歲所入，止有此數，其可忍併徵以盡人財？」如此，則所紓民力皆國之力，所裕民財皆國之財也。況新稅不逋，則歲有常盈；前者不加，則後者可繼矣。至如鈔法者，國家所以操利權于上，而不制于天、不聽于
translation_en:
…I have often observed this: a traveler whips an exhausted, emaciated horse along a journey of a thousand li. The more urgently he whips it, the more exhausted it becomes. Unaware that he should let it rest a little, he will not stop until it collapses. The people, too, have long been on the verge of collapse. Can we fail to consider how to give them a little respite? For present purposes, the regular land-tax quota cannot be reduced. But should we not allow the people freely to reclaim abandoned agricultural garrison lands along the frontier and uncultivated fields throughout the prefectures? If we truly told the people, “There will be no cadastral resurvey and no new tax assessment,” and maintained this policy for several years, no land in the interior or on the frontier would remain uncultivated. With all such land under cultivation, grain would be abundant, frontier inhabitants would have twice as much to eat, and people without settled livelihoods would gain regular occupations. Military provisions would thus be sufficient without transporting supplies, and the people would have secure livelihoods without relief loans. Moreover, as land is opened up, people will gather there; the frontier garrisons would have ample households and population without waiting for recruitment or fictitious increases [?].

The current year’s taxes cannot be suspended. But could we not halt and remit the advance levying of equalized corvée obligations and the collection of tax arrears alongside current dues? Let us truly make this clear to the people: “The people’s annual income amounts to only so much. How could we bear to collect these levies together and exhaust their resources?” In this way, all the people’s strength that we spare is the state’s strength, and all the people’s wealth that we allow to grow is the state’s wealth. Moreover, if current taxes do not fall into arrears, there will be a regular annual surplus. If earlier liabilities are not added to present demands, subsequent payments can continue.

As for the paper-currency system, it is the means by which the state retains control over financial advantage at the top, without being constrained by Heaven or subject to…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人者也此法廢而財源始聽命于下矣今
之鈔法旣不可復可不通其變而易之爲
泉布乎鹽法者
國家所以因地之利以代飛輓以充軍實者
也自鈔法廢而餘鹽不輸于官私鹽日益
廣矣今泉布可舉則可不復其
舊制而厚償以收其餘乎謂
宗室爲天潢所宜厚是矣然爵不可降而祿
與時宜在
===
太祖初年已議裁省今法其意而因世以定殺
可也謂社倉爲荒政之義舉是矣然以官
强之則不勝其騷然在昔家給人足與發
自藉令任其便而勿煩其政令可也不但
已也蘇軾所謂三冗其在于今非冗所當
去者乎其曰冗吏非特郡邑佐幕丞使之
微所當裁也由丞簿而上凡中外鄉大夫
武廕常侍之屬試職
祖宗之列簿而考之不有所當議乎其曰冗兵
punctuated: 人者也。此法廢，而財源始聽命于下矣。今之鈔法旣不可復，可不通其變而易之爲泉布乎？鹽法者，國家所以因地之利，以代飛輓，以充軍實者也。自鈔法廢，而餘鹽不輸于官，私鹽日益廣矣。今泉布可舉，則可不復其舊制，而厚償以收其餘乎？謂宗室爲天潢所宜厚，是矣。然爵不可降，而祿與時宜。在太祖初年，已議裁省，今法其意，而因世以定殺，可也。謂社倉爲荒政之義舉，是矣。然以官强之，則不勝其騷然。在昔家給人足，與發自藉令，任其便而勿煩其政令，可也。不但已也，蘇軾所謂三冗，其在于今，非冗所當去者乎？其曰冗吏，非特郡邑佐幕丞使之微所當裁也。由丞簿而上，凡中外鄉大夫、武廕常侍之屬，試職祖宗之列簿而考之，不有所當議乎？其曰冗兵，
translation_en:
…people. Once this system was abolished, the sources of revenue began to fall under the control of those below. Since the paper-currency system cannot now be restored, should we not adapt to changed circumstances and replace it with coinage?

The salt system is the means by which the state draws upon the advantages of the land to replace arduous supply transport and replenish military provisions. Since the paper-currency system was abolished, surplus salt has ceased to be delivered to the authorities, and illicit salt has circulated ever more widely. If coinage can now be introduced, should we not restore the old system and offer generous payment to purchase the surplus?

It is right to say that members of the imperial clan, as descendants of the imperial line, deserve generous treatment. Yet although their noble ranks cannot be lowered, their stipends should suit the circumstances of the time. Already in the early years of Taizu’s reign, reductions were discussed. We may now follow his intention and determine graduated reductions according to present circumstances.

It is right to say that community granaries are a righteous undertaking for famine relief. Yet if officials compel people to establish them, the resulting disturbance becomes unbearable. In former times, households had adequate supplies and individuals had enough; the following wording concerning how the undertaking originated is unclear [?]. It would be acceptable to let people act as convenient for them, without burdening them with official commands.

Nor is this all. Are not the three kinds of redundancy spoken of by Su Shi, as they exist today, redundancies that ought to be eliminated? As for redundant officials, it is not merely the minor posts of prefectural and county assistants, staff officers, vice magistrates, and commissioners [?] that should be reduced. From vice magistrates and registrars upward, among all the central and local dignitaries [?], those holding posts through military protection privileges, and regular attendants, if we were to consult [?] the registers of the imperial ancestors and examine them, would there not be matters requiring deliberation? As for redundant soldiers…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者非特郡國之兵所當抑也內而宿衛之
士外而邊陲之徒試取
國家之尺籍而檢之不有所當汰乎其曰冗
食非特闒闠僭侈不經所當禁也由內外
百司庶府之所需以至于無名徵誅掊克
之所括有不可裁者乎夫如是爲之在我
者旣以制節謹度不爲耗利之端施之在
上者又以導利于民而不爲專利之計是
雖不足以給目前一時之急而民富則國
不至于獨貧實所以爲萬世悠久之利也
===
此在吾
君吾相一心以爲天下而不爲自便之圖凡謀
有合于遠大勿嫌于更張言有裨于
社稷勿遺于芻蕘然後君子策羣力之畢集而足
國足民之道或庶幾矣愚生狂瞽之見如
此執事其勿以爲迂焉
第五問
戴廷禮
punctuated:
者，非特郡國之兵所當抑也。內而宿衛之士，外而邊陲之徒，試取國家之尺籍而檢之，不有所當汰乎？其曰冗食，非特闒闠僭侈不經所當禁也。由內外百司庶府之所需，以至于無名徵誅掊克之所括，有不可裁者乎？夫如是爲之，在我者旣以制節謹度，不爲耗利之端；施之在上者，又以導利于民，而不爲專利之計。是雖不足以給目前一時之急，而民富則國不至于獨貧，實所以爲萬世悠久之利也。
此在吾君吾相一心以爲天下，而不爲自便之圖。凡謀有合于遠大，勿嫌于更張；言有裨于社稷，勿遺于芻蕘。然後君子策羣力之畢集，而足國足民之道或庶幾矣。愚生狂瞽之見如此，執事其勿以爲迂焉。
第五問
戴廷禮
translation_en:
…as for these, it is not only the troops of the prefectures and principalities whose numbers should be curbed. Within the capital are the palace guards; beyond it are the men stationed on the frontiers. If we were to take up the state’s military registers and inspect them, would there not be some who ought to be discharged? When he speaks of superfluous consumption, it is not only the presumptuous, extravagant, and improper spending of the lowly [?] that should be prohibited. From the requirements of the many offices and repositories in the capital and the provinces, down to what is amassed through unauthorized levies and oppressive exactions, is there anything that cannot be reduced? If we proceed in this way, we shall, for our own part, exercise restraint and observe limits carefully, creating no occasion for the waste of resources. Those governing above will likewise direct material benefits toward the people, without devising schemes to monopolize them. Though this may not suffice to meet an immediate, temporary emergency, if the people are prosperous, the state cannot alone remain poor. This is truly the means of securing enduring benefit for ten thousand generations.
This depends upon our sovereign and our chief ministers being of one mind in working for all under Heaven, rather than devising plans for their own convenience. Whenever a proposal accords with great and far-reaching aims, let them not shrink from reform; whenever words benefit the altars of soil and grain, let them not disregard them because they come from grass-cutters and wood-gatherers. Only then may gentlemen marshal the combined efforts of all, and the way to provide adequately for both state and people may perhaps be within reach. Such are this foolish student’s rash and unenlightened views. May you, honored examiners, not deem them impractical.
Fifth Policy Question
Dai Tingli

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭謝　批〔時論邊事何多泛之無當于用凡以龍泮談兵所見也子能考古任將馭兵之術以策今備將足兵之〕
宜起弊振頹切中機要其先天下之憂者乎宜錄以式
考試官教諭張　批〔博古審今切時確見氣骨之雄偉文詞之藻贍不暇論也佳士佳士〕
考試官學正高　批〔論馭將兵之道條悉古今籌邊終始執此以往邊不足備矣列中數萬甲兵當於子亦云〕
竊聞易之蠱曰先甲三日後甲三日說者
謂前事將壞當自新以謹其後後事方始
當丁寧以監其失夫今之邊事蠱已極矣
所恃自新丁寧以爲善後之謀者必上有
安攘之誠而後法有所主下有負荷之忠
而後治有可圖蓋人情狃于故常而憚於
紛更况法立而行有未善又因以究其所
繇則利害懸焉自非上不規規于因仍下
不屑屑于利害其曷以爲振蠱之永圖哉
夫夷狄之爲中國患雖在盛世能使天地
之平成而不能亡徂征之師能致海內之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭謝　批〔時論邊事，何多泛之無當于用！凡以龍泮談兵所見也。子能考古任將馭兵之術，以策今備將足兵之〕宜，起弊振頹，切中機要，其先天下之憂者乎！宜錄以式。
考試官教諭張　批〔博古審今，切時確見。氣骨之雄偉，文詞之藻贍，不暇論也。佳士！佳士！〕
考試官學正高　批〔論馭將兵之道，條悉古今，籌邊終始。執此以往，邊不足備矣。列中數萬甲兵，當於子亦云。〕
竊聞《易》之《蠱》曰：「先甲三日，後甲三日。」說者謂：「前事將壞，當自新以謹其後；後事方始，當丁寧以監其失。」夫今之邊事，蠱已極矣。所恃自新丁寧以爲善後之謀者，必上有安攘之誠，而後法有所主；下有負荷之忠，而後治有可圖。蓋人情狃于故常，而憚於紛更，况法立而行有未善，又因以究其所繇，則利害懸焉。自非上不規規于因仍，下不屑屑于利害，其曷以爲振蠱之永圖哉！夫夷狄之爲中國患，雖在盛世，能使天地之平成，而不能亡徂征之師；能致海內之
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔Why are so many contemporary discussions of frontier affairs vague and of no practical use? This all reflects the outlook of those who discuss warfare within the schools [?]. You have examined ancient methods of appointing commanders and managing troops to propose appropriate measures for providing commanders and sufficient troops today.〕 You remedy abuses and revive what has fallen into decline, striking precisely at the crucial issues. Are you not one who worries before all others under Heaven? This deserves to be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔Widely versed in antiquity and discerning in your assessment of the present, you offer sound insights directly pertinent to the times. There is scarcely time to discuss the grandeur of your writing’s spirit and structure or the richness of its diction. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕

Comment by Examiner Gao, School Instructor: 〔In discussing how to manage commanders and troops, you systematically examine past and present and consider frontier planning from beginning to end. Proceeding on this basis, preparing the frontier’s defenses would present no difficulty. The saying about “tens of thousands of armored soldiers within the ranks [?]” should apply to you as well.〕

I have humbly heard that the Book of Changes says in the hexagram Gu, “Decay”: “Three days before the jia day; three days after the jia day.” Commentators explain: “When earlier undertakings are about to fall into ruin, one should renew oneself to take care over what follows; when subsequent undertakings are just beginning, one should exercise repeated care to watch for their failings.” Now the decay in our frontier affairs has reached its extreme. If we are to rely on renewal and repeated care to devise measures for setting matters right, those above must first sincerely seek peace within and the repulsion of external threats; only then will regulations have a guiding purpose. Those below must loyally shoulder their responsibilities; only then can good government be pursued. For human nature clings to familiar practices and fears disruptive changes. Moreover, when regulations have been established but their implementation is imperfect, and the reasons are then investigated, questions of personal advantage and harm hang in the balance. Unless those above cease narrowly adhering to precedent, and those below cease fussing over personal advantage and harm, how can there be a lasting plan to remedy this decay?

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
嚮風而不能亡蒲代之役其所賴以爲克
敵制勝之本者寧有要于兵將哉在昔文
武一而已矣無事則將歸卿列有事則卿
莅戎行故召虎以文德而平淮夷方叔以
元老而征荊蠻無專將也兵農一而已矣
居常則負耒而耕遇變則荷戈而戰故居
有積倉行有褁糧無養兵之費也厥後有
智將賢將儒將才將千萬人之將所貴乎
求之廣者世胄可使也而穰苴以典司馬
===
因勢可使也而夷吾以佐九合仇讎可使
也而雍齒封于列侯行伍可使也而李廣
起于都尉良家子可使也而奉世拜以光
祿亡命可使也而馬援授以大中俘虜可
使也而敬德納于幕下武科可使也而子
儀蒋位中令老可使也而非熊以之興周
稚可使也而甘羅以之佐秦吏可使也而
蕭何拜以相漢儒可使也而馮異封以應
國貧可使也而齊王起于淮陰賤可使也
punctuated: 嚮風而不能亡蒲代之役，其所賴以爲克敵制勝之本者，寧有要于兵將哉？在昔文武一而已矣，無事則將歸卿列，有事則卿莅戎行，故召虎以文德而平淮夷，方叔以元老而征荊蠻，無專將也。兵農一而已矣，居常則負耒而耕，遇變則荷戈而戰，故居有積倉，行有褁糧，無養兵之費也。厥後有智將、賢將、儒將、才將、千萬人之將。所貴乎求之廣者，世胄可使也，而穰苴以典司馬；因勢可使也，而夷吾以佐九合；仇讎可使也，而雍齒封于列侯；行伍可使也，而李廣起于都尉；良家子可使也，而奉世拜以光祿；亡命可使也，而馬援授以大中；俘虜可使也，而敬德納于幕下；武科可使也，而子儀蒋位中令；老可使也，而非熊以之興周；稚可使也，而甘羅以之佐秦；吏可使也，而蕭何拜以相漢；儒可使也，而馮異封以應國；貧可使也，而齊王起于淮陰；賤可使也。
translation_en: …to submit to its civilizing influence, yet could not dispense with the campaigns against Pu and Dai [?]. As for the foundation on which defeating the enemy and securing victory depend, could anything be more essential than soldiers and commanders? In antiquity, civil and military service were one. In peaceful times, commanders returned to the ranks of ministers; when trouble arose, ministers took charge of the armies. Thus Shao Hu pacified the Huaiyi through civil virtue, and Fang Shu campaigned against the Jingman as a senior minister. There were no exclusively military commanders. Soldiers and farmers likewise were one. In ordinary times they carried ploughs and cultivated the fields; when disturbances arose, they shouldered weapons and fought. Thus, at home they had grain accumulated in granaries, and on campaign they carried provisions. There was no expense for maintaining a standing army. In later times there were wise commanders, worthy commanders, scholarly commanders, talented commanders, and commanders capable of leading thousands or tens of thousands of men. What mattered was seeking them widely. Men of hereditary standing could be employed: Rangju was entrusted with the office of Marshal. Men who made use of circumstances could be employed: Yiwu assisted in the nine assemblies of the lords. Enemies could be employed: Yong Chi was enfeoffed among the ranked marquises. Men from the ranks could be employed: Li Guang rose to become a Commandant. Sons of respectable families could be employed: Feng Fengshi was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Fugitives could be employed: Ma Yuan was appointed Grand Master of the Palace [?]. Captives could be employed: Jingde was received into the commander's staff. Men recruited through the military examinations could be employed: Guo Ziyi attained the position of Director of the Secretariat [?]. The old could be employed: Feixiong helped bring Zhou to power. The young could be employed: Gan Luo assisted Qin. Clerks could be employed: Xiao He was appointed to serve as Counselor-in-Chief of Han. Scholars could be employed: Feng Yi was enfeoffed in Ying [?]. The poor could be employed: the King of Qi rose from Huaiyin. Men of lowly status could be employed…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而衛青發于人奴凡所以求之者不旣廣
乎然求之旣廣而任之不專則亞夫以抗
命疎何以平七國之反郭進以誣訟棄何
以釋北顧之憂任專矣而儲之不豫緩急
將何賴焉故霍去病之以侍中甘延壽之
以羽林郎皆其所嘗試而素識者也此古
之所以任將者則然耳而所以駕馭倡導
之術不存焉至于兵之爲制有六軍三軍
二軍一軍之分初皆自爲之食至漢之三
===
變唐之三變以及民兵募兵義勇之設而
其食皆仰給于官矣歷代所以優其養者
鹽筴可資也而管仲以富青齊轉漕可資
也而相國以給關中入粟可資也而鼂錯
以實塞下屯種可資也而充國以戍金城
委積可資也而食其以守成皐市租可資
也而魏尚以給雲中田稅可資也而寇恂
以移屬縣糴粟可資也而耿中丞以給湟
中貿易可資也而張詠以給益州充羨可
punctuated:
而衛青發于人奴。凡所以求之者，不旣廣乎？然求之旣廣，而任之不專，則亞夫以抗命疎，何以平七國之反？郭進以誣訟棄，何以釋北顧之憂？任專矣，而儲之不豫，緩急將何賴焉？故霍去病之以侍中，甘延壽之以羽林郎，皆其所嘗試而素識者也。此古之所以任將者則然耳，而所以駕馭倡導之術不存焉。
至于兵之爲制，有六軍、三軍、二軍、一軍之分，初皆自爲之食。至漢之三變、唐之三變，以及民兵、募兵、義勇之設，而其食皆仰給于官矣。歷代所以優其養者，鹽筴可資也，而管仲以富青齊；轉漕可資也，而相國以給關中；入粟可資也，而鼂錯以實塞下；屯種可資也，而充國以戍金城；委積可資也，而食其以守成皐；市租可資也，而魏尚以給雲中；田稅可資也，而寇恂以移屬縣；糴粟可資也，而耿中丞以給湟中；貿易可資也，而張詠以給益州；充羨可
translation_en:
…and Wei Qing rose from slavery. Were not the means by which such men were sought already broad indeed? Yet if the search was broad but those appointed were not given undivided authority, then, had Yafu been estranged for resisting orders, how could he have quelled the rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms? Had Guo Jin been dismissed because of false accusations, how could he have relieved anxiety over the northern frontier? Even with undivided authority entrusted to them, if men had not been prepared beforehand, upon whom could one rely in an emergency? Thus Huo Qubing, through service as Palace Attendant, and Gan Yanshou, through service as Gentleman of the Feathered Forest Guard, were both men whose abilities had been tested and long known. Such, then, were the ancient methods of appointing generals; yet the arts of controlling, encouraging, and guiding them are not contained here.
As for military organization, there were distinctions between establishments of six armies, three armies, two armies, and one army. Initially, all provided their own food. After the three changes under the Han and the three changes under the Tang, and with the establishment of militia, recruited troops, and volunteer forces, their provisions all came to depend upon official supplies. Successive dynasties provided generously for their maintenance through various means. Salt revenues could be drawn upon, and Guan Zhong used them to enrich Qing and Qi. Grain transport could be drawn upon, and the Chief Counselor used it to provision Guanzhong. Grain contributions could be drawn upon, and Chao Cuo used them to fill the frontier granaries. Military agricultural colonies could be drawn upon, and Chongguo used them to maintain the garrison at Jincheng. Accumulated stores could be drawn upon, and Shiqi [?] used them to defend Chenggao. Market levies could be drawn upon, and Wei Shang used them to provision Yunzhong. Land taxes could be drawn upon, and Kou Xun used them for transfers to subordinate counties [?]. Grain purchases could be drawn upon, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Geng used them to provision Huangzhong. Trade could be drawn upon, and Zhang Yong used it to provision Yizhou. Surplus funds could…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
資也而左藏以發餞鏈錦綺可資也而慶
曆歲出百萬珍珠可資也而寶元以市軍
儲進獻可資也而許玄豹以充邊餉中禁
可資也而內侍省以贍軍旅凡所以養之
者不既厚乎然養之既厚而擇之不精則
車下虎士何以勝合淝之役丹陽青巾何
以收陷堅之功選之精矣而練之不熟則
制將安恃焉故春蒐夏苗秋獮冬狩以
獮狩皆所以振旅而服習者也此古之馭
===
兵者則然耳而所以推赤感動之道不存
焉要之將者兵之統兵者將之衛均之所
當重也而將為要蓋天下無必勝之兵而
有不可敗之將不然李信以二十萬而不
勝王翦以六十萬而勝獨非秦士哉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝應天順人闢
乾坤于腥羶之餘而漠北一掃我
成祖文皇帝靖難定鼎揭
punctuated:
資也，而左藏以發餞鏈；錦綺可資也，而慶曆歲出百萬；珍珠可資也，而寶元以市軍儲；進獻可資也，而許玄豹以充邊餉；中禁可資也，而內侍省以贍軍旅。凡所以養之者，不既厚乎？然養之既厚，而擇之不精，則車下虎士何以勝合淝之役？丹陽青巾何以收陷堅之功？選之精矣，而練之不熟，則制將安恃焉？故春蒐、夏苗、秋獮、冬狩，以獮狩皆所以振旅而服習者也。此古之馭兵者則然耳，而所以推赤感動之道不存焉。要之，將者兵之統，兵者將之衛，均之所當重也，而將為要。蓋天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將。不然，李信以二十萬而不勝，王翦以六十萬而勝，獨非秦士哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝應天順人，闢乾坤于腥羶之餘，而漠北一掃；我成祖文皇帝靖難定鼎，揭
translation_en:
…could be drawn upon, and the Left Treasury disbursed funds [?]. Brocades and figured silks could be drawn upon, and during the Qingli reign period a million were issued annually. Pearls could be drawn upon, and during the Baoyuan reign period they were used to purchase military provisions. Offerings could be drawn upon, and Xu Xuanbao used them to replenish frontier military supplies. The inner palace’s resources could be drawn upon, and the Palace Domestic Service used them to support the troops. Were not all these means of sustaining them already generous?
Yet if their support was generous but their selection insufficiently exacting, how could the fierce warriors beneath the chariots have won the battle of Hefei? How could the blue-turbaned troops of Danyang have achieved the feat of breaking through strong defenses? If selection was exacting but training insufficiently thorough, what could commanders rely upon to exercise control [?]? Thus there were the spring sou hunts, summer miao hunts, autumn xian hunts, and winter shou hunts; these hunts [?] all served to marshal the troops and accustom them to their duties. Such were the practices of those who managed armies in antiquity, yet the means of moving men through heartfelt sincerity were absent from them. In essence, generals command the soldiers, and soldiers protect the generals. Both deserve weight, but the generals are the key. For there are no soldiers under Heaven who are certain to win, but there are generals who cannot be defeated. Otherwise, when Li Xin failed with two hundred thousand men and Wang Jian succeeded with six hundred thousand, were they not all soldiers of Qin?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao responded to Heaven and followed the people, opening up Heaven and Earth after the lingering stench of the alien rulers and sweeping clean the lands north of the desert. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen quelled the troubles and established his rule, raising …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
日月于繼明之後而虜庭三犂當時所以鼓舞
一世之豪傑綱維仁義之師旅固非特比
跡湯武而已我
列聖相承撫者定之業際亨嘉之運歸馬放牛
韜弓戢戈武備之不講久矣狂虜抵隙投
間非特肆侮寧一朝一夕之故哉頃歲東
潰薊垣西踰鴈代焚戮之慘致厪
九重西顧之憂于是
詔下廷臣上陳經略之方又
===
===
遣使行邊以求邊臣所不敢言所不能爲之
事一時條具封事凡馭將論兵之策誠有
如執事所云者及輔臣陳
大閱之典以爲積弊之餘非
聖天子躬率于其上不足以爲多方之表我
皇上欣然嘉納乃
躬御戎服
親駕六飛率勳戚大小臣工以講武事殆遠追
瞻洛之盛而陋馳射上林于不足言矣風
punctuated: 日月于繼明之後，而虜庭三犂。當時所以鼓舞一世之豪傑，綱維仁義之師旅，固非特比跡湯武而已。我列聖相承，撫者定之業，際亨嘉之運，歸馬放牛，韜弓戢戈，武備之不講久矣。狂虜抵隙投間，非特肆侮，寧一朝一夕之故哉？頃歲東潰薊垣，西踰鴈代，焚戮之慘，致厪九重西顧之憂。于是詔下廷臣，上陳經略之方，又遣使行邊，以求邊臣所不敢言、所不能爲之事。一時條具封事，凡馭將論兵之策，誠有如執事所云者。及輔臣陳大閱之典，以爲積弊之餘，非聖天子躬率于其上，不足以爲多方之表。我皇上欣然嘉納，乃躬御戎服，親駕六飛，率勳戚大小臣工以講武事，殆遠追瞻洛之盛，而陋馳射上林于不足言矣。風
translation_en: …the sun and moon after the succession to enlightened rule, and three times ploughed through the enemy’s court. The means by which he then inspired the outstanding men of his age and held together armies of benevolence and righteousness surely did more than merely equal the achievements of Tang and Wu. Our successive sage emperors inherited one another’s rule, preserving the established undertaking [?] and enjoying an age of prosperity and auspicious concord. Horses were returned to pasture and oxen set free; bows were sheathed and weapons put away. Military preparedness has long been neglected. The reckless northern enemy exploits gaps and seizes opportunities; its insolence is no isolated occurrence. Could this situation have arisen in a single day or night? In recent years, it broke through the defenses of Ji in the east and crossed Yan and Dai in the west. The horrors of burning and slaughter caused His Majesty, within the palace, anxiety as he looked westward. An edict therefore ordered the court officials to submit plans for strategic management. Envoys were also sent to inspect the frontier and seek out matters that frontier officials dared not discuss or could not undertake. At once, sealed memorials set out proposals in detail; among their plans for controlling generals and discussing military affairs, there were indeed proposals such as you, sir, have mentioned. When the grand secretaries proposed the ceremony of a grand military review, they argued that, after so many accumulated abuses, only the Sage Son of Heaven’s personal leadership from above could provide a model for all regions. Our emperor gladly approved and accepted their proposal. He personally donned military dress and rode out in his imperial carriage drawn by six swift horses, leading meritorious nobles, imperial relatives, and officials of every rank in the practice of military affairs. This almost recaptured the ancient splendor of the royal inspection at Luo, making mounted archery in Shanglin seem paltry and scarcely worth mentioning. The influence…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聲所感固宜將懷敵愾之心士增踴躍之
氣內有以銷姦宄之萌外有以落腥羶之
膽而廓清之績乃猶未見焉無亦因襲之
弊未易卒更乎夫以虜之爲患昔也止于
秋防今四時並禦矣昔間數歲一犯今歲
以爲常矣昔止于野掠未攻堡也今不特
攻堡而攻州郡矣昔所得止于芻畜布帛
今則寶玉綺繡無所不掠矣大入則大利
小入則小利未聞一遭挫焉竊恐犬羊之
===
性易逞而谿壑之欲未艾其或妄肆匪茹
則可慮孰大于是哉顧吾所以禦之者尚
復狃于故常而無肯能任其責其諸病者
日損月削坐視其困而莫一投劑焉此賈
生所謂可爲長太息者也自愚言之欲捄
弊者不可不窮其源欲證今者不可不求
諸古以言乎馭將古者推轂而寄以閫外
授劒而許以副將今之將有不行于士矣
矧偏裨乎古者將有便宜置吏收市租于
punctuated:
聲所感，固宜將懷敵愾之心，士增踴躍之氣，內有以銷姦宄之萌，外有以落腥羶之膽，而廓清之績乃猶未見焉。無亦因襲之弊未易卒更乎？夫以虜之爲患，昔也止于秋防，今四時並禦矣；昔間數歲一犯，今歲以爲常矣；昔止于野掠，未攻堡也，今不特攻堡而攻州郡矣；昔所得止于芻畜布帛，今則寶玉綺繡無所不掠矣。大入則大利，小入則小利，未聞一遭挫焉。竊恐犬羊之性易逞，而谿壑之欲未艾，其或妄肆匪茹，則可慮孰大于是哉？顧吾所以禦之者，尚復狃于故常，而無肯能任其責。其諸病者日損月削，坐視其困，而莫一投劑焉。此賈生所謂可爲長太息者也。
自愚言之，欲捄弊者，不可不窮其源；欲證今者，不可不求諸古。以言乎馭將，古者推轂而寄以閫外，授劒而許以副將；今之將有不行于士矣，矧偏裨乎？古者將有便宜置吏，收市租于
translation_en:
…the influence of this example should surely inspire commanders with hatred of the enemy and heighten the soldiers’ eagerness for action. Within, it should extinguish the beginnings of treachery and disorder; beyond the borders, it should strike terror into those reeking of flesh and mutton. Yet the achievement of clearing away the enemy remains unseen. Is this perhaps because the abuses perpetuated by established practice cannot readily be changed all at once? As for the trouble caused by the invaders, formerly defense was needed only in autumn; now we must resist them in all four seasons. Formerly they invaded once every several years; now invasion is an annual occurrence. Formerly they merely plundered the countryside and did not attack forts; now they attack not only forts but prefectures and departments as well. Formerly their booty consisted only of fodder, livestock, cloth, and silk; now they plunder everything, including precious stones, jade, figured silks, and embroidery. A great incursion brings great gains, a small incursion small gains; we have never heard of their suffering even a single reverse. I fear that their canine and ovine nature readily runs unchecked, while their appetite, as bottomless as a ravine, remains unsated. Should they recklessly unleash their implacable savagery, what greater cause for concern could there be? Yet our means of resisting them remain bound to habitual practices, and no one is willing and able to assume responsibility. It is like a sick person [?] wasting away day by day and month by month: we sit watching his distress, yet no one administers a single dose of medicine. This is what Master Jia called cause for a long, deep sigh.
In my humble view, anyone wishing to remedy abuses must trace them to their source; anyone wishing to assess the present must seek guidance in antiquity. Consider the handling of commanders. In antiquity, the ruler pushed the departing general’s chariot wheels and entrusted him with affairs beyond the capital’s gates; he bestowed a sword and granted him authority over deputy commanders [?]. Today there are commanders whose orders do not prevail even among their soldiers, much less among their subordinate commanders! In antiquity, commanders had discretionary authority to appoint officers and collect market taxes in …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
幕府不問所出矣今稽餉之使交馳于道
矣況置吏乎古有軍中不奉詔而天子按
轡者今事機在邊陲而文法由中制矣古
有日擊牛饗士而大破匈奴者今不以爲
玩愒則咎以靡費矣古者賞不踰時罪疑
惟輕本以示勸也今經歲而功罪不決可
乎古有終日鞭七人貫三人耳而知敗有
試以婦人寵臣而知成今之教習有是嚴
焉否耶古有十六年而屯青州十七年而
===
守關西今之任將有是久焉否耶今之督
撫非古卿士脩我戎乎旣命以節制一方
矣爲其可信也乃功罪不信以爲功罪必
察焉出納不信以爲出納必察焉古郡守
之不如是贅員而已矣夫以馭將之道寖
不如古而欲求功業之無前胡可得哉以
言乎馭兵古者天子之于戍士出則歌采
薇以遣之歸則歌杕杜以勞之今且不恤
于有司矣安望其上優于
punctuated:
幕府，不問所出矣。今稽餉之使交馳于道矣，況置吏乎？古有軍中不奉詔而天子按轡者，今事機在邊陲而文法由中制矣。古有日擊牛饗士而大破匈奴者，今不以爲玩愒，則咎以靡費矣。古者賞不踰時，罪疑惟輕，本以示勸也。今經歲而功罪不決，可乎？古有終日鞭七人、貫三人耳而知敗，有試以婦人、寵臣而知成。今之教習有是嚴焉否耶？古有十六年而屯青州，十七年而守關西。今之任將有是久焉否耶？今之督撫，非古卿士「脩我戎」乎？旣命以節制一方矣，爲其可信也。乃功罪不信，以爲功罪必察焉；出納不信，以爲出納必察焉。古郡守之不如，是贅員而已矣。夫以馭將之道寖不如古，而欲求功業之無前，胡可得哉？
以言乎馭兵，古者天子之于戍士，出則歌《采薇》以遣之，歸則歌《杕杜》以勞之。今且不恤于有司矣，安望其上優于
translation_en:
…at military headquarters, without inquiry into the source of the funds. Today, envoys auditing military provisions hurry back and forth along the roads; how much less could generals appoint their own officers? In antiquity, there was a commander who would not obey an imperial command within his camp, and the Son of Heaven reined in his horse. Today, critical developments occur on the frontier, yet bureaucratic rules are imposed from the center. In antiquity, there was a commander who slaughtered oxen daily to feast his soldiers and inflicted a crushing defeat on the Xiongnu. Today, such conduct would be condemned either as idle dalliance or as extravagant waste. In antiquity, rewards were not delayed, and doubtful offenses received lighter penalties: the purpose was to encourage service. Today, whole years pass without merit or guilt being settled. Can this be right? In antiquity, defeat could be foreseen when a commander spent the day whipping seven men and piercing the ears of three; success could be foreseen when military discipline was tested on women and favored ministers. Is military training today so strict? In antiquity, commanders remained stationed in Qingzhou for sixteen years and defended Guanxi for seventeen. Are generals today entrusted with commands for so long? Are today’s supreme commanders and grand coordinators not like the ministers of antiquity charged to “put our forces in order”? They have been appointed to exercise military authority over a region because they are deemed trustworthy. Yet their assessments of merit and guilt are distrusted, on the grounds that these must be investigated; their receipts and disbursements are distrusted, on the grounds that these too must be investigated. They fall short even of the commandery governors of antiquity: they are merely superfluous officials. When our methods of directing generals fall ever further below those of antiquity, how can we hope to achieve unprecedented feats?
As for directing soldiers, in antiquity the Son of Heaven sent garrison troops off with the song “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei), and welcomed them back with “The Solitary Pear Tree” (Di du) to acknowledge their toil. Today, they receive no care even from the responsible officials. How can we expect them to receive generous treatment higher up, at …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝乎古將帥之于士卒未食不先飯未臥不
先寢今視之如犬馬矣安望其共甘苦乎
古士飽馬騰而後可以利戰今一斛之粟
將不免于枵腹矣古畏我而不畏敵今紀
律亡素退則有生之望矣古者秦以銳士
强齊以技擊勝今則有不辨金鼓之節幟
文之度矣可乎古者帶甲千人則有明習
占候通曉夷情扛鼎超關健步巧詞可爲
先鋒嚮諜者今之部曲動以萬計不知備
===
此數者否耶古有養以國士則報以國士
養以衆人則報以衆人今則一切視之且
無選鋒之養矣而一旦臨敵不知有能奮
勇前驅否耶入衛之兵非延寧之勁卒乎
然千里裹甲經歲始還困敝憔悴人所共
知而徒以憚其撤兵之嫌無肯力任其責
而主之者是土苴而已矣夫以馭兵之道
寖不如古而欲求安攘之攸賴胡可得哉
此
punctuated: 朝乎？古將帥之于士卒，未食不先飯，未臥不先寢。今視之如犬馬矣，安望其共甘苦乎？古士飽馬騰而後可以利戰，今一斛之粟，將不免于枵腹矣。古畏我而不畏敵，今紀律亡素，退則有生之望矣。古者秦以銳士强，齊以技擊勝，今則有不辨金鼓之節、幟文之度矣，可乎？古者帶甲千人，則有明習占候、通曉夷情、扛鼎超關、健步巧詞，可爲先鋒嚮諜者。今之部曲動以萬計，不知備此數者否耶？古有養以國士則報以國士，養以衆人則報以衆人。今則一切視之，且無選鋒之養矣，而一旦臨敵，不知有能奮勇前驅否耶？入衛之兵，非延寧之勁卒乎？然千里裹甲，經歲始還，困敝憔悴，人所共知，而徒以憚其撤兵之嫌，無肯力任其責而主之者，是土苴而已矣。夫以馭兵之道寖不如古，而欲求安攘之攸賴，胡可得哉？此
translation_en:
…at court? In antiquity, generals would not eat before their soldiers had eaten, nor retire before their soldiers had lain down. Now they regard them as dogs and horses: how can one expect them to share their soldiers’ comforts and hardships? In antiquity, only when the soldiers were well fed and the horses spirited could they fight to advantage. Now, with one hu of grain, they will still not escape empty bellies [?]. In antiquity, soldiers feared their own commanders rather than the enemy. Now discipline has no established foundation, and retreat offers hope of survival. In antiquity, Qin grew strong through its elite soldiers, and Qi prevailed through its skilled fighters. Now there are soldiers who cannot distinguish the signals of gongs and drums or the prescribed patterns of banners. Can this be acceptable? In antiquity, among a thousand armored men there would be those well versed in divination and observing portents, thoroughly acquainted with the circumstances of the foreign peoples, strong enough to lift tripods and vault barriers, swift of foot or skillful of speech, who could serve as vanguard troops, guides, and spies. Today, military contingents routinely number in the tens of thousands; I wonder whether they possess men with all these abilities.

In antiquity, those maintained as outstanding men of the realm repaid their patrons as outstanding men; those maintained as ordinary men repaid them as ordinary men. Today, all are regarded alike, and there is not even special provision for picked vanguard troops. When they suddenly face the enemy, I wonder whether any can rouse their courage and charge ahead. Are not the troops brought in to defend the capital the stalwart soldiers of Yansui and Ningxia? Yet they travel a thousand li bearing armor and return only after a year has passed. Their exhaustion and suffering are known to everyone. Merely for fear of incurring suspicion by withdrawing troops, however, no one is willing firmly to assume responsibility and advocate their withdrawal. This is simply to treat them as worthless refuse. When the methods of commanding troops fall ever further below those of antiquity, how can one hope to find in them a reliable means of securing peace at home and repelling enemies abroad? This…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
明諭所謂邊臣不敢言不能爲之事意者其在
玆乎或曰將必試戰而後可知也其誰與
儲今內地衛士且分番以戍邊矣則中外
百夫長以上可無分番習戰于諸邊之幕
乎或曰客兵尚不足用也而撤之其誰與
防今土著之兵視客兵既不侔矣則附邊
州縣可無易而爲衛所抽之以分戍乎雖
然儲將足兵固所以爲振蠱之圖而其要
尤莫切于理財其本尤莫先于務實善乎
===
宋臣蘇轍有言曰苟無其財雖聖賢不能
自致于跬步苟有其財雖庸人可以一日
而千里方今
聖天子賢宰執蚤夜圖惟化理所以爲籌邊之
計者可謂有務實之心矣乃司事者可不
思爲體
國之忠而應之以實乎愚生密邇邊陲竊嘗
有概于中而不能以自達敢僭言之以爲
明問復
punctuated:
明諭所謂邊臣不敢言、不能爲之事，意者其在玆乎？或曰：「將必試戰而後可知也，其誰與儲？」今內地衛士且分番以戍邊矣，則中外百夫長以上，可無分番習戰于諸邊之幕乎？或曰：「客兵尚不足用也，而撤之，其誰與防？」今土著之兵視客兵既不侔矣，則附邊州縣，可無易而爲衛所，抽之以分戍乎？雖然，儲將足兵，固所以爲振蠱之圖，而其要尤莫切于理財，其本尤莫先于務實。善乎！宋臣蘇轍有言曰：「苟無其財，雖聖賢不能自致于跬步；苟有其財，雖庸人可以一日而千里。」

方今聖天子、賢宰執，蚤夜圖惟化理，所以爲籌邊之計者，可謂有務實之心矣。乃司事者，可不思爲體國之忠，而應之以實乎？愚生密邇邊陲，竊嘗有概于中，而不能以自達，敢僭言之，以爲明問復。
translation_en:
…might this be what the enlightened instruction means by matters that frontier officials dare not speak of and cannot carry out?

Some say: “A commander’s ability can be known only after he has been tested in battle. Who, then, can be held in reserve?” Even guardsmen from the interior now serve in rotations on frontier garrison duty. Should not officers commanding a hundred men and above, both within and outside the capital, likewise take turns learning warfare at the headquarters of the various frontier commands? Some say: “Even the troops brought in from elsewhere are insufficient. If they are withdrawn, who will defend the frontier?” Since locally settled troops already receive unequal treatment compared with troops brought in from elsewhere, should not the subprefectures and counties adjoining the frontier be converted into guards and battalions, with men drawn from them for assignment to garrison duty?

Nevertheless, maintaining a reserve of commanders and ensuring sufficient troops are certainly means of remedying deterioration, but nothing is more crucial to this undertaking than managing finances, and nothing takes greater precedence at its foundation than attending to practical realities. Well said were these words of Su Zhe, a minister of the Song: “Without the necessary funds, even sages and worthies cannot advance half a pace; with the necessary funds, even an ordinary man can travel a thousand li in a day.”

Now our sage Son of Heaven and worthy grand councilors deliberate morning and night on moral transformation and good government. Their plans for frontier affairs may indeed be said to show a commitment to practical realities. Should not those charged with carrying them out seek to exercise the loyalty that takes the state’s concerns to heart, and respond with concrete action? I, an unworthy student living very near the frontier, have privately long felt deeply concerned, yet have been unable to make my views known. I venture presumptuously to state them here in reply to your illuminating question.

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
隆慶四年秋八月陝西當大
比所部士維時巡按監察御
史郭〔庭梧〕祇率百司共服厥
役綜理內外纖悉周毖始七
日癸卯鎖院越甲子告竣事
凡二十有二日御史躬執局
鑰蚤夜罔或暇逸錄成將報
===
之
天府〔師載〕得有言于後用諗厥多
士曰〔師載〕不敏竊聞之虞庭
納言必試功而後庸周官言
揚必任事而後祿夫言之不
易取在盛世已然矣今〔師載〕
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

隆慶四年秋八月，陝西當大比所部士。維時巡按監察御史郭〔庭梧〕祇率百司，共服厥役，綜理內外，纖悉周毖。始七日癸卯鎖院，越甲子告竣事，凡二十有二日。御史躬執局鑰，蚤夜罔或暇逸。錄成，將報之天府，〔師載〕得有言于後，用諗厥多士曰：「〔師載〕不敏，竊聞之，虞庭納言，必試功而後庸；周官言揚，必任事而後祿。夫言之不易取，在盛世已然矣。今〔師載〕
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the fourth year of Longqing [1570], Shaanxi was due to hold the triennial examination for the scholars within its jurisdiction. At that time, Regional Inspector Guo Tingwu reverently led the officials of all offices in carrying out their duties. He supervised affairs inside and outside the examination compound, attending carefully and thoroughly to every detail. The compound was locked on the seventh day, guimao, and proceedings were declared complete on jiazi, twenty-two days in all. The censor personally held the keys to the compound, allowing himself no leisure or ease, morning or night. When the record was completed and was about to be submitted to the imperial archives, I, Shizai, was afforded the opportunity to append some words, with which to address the assembled scholars:

“I, Shizai, am untalented, but have heard that at the court of Shun, those whose words were accepted had to have their accomplishments tested before they were employed; under the Offices of Zhou, those recommended for their words had to be entrusted with duties before receiving emoluments. Even in those flourishing ages, men were not readily selected on the strength of words alone. Now I, Shizai, …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所爲試爾與爾所自爲見揚
旣感惟其言而所謂功與事
者又在爾多士他日非吾所
能與焉〔師 載〕曷言哉矧玆西
土山川炳靈古帝王所更居
賢喆挺出歷我
明二百有餘歲道化旁浹人文宣
===
朗士生其間涵育漸被策勳
茂實以淩軼前碩自制科以
還章章明備〔師 載〕又何言哉
雖然事有出于習見而可以
相證者君子恒藉以反觀焉
請以余道途所感藉以爲喻
可乎始余之發渭水也屬時
punctuated:
所爲試爾，與爾所自爲見揚，旣感惟其言，而所謂功與事者，又在爾多士他日，非吾所能與焉。〔師 載〕曷言哉？矧玆西土，山川炳靈，古帝王所更居，賢喆挺出。歷我明二百有餘歲，道化旁浹，人文宣朗。士生其間，涵育漸被，策勳茂實，以淩軼前碩，自制科以還，章章明備。〔師 載〕又何言哉？

雖然，事有出于習見而可以相證者，君子恒藉以反觀焉。請以余道途所感，藉以爲喻，可乎？始余之發渭水也，屬時
translation_en:
…my examining you, and your gaining recognition through your own efforts, have depended solely upon words [?]. Yet what are called achievements and service remain for you scholars to accomplish in days to come; they are not things in which I can participate. What can I, Shizai, say? Moreover, this western land has mountains and rivers radiant with spiritual potency. Ancient emperors and kings successively made their homes here, and worthy and wise men have risen to distinction. Throughout the more than two hundred years of our Ming dynasty, moral transformation has spread far and wide, and cultural accomplishment has shone brightly. Scholars born here, nurtured and gradually imbued with these influences, have established meritorious achievements and abundant substantive accomplishments, surpassing the eminent men of earlier times. Since the institution of the examination system, the evidence has been manifest and fully documented. What more can I, Shizai, say?

Nevertheless, among familiar sights and experiences there are things that can corroborate one another, and the gentleman regularly draws upon them for self-reflection. May I take what struck me during my journey and use it as an analogy? When I first set out from the Wei River, it was the season of…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
秋陽歊烈鬱暑蒸炎塵囂紛
沓縈紆悶爍求片雲之覆一
霑清澍不可得也迨膏車叩
關西南望見終南太白之巔
煙嵐四塞觸石蓬起竊心欣
然以爲將雨之候也少焉飄
飄掀揭而杲然日出矣詰朝
===
渡潼津跋華山之麓褰帷四
望其雲猶是也已而頹飈怒
號氷雹蕩薄脫木偃禾惟民
之災又明日巔瞻豐原雲峯
千疊氤氳彌漫余爲此懼方
將戒徒疾馳而霡霂漸零寔
稱甘霖嗟乎天下事幻化曷
punctuated: 秋陽歊烈，鬱暑蒸炎，塵囂紛沓，縈紆悶爍，求片雲之覆、一霑清澍，不可得也。迨膏車叩關，西南望見終南太白之巔，煙嵐四塞，觸石蓬起，竊心欣然，以爲將雨之候也。少焉，飄飄掀揭，而杲然日出矣。詰朝，渡潼津，跋華山之麓，褰帷四望，其雲猶是也。已而頹飈怒號，氷雹蕩薄，脫木偃禾，惟民之災。又明日，巔瞻豐原，雲峯千疊，氤氳彌漫，余爲此懼，方將戒徒疾馳，而霡霂漸零，寔稱甘霖。嗟乎！天下事幻化曷
translation_en:
…the autumn sun blazed fiercely; oppressive heat steamed and scorched. Dust and commotion crowded about me, entangling and stifling me in the heat. I sought the shelter of a single cloud, one refreshing shower to moisten me, but could find neither. When I had greased my carriage and reached the pass, I looked southwest and saw the summits of Zhongnan and Taibai. Mist and mountain vapors filled every direction, billowing up where they met the rocks. Inwardly delighted, I took this as a sign of impending rain. Before long, however, the clouds lifted and scattered, and the sun shone brightly forth.
The next morning I crossed Tong Ford and traveled along the foot of Mount Hua. Raising the carriage curtain, I looked in all directions: the clouds were just as before. Presently violent gusts roared in fury, and hail swept and battered the land, stripping trees and flattening grain—a calamity for the people. The following day, looking up toward Fengyuan [?], I saw clouds piled like peaks in a thousand layers, their vapors spreading everywhere. This frightened me. Just as I was about to order my attendants to hurry onward, a fine rain began gradually to fall: truly it deserved to be called a welcome, nourishing rain. Alas! The affairs of the world shift and transform—how …

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
常疑信士從獨雲乎哉易曰
雲從龍京房易飛候占曰西
方有大雲五色下有賢人甚
矣雲之象類吾賢也抑余又
聞終南太白盤亙西極崑崙
爾多士非鍾諸山之秀而毓
者耶始余讀子所爲文見其
===
詞鋒絢爛耀然奪目者則以
爲景雲敷華揚采郁郁紛紛
者則以爲卿雲磅礴雄渾一
瀉千里者則以爲有渰之雲
至和所發縱横昭回足以爲
文治之光者則以爲慶雲紆
徐龐雅潤澤春容者則以爲
punctuated: 常？疑信士從，獨雲乎哉？《易》曰：「雲從龍。」京房《易飛候占》曰：「西方有大雲，五色，下有賢人。」甚矣，雲之象類吾賢也！抑余又聞終南、太白盤亙西極崑崙，爾多士非鍾諸山之秀而毓者耶？始余讀子所爲文，見其詞鋒絢爛、耀然奪目者，則以爲景雲；敷華揚采、郁郁紛紛者，則以爲卿雲；磅礴雄渾、一瀉千里者，則以爲有渰之雲；至和所發、縱横昭回、足以爲文治之光者，則以爲慶雲；紆徐龐雅、潤澤春容者，則以爲
translation_en: …constant? Doubt and belief, and what scholars follow [?]—is this true only of clouds? The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon.” Jing Fang’s Prognostications of Flying Signs in the Changes (Yi feihou zhan) says: “In the west there is a great cloud of five colors; beneath it is a worthy man.” How closely the forms of clouds resemble our worthy scholars! Moreover, I have heard that Zhongnan and Taibai stretch westward as far as Kunlun. Were you many scholars not nurtured by the concentrated excellence of these mountains? When I first read your compositions, those whose verbal brilliance dazzled the eyes I regarded as radiant clouds; those unfolding their splendor and displaying their colors in rich profusion I regarded as auspicious clouds; those vast and powerful, pouring forth a thousand li in a single surge, I regarded as gathering rain clouds. Those issuing from perfect harmony, spreading their radiance in every direction, and worthy of lending luster to civil governance I regarded as clouds of good omen. Those leisurely and ample, dignified and elegant, with the moist freshness of spring, I regarded as…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不崇朝而雨是曰泰山之雲
爾多士繼自今以往將搏空
扶揺而上從六龍徧八極驅
策風雷霖雨萬方此余嚮所
謂竊心欣然以爲將雨之徵
也是惟爾多士其或覆日而
爲霿雲積陰而爲霐雲汩沒
===
芬華與時升沉廻翔滅軌而
爲浮雲又其或獵聲寡實尺
寸靡所自樹覥焉抱三有負
如吾鄉所見西郊之雲甚或
憑藉矯假鼓迅烈以自封殖
爲冰爲雹是謂暴雲茲亦惟
爾多士方今
punctuated: 不崇朝而雨，是曰泰山之雲。爾多士，繼自今以往，將搏空扶揺而上，從六龍，徧八極，驅策風雷，霖雨萬方。此余嚮所謂竊心欣然以爲將雨之徵也，是惟爾多士。其或覆日而爲霿雲，積陰而爲霐雲，汩沒芬華，與時升沉，廻翔滅軌而爲浮雲；又其或獵聲寡實，尺寸靡所自樹，覥焉抱三有負，如吾鄉所見西郊之雲；甚或憑藉矯假，鼓迅烈以自封殖，爲冰爲雹，是謂暴雲。茲亦惟爾多士。方今
translation_en:
…bringing rain before the morning is over: these are called the clouds of Mount Tai. You assembled scholars, from this time onward, will soar into the sky upon the whirlwind, follow the six dragons of the imperial chariot throughout the eight extremities, marshal wind and thunder, and bring ample rain to every region. This is what I meant earlier when I said that, rejoicing inwardly, I took these as signs of coming rain. This rests with you assembled scholars.

Some, however, may obscure the sun and become clouds of murk, or gather darkness and become clouds of gloom, submerging their fragrance and brilliance, rising and sinking with the times, wheeling about and effacing their tracks to become drifting clouds. Others may chase reputation while possessing little substance, unable to establish even the slightest achievement, shamelessly bearing three failings [?], like the clouds I have seen in the western outskirts of my home region. Still others may exploit borrowed authority and false pretensions, stirring up violent forces to enrich themselves, producing ice and hail: these are called violent clouds. This, too, rests with you assembled scholars. At present…

title: 隆慶四年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖天子寤寐求賢匪徒曰得夫才
而已蓋誠欲得夫若濟大旱
之商霖也〔師載〕以讝陋謬膺
茲典日惴惴懼不克任亦匪
徒曰得夫才而已蓋誠欲得
夫瓌瑋廊廟之器異日對
大廷聽臚傳五色横空覆蓋使
===
天下後世指其名曰此某所
舉鄉雲士也〔師載〕將有餘榮
焉不爾則將有餘咎焉夫爾
諸士平居所稱述時雨之化
受之于師而習之已者非一
日矣使一出而旋悖焉上無
以仰成
punctuated: 聖天子寤寐求賢，匪徒曰得夫才而已，蓋誠欲得夫若濟大旱之商霖也。〔師載〕以讝陋，謬膺茲典，日惴惴懼不克任，亦匪徒曰得夫才而已，蓋誠欲得夫瓌瑋廊廟之器，異日對大廷，聽臚傳，五色横空覆蓋，使天下後世指其名曰：「此某所舉鄉雲士也。」〔師載〕將有餘榮焉；不爾，則將有餘咎焉。夫爾諸士平居所稱述時雨之化，受之于師而習之已者，非一日矣。使一出而旋悖焉，上無以仰成
translation_en:
…the sagely Son of Heaven seeks worthy men both waking and sleeping. His purpose is not merely to obtain talented men: he truly wishes to obtain men like the rain that relieved a great drought under the Shang dynasty. I, 〔Shi Zai〕, despite my shallow limitations [?], have undeservedly been entrusted with this examination. Every day I tremble with fear that I cannot fulfill my charge. My purpose, too, is not merely to obtain talented men: I truly wish to find extraordinary men fit for service at court, who will one day answer before the great court and hear their names proclaimed, spreading across the sky in five-colored clouds and sheltering all beneath them. Then people throughout the world and in later generations may point to their names and say: “These are the cloud-like scholars whom so-and-so recommended from his province.” I, 〔Shi Zai〕, shall thereby enjoy lasting honor; otherwise, lasting blame will be mine.
You scholars have long spoken of the transforming influence of timely rain—the teaching you received from your teachers and practiced yourselves [?]. This has continued for more than a single day. If, as soon as you enter public service, you turn against it, the sovereign will have no means of relying upon you for accomplishment…
